# Innvil — Project Documentation

## Overview

Innvil is a **no-code white-label SMM panel builder** built with Next.js + Supabase + Vercel. Users create independent, white-label SMM panels with their own subdomain, storefront, customer dashboard, and wallet. Innvil charges a **5% commission only** on completed orders — no monthly rent, no setup fees.

---

## Tech Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|-------|------------|
| Frontend | Next.js 16.2+ (App Router, Turbopack) |
| UI Components | React 19+ with Lucide icons |
| Charts | Recharts |
| Styling | Tailwind CSS |
| Backend/Database | Supabase (PostgreSQL) |
| Auth | Supabase Auth |
| Hosting | Vercel |
| State Management | React hooks (useState/useContext) |

> Upgraded from Next.js 14 / React 18 on 2026-07-07 — Next 14.x stopped receiving
> security patches (Vercel's May 2026 advisory cluster only patches 15.5.18+/16.2.6+).
> See CLAUDE_PROGRESS.txt for the full upgrade log.

---

## Terminology

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| **Innvil** | The platform itself — the panel builder |
| **Panel** | A white-label SMM storefront created by a user |
| **Panel Owner** | A user who creates and manages a panel |
| **Customer** | End user who registers on a panel to order SMM services |
| **Provider** | The SMM API provider a panel owner connects to (bring-your-own) |
| **Floor/Price Floor** | Minimum price enforced by the provider — panel owners cannot price below it |
| **Markup** | The percentage added above the provider's floor price |
| **Live Panel** | A customer-facing panel storefront |
| **Super Admin** | Innvil platform administrator — never visible to panel owners or customers |

## Coding Standards

### Component Structure
- Use functional components with React hooks
- Keep components focused and single-purpose
- Co-locate component-specific styles when possible
- Use `.jsx` for components, `.js` for utilities and data

### Naming Conventions
- Components: PascalCase (`PanelAdmin`, `StatusBadge`)
- Functions/Variables: camelCase (`handleStatusChange`, `panelStatuses`)
- Constants: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE for configuration objects (`PANEL_STATUSES`)
- CSS classes: lowercase with hyphens (BEM-ish via Tailwind)

### Styling
- Use Tailwind CSS utility classes
- Custom styles via `GlobalStyle` component (inline `<style>` tag)
- Design tokens defined in `src/styles/globals.css`

### State Management
- Local state: `useState` for component-level state
- Cross-component state: props drilling for simple cases
- Consider Context API or Zustand for complex shared state

## Architecture

```
innvil/
├── app/                    # Next.js App Router
│   ├── page.tsx           # Root — REAL auth-driven (signed out→public/login,
│   │                      #   signed in→dashboard). Dev switcher at /?preview=1
│   ├── PreviewSwitcher.tsx# The old world-switcher harness (dev only)
│   ├── p/[subdomain]/     # REAL customer storefront (page.tsx + Storefront.tsx)
│   ├── layout.tsx         # Root layout with fonts
│   └── globals.css        # Tailwind + design tokens
├── src/
│   ├── components/        # Reusable UI components
│   │   ├── ui/            # Base components (Card, Toggle, Pill, etc.)
│   │   ├── panels/        # Innvil app, Super Admin (index.tsx)
│   │   │   └── admin/     # Panel Owner admin: PanelAdmin shell, AdminTabs, CustomerDrawer
│   │   │                  # (Categories merged into the Services "Catalog" tab)
│   │   └── customer/      # Customer-facing experience (Phase 1)
│   │       ├── index.tsx            # CustomerPanel — status-aware entry
│   │       ├── CustomerLanding.tsx  # White-label landing (auth only)
│   │       ├── CustomerDashboard.tsx# Dashboard/Orders/Wallet/Tickets/API/Profile
│   │       ├── NewOrder.tsx         # Progressive order form + smart search
│   │       └── PlatformIcons.tsx    # Monochrome brand glyphs + platform buttons
│   ├── data/              # Mock data and constants
│   ├── types/             # Shared TS interfaces (index.ts) + DB row types (db.ts)
│   ├── hooks/             # Custom React hooks
│   ├── lib/               # Utility functions
│   │   └── supabase/      # client.ts, server.ts, admin.ts, middleware.ts, constants.ts
│   │                      #   (storefront uses a separate session cookie)
│   └── styles/            # Global CSS and design tokens
├── supabase/
│   ├── migrations/        # 0001_init (schema), 0002_rls (policies),
│   │                      # 0003 (category parent_id), 0004 (services.local_id),
│   │                      # 0005 (panel_payment_gateways + gateway key RPCs)
│   └── README.md          # how to apply migrations + env
├── middleware.ts          # Supabase session refresh
├── public/                # Static assets
├── .env.local.example     # Environment variables template
├── package.json
├── tailwind.config.ts
├── next.config.js
└── CLAUDE.md
```

## Panel Statuses

| Status | Customer Can Browse | Customer Can Order | Description |
|--------|--------------------|--------------------|-------------|
| `draft` | No | No | Panel is being set up. Not visible to customers. |
| `live` | Yes | Yes | Fully operational. |
| `inactive` | Yes | No | Browsable, login, dashboard, history, wallet balance, deposits. No new orders. |
| `suspended` | No | No | Offline. Panel owner must contact Innvil support. |
| `maintenance` | No | No | Temporarily offline. Auto-returns to previous status. |

## Recent Updates

### 2026-08-27 — Fix: every page ALSO independently re-fetched what its own shell context had just fetched (v1.47.83)
- **Follow-up to v1.47.82, per a live "still has visible delays" report.** That pass eliminated the
  redundancy INSIDE `getWatchShellContext`/`getWatchAccessState` (Communities/Watchers/Capacity computed once,
  not 3-10x, within each of those two functions). What survived was a SECOND layer of the same problem: every
  individual page called `getWatchShellContext(...)` (for the sidebar) **and separately** called its own
  `listAccountCommunities`/`listAccountWatchers`/`getAccountCapacity`/`getCommunityOperationalStats`/
  `getAccountSlotBreakdown`/`getAccountActivityTrend`/`getAccountProjectDetail`/`getAccountCommunityDetail`/
  `getAccountWatcherDetail` for its own content — none of which shared data with the shell context that had
  JUST computed the exact same thing moments earlier in the same request. `/usage` was the worst single
  offender: it called `getAccountCapacity`, `countRecentModerationActions` (×2), `listAccountCommunities`,
  `listAccountWatchers`, AND `getWatchShellContext` all in one `Promise.all` — 5 independent trips through the
  same underlying data for one page load.
- **Fix**: `getWatchShellContext` now returns the `communities`/`watchers` it already computed (new
  `WatchShellContext` type, `watch-page.ts`), alongside the existing `capacity`/`attentionCount`. Every one of
  the 12 Watch pages (`/activity`, `/billing`, `/communities`, `/communities/[id]`, `/deployments`, `/plans`,
  `/projects`, `/projects/[id]`, `/settings`, `/usage`, `/watchers`, `/watchers/[id]`) was updated to read
  `shell.communities`/`shell.watchers`/`shell.capacity` directly instead of re-fetching them, and to pass
  `shell.communities` into every other function that accepts a pre-fetched-data parameter. Widened 6 more
  functions in `watch-runtime.ts` to accept one (`getAccountSlotBreakdown`, `getAccountActivityTrend`,
  `getAccountProjectDetail`, `getAccountCommunityDetail`, `getAccountWatcherDetail`) — same additive,
  backward-compatible pattern as v1.47.82 (falls back to fetching internally when omitted, so no other caller
  is affected). Kept genuinely-independent queries (payment history, trial state, gateways, credit balance,
  etc.) running in the SAME `Promise.all` as `getWatchShellContext` rather than sequencing them needlessly —
  only queries that actually depend on Communities/Watchers/Capacity were moved after the shell resolves.
- No migration (pure read-path refactor, zero behavior change — confirmed via a repo-wide grep that no page
  still calls `listAccountCommunities`/`listAccountWatchers`/`getAccountCapacity` alongside
  `getWatchShellContext` anymore). 1859 tests pass (unchanged), `tsc --noEmit` clean, production build clean
  (same 58-route output as before).
- **Deployed to Production**, verified live on `innvil.cloud`/`watch.innvil.cloud`.

### 2026-08-27 — Fix: every real Watch page redundantly re-fetched the same Communities/Watchers/Capacity data 3-10x per load (v1.47.82)
- **Live report: "the system currently feels too heavy. overview or other menus takes forever."** Traced to a
  real, quantifiable N-times-redundant-query bug in the shared read layer (`watch-runtime.ts`), not a single
  slow query or an infinite loop. `listAccountCommunities()` (a 4-SEQUENTIAL-round-trip chain: projects →
  communities → deployments → moderators) was being called independently, with no data sharing, from inside
  `listAccountWatchers`, `getAccountCapacity`, `listAccountActivity`, `countRecentModerationActions`,
  `getCommunityOperationalStats`, AND `listAccountAttentionItems` — and **`listAccountAttentionItems` also
  re-ran the ENTIRE `getAccountCapacity` computation a second time internally**, which itself re-triggered
  `listAccountCommunities`/`listAccountWatchers` yet again. Both hot-path entry points every real page goes
  through hit this: **`getWatchShellContext`** (`watch-page.ts`, called by every one of the 10+ non-Overview
  Watch routes via `requireWatchPage()`) fired the chain ~3x per page just from its own
  `Promise.all([getAccountCapacity, listAccountAttentionItems])`; **`getWatchAccessState`** (Overview's own
  data loader) fired it **8-10 times** in a single page load from its 10-item `Promise.all`. Running "in
  parallel" didn't help — all those redundant chains still compete for the same Supabase connection pool and
  multiply total DB round trips for zero additional information.
- **Fix: fetch Communities/Watchers/Capacity ONCE per request and thread them down, rather than adding any
  caching layer** (no request-scoped or cross-request cache was introduced — every value is still fetched
  fresh on every call, just without the redundant repeat trips, so there's no new staleness risk). Widened 6
  functions in `watch-runtime.ts` — `listAccountWatchers`, `getAccountCapacity`, `listAccountActivity`,
  `countRecentModerationActions`, `getCommunityOperationalStats`, `listAccountAttentionItems` — to each accept
  an **optional pre-fetched-data parameter**, falling back to their original internal fetch when omitted
  (fully backward compatible — confirmed via a full grep that every OTHER existing call site across the app,
  e.g. `/activity`, `/billing`, `/communities`, `/deployments`, `/plans`, `/projects/[id]`, `/settings`,
  `/usage`, `/watchers`, `/watchers/[id]`, never passes a 3rd/4th positional argument, so none of them are
  affected by this change at all). `getWatchShellContext` and `getWatchAccessState` were rewritten to fetch
  Communities once → Watchers (reusing Communities) → Capacity (reusing both) → everything else (reusing all
  three) — collapsing what was previously ~8-25 redundant round trips per page load down to the real minimum.
- No migration (pure read-path refactor, zero schema/behavior change — every returned value is byte-identical
  to before, only computed once instead of many times). 1859 tests pass (unchanged — no logic changed, only
  call-graph structure), `tsc --noEmit` clean, production build clean (all 60+ routes present, unchanged).
- **Deployed to Production**, alongside v1.47.79/80/81 (the Watcher Ops moderation-reporting expansion, the
  Plans & Billing docs restructure, and the 0109 migration fix) — all four verified live on `innvil.cloud`/
  `www.innvil.cloud`/`*.innvil.cloud`/`watch.innvil.cloud` via `vercel alias ls` + live host checks.
- **Not yet touched, a smaller remaining opportunity**: each individual page's OWN page-specific data function
  (e.g. `/communities`'s own `Promise.all([getCommunityOperationalStats, getAccountCapacity])`) still makes its
  own single (non-multiplied) call rather than sharing with `getWatchShellContext`'s already-fetched data from
  the same request — a real but much smaller optimization than the one fixed here, since the dominant, ~3-10x
  multiplied cost was the shared per-page guard fixed in this pass, not each page's own single extra fetch.

### 2026-08-27 — Fix: migration 0109 failed on a database where 0059 was never applied (v1.47.81)
- **Live report**: running migration `0109_watcher_ops_reports.sql` failed with `42P01: relation
  "moderator_media_dedup" does not exist`. That table is created by `0059_media_moderation.sql` (the original
  photo/video moderation feature) — its absence means that migration hasn't been applied to this database yet.
- **Impact, stated accurately (checked, not assumed)**: `loadMediaDedup`/`recordMediaDedup`
  (`community-runtime.ts`) both destructure only `{ data }` from their Supabase calls, discarding `error` — so
  a missing table degrades SOFTLY, not as a crash: media classification/enforcement (delete/warn/mute/kick/
  purge) still runs correctly end-to-end, only the cost-saving dedup CACHE silently never persists, meaning a
  duplicate file repost gets reclassified from scratch instead of reusing a cached verdict. Not a moderation-
  safety gap — a cost-efficiency one, contingent on running `0059`.
- **Fix**: `0109`'s constraint-widening step now uses `alter table if exists` (the same pattern migration
  `0070` already used for this exact table) instead of a bare `alter table` — it's a safe no-op when
  `moderator_media_dedup` doesn't exist yet, rather than a hard failure blocking the rest of the migration
  (the new `watch_moderation_reports` table, unrelated to this table, still gets created either way).
- **Action needed**: check whether `0059_media_moderation.sql` (and any other migrations before it) have
  actually been applied to this database — if not, run `0059` first to get real media-moderation dedup
  caching, then re-run `0109` (or just the now-safe constraint block) to pick up the widened `DELETE_KICK`
  check once the table exists.
- No test/code changes — pure SQL-migration fix, nothing to typecheck/test beyond the full existing suite
  (unaffected, still 1859 passing).

### 2026-08-27 — Watcher Ops: Escalation Group expanded into a real moderation operations/audit channel (v1.47.79)
- **Expands the private Escalation Group (Phase 1, v1.47.73) from a knowledge-only channel into "Watcher Ops"**
  — per explicit spec, it now also carries structured moderation reports (warnings, temporary mutes, kicks,
  message purges, scam/NSFW removals, and permission failures) alongside the existing unanswered-question
  workflow. **Zero changes to the documentation portal architecture, zero backend rewrite of unrelated Watcher
  behavior** — this is additive: new enforcement outcomes, a new reporting engine, and dashboard/docs/landing
  surfacing, all reusing existing infrastructure (the same connect flow, the same shared per-community warning
  state, the same Telegram token resolution).
- **Real enforcement-model change** (`link-moderation.ts`/`media-moderation.ts`) — supersedes the earlier warn-
  then-ban model with the spec's own graduated mute-then-kick-and-purge model, and NEVER produces a permanent
  `DELETE_BAN` from automatic enforcement anymore (the type is kept, reserved for a possible future manual
  admin action): **spam** (unsolicited promotion + an obvious flood burst, unified into one progression) —
  warning 1 mutes 10 minutes, warning 2 mutes 30 minutes, the 3rd violation kicks + purges recent messages
  (`SPAM_WARNING_LIMIT = 2`, replaces `PROMOTION_WARNING_LIMIT = 3`). **Scam/phishing** — warning 1 mutes 30
  minutes, the 2nd confirmed offense kicks + purges (no more 3rd-tier ban fallback). **Explicit content** (a
  link, or media at high confidence) — zero-tolerance, immediate kick + purge, no warning required, matching
  "no warning is required" for prohibited NSFW content exactly. Media's own borderline path (explicit-but-not-
  high-confidence, or uncertain-at-high-confidence) reuses the same `SPAM_WARNING_LIMIT`, ending in kick+purge
  instead of a ban. `ModerationEnforcement`'s `DELETE_WARN` gained an optional `muteMinutes`; `DELETE_KICK`
  gained a `purge: boolean`. Public warning text: the scam first-offense template now states the real 30-minute
  mute duration verbatim; the AI-phrased promotion-warning body gets a new DETERMINISTIC mute-duration sentence
  appended after generation (`spamWarningMuteSentence`) — the exact number is never left to the model to state.
- **Real Telegram mute execution** — `event-types.ts`'s `RESTRICT_USER` gained a `mode: "MUTE"` variant
  (`muteMinutes`); `executeAction` calls `restrictChatMember` with every `can_send_*` permission off and a real
  `until_date` computed at execution time (never decision time, avoiding clock-skew). **Real bounded message
  purge** — new `purgeUserMessages()` (`community-runtime.ts`) queries the sender's recent messages in that
  Community (bounded to 50, within the last 47 hours — safely inside Telegram's own ~48h delete window) and
  deletes each via the EXISTING `DELETE_MESSAGE` action per id, counting only real Telegram-confirmed
  successes — never claims a purge succeeded unless Telegram actually confirmed it (spec §12), matching the
  file's own established "never fabricate success" discipline.
- **New pure module `src/lib/moderator/watcher-ops-report.ts`** — deterministic, template-based report
  formatting (`formatModerationReportText`/`moderationReportHeading`), matching the spec's own heading
  vocabulary exactly ("Spam Warning" / "Repeated Spam" / "User Removed — Repeated Spam" / "Scam Link Removed" /
  "User Removed — Repeated Scam Links" / "User Removed — Prohibited NSFW Content" / "Moderation Action
  Partially Failed"). A failed primary action (mute/kick/ban) renders its OWN line as a real failure
  ("User removal failed"), per-item — never a generic "Attempted:" header papering over unchanged success
  text — while an independently-failed purge states its own honest failure reason, distinct from the primary
  action's outcome. **Zero AI/LLM import anywhere in this file** — a report built here structurally cannot
  consume AI Generation pool / BYO usage accounting, by construction, not by a special-cased exemption flag.
- **New `sendModerationReport()`** (`escalation-runtime.ts`) — reuses `resolveProjectEscalationTarget`/
  `tokenForDeployment` verbatim (never a second "which group" resolution); a project with no configured
  Escalation Group is a silent, expected no-op (the moderation action itself already happened and is never
  blocked/reversed by the absence of a reporting channel — Watcher Ops is strongly recommended, never
  required). A failed Telegram send is still persisted as real audit history (`sent: false`), never dropped.
- **New migration `0109_watcher_ops_reports.sql`** — `watch_moderation_reports` (the structured event as the
  source of truth, per spec §22 — project/community/Telegram-user/Watcher/violation-category/warning-number/
  mute-minutes/action-types/purge-result/failure-reason/previous-history/report-text/sent, service-role only
  RLS, matching every other Watch runtime table) + widens `moderator_media_dedup`'s `enforcement_kind` check
  constraint to include the new `DELETE_KICK` outcome media moderation can now produce.
- **Dashboard**: the Project detail page's "Escalations" tab is now labeled **"Watcher Ops"** and shows BOTH
  feeds in one chronologically-merged, visually-distinguished list (`ProjectEscalationsTab.tsx`) — a
  "Knowledge Escalation" heading (teal) for unanswered questions, and a "Moderation Action" (amber) / "Watcher
  Error" (red, when the Telegram action itself failed) heading for real enforcement events, each showing the
  exact deterministic report text. A new **"Watcher Ops not configured"** recommendation banner (amber) shows
  whenever the Project has no connected Escalation Group, per spec §19 — states plainly it's optional and
  never consumes a slot. New `listProjectModerationReports()` action mirrors `listProjectEscalations()` exactly
  (same ownership check, same 100-row cap, same community/Watcher name resolution).
- **Free Trial inclusion (spec §20) — already structurally true, verified rather than newly built**: neither
  `resolveProjectEscalationTarget`/`createEscalation`/`sendModerationReport` nor the link/media moderation
  functions have any tier/entitlement gate at all — Watcher Ops works identically for a trial account.
- **Slot rule (spec §21) — unchanged, re-verified**: this pass adds zero new community/deployment concepts:
  an Escalation Group still never consumes a Watcher slot or counts toward the plan's Community allowance
  (unchanged from v1.47.73's `connection_type = 'escalation_group'` filtering in `watch-runtime.ts`).
- **Docs**: extended the existing "Watcher Ops / Escalation Group" article to describe both post kinds and the
  optional-but-strongly-recommended framing; added a new "Watcher Ops Moderation Reports" article (deterministic/
  no-AI-usage, real-outcomes-only, shared-per-Community state, single-enforcer dedup, Free Trial inclusion) —
  purely additive content, zero changes to the Help Center's rendering/routing architecture.
- **Landing/footer**: the "Escalate" pillar and a new "Watcher Ops reports" feature card (Operate group) now
  state the real audit-trail capability on the main landing; `/why-watchers`' escalation card and the shared
  `WatchFooter` gained matching mentions/links — the same "surface real, already-shipped capabilities, invent

- New tests: `watcher-ops-report.test.ts` (+13, new file — every heading/template combination incl. the
  per-item failure-vs-success distinction, deterministic-repeatability, and the never-fabricate-a-purge-count

  `media-warning.test.ts`/`link-classify.test.ts` (pinned-value updates for the new mute/kick/purge model —
  every prior DELETE_BAN-producing scenario now asserts the corresponding DELETE_KICK+purge outcome), plus 2
  new content.ts tests. 1852 tests pass (up from 1828), `tsc --noEmit` clean, production build clean.
- **Not built this pass** (documented, not silently skipped): Telegram-message-editing report consolidation for
  a rapid multi-message burst (the flood-forced-kick path already collapses most bursts into one kick+purge

### 2026-08-27 — Fix: a dismissive "nothing, just checking" reply got re-greeted as if the chat were new (v1.47.78)
- **Live bug, reported with a screenshot**: after Ms VP asked "hey K! 👋 what's up?", K replied "nothing, just
  checking" (a Telegram reply to that message) and got ANOTHER fresh greeting back ("hey K! good to see you
  👋") — reading as if the conversation had never happened. Root cause: `isAcknowledgementOnly()` requires at
  least one recognized ACK_TOKENS/laugh/resolved-ack word to fire, and "nothing"/"checking" aren't in that
  vocabulary — so the message fell through every TRIVIAL check to plain `SUBSTANTIVE` → `CASUAL_CHAT`, with
  nothing telling the (cheap, DeepSeek-routed) generation that a greeting had JUST happened one turn ago.
- **New `DISMISSIVE_CLOSING_RE`** (`chatter-coordinator.ts`) — a fully anchored (`^...$`) pattern recognizing
  the specific "nothing (much)"/"not much"/"nm"/"nada", optionally followed by "just checking/looking/
  browsing/scrolling/lurking (in/around)" idiom — the classic reply shape to a rhetorical "what's up?"/"how's
  it going?". Deliberately NOT a loose bounded-length tail (which would also swallow a real complaint that
  happens to start the same way, e.g. "nothing works anymore") — the trailing continuation is enumerated
  explicitly, so anything not matching this precise shape (including "nothing works") falls through to
  ordinary `SUBSTANTIVE` unchanged. Folded into `classifyMessageKind`'s `TRIVIAL` branch alongside the existing
  `CLOSING_ACK_RE`/`isPositiveClosing`/`isAcknowledgementOnly` checks, and into the exported
  `isSimpleClosingAcknowledgement` (used by the bot-ack `COMMUNITY_HANDOFF` decision) for consistency.
- **Resolves to REACT, never `SHORT_ACK` or a fresh reply** — checked in `selectChatterAction`'s `TRIVIAL`
  branch right after the existing `POSITIVE_WORD_RE` check (before the directed/ambient split), so it applies
  whether or not the message happens to be a Telegram reply/mention: a directed dismissive reply reacts with
  👍 to whichever moderator is addressed; an ambient one reacts only if a genuinely relevant candidate exists
  (`pickRelevantReactor` — `wasLastSpeaker`/`recentlyParticipated`), and stays a real `SILENCE` when nothing is
  relevant (a contextless "nothing much" out of nowhere still doesn't force a reaction). A message ending in
  `?` is still routed to a real answer (question-detection already runs first in `classifyMessageKind`'s
  ordering) — "nothing much, what about you?" is never swallowed by this check.
- New tests (`chatter-coordinator.test.ts`, +7): the exact live-bug repro (directed → REACT 👍, reason
  `dismissive_closing_acknowledged`), bare "nothing"/"nm"/"nada" alone, the ambient-relevant-candidate and
  ambient-no-candidate cases, two false-positive guards ("nothing works anymore", a longer message merely
  starting with "nothing"), and the question-ending exception. 1835 tests pass (up from 1828), `tsc --noEmit`
  clean. No migration — pure classification-logic change, no schema/backend involved.

### 2026-08-26 — Shared Escalation Group — Phase 1 closed loop (v1.47.73)
- **New human-in-the-loop escalation system for Innvil Watch, per two verbatim user specs** ("Shared
  Escalation Group Knowledge Instructions" + "Escalation Group Slot Rule"). When a Watcher genuinely can't
  answer a question from Project Knowledge, it now forwards the question to a private, project-configured
  Telegram group instead of guessing; a real admin of that group replies; the approved answer is relayed back
  to the original community and may optionally be promoted to permanent Project Knowledge (with optional
  expiration for time-sensitive facts). **Phase 1 scope, confirmed via 3 `AskUserQuestion` clarifications**:
  the full closed loop (confidence-gated trigger, 0-slot billing, real Telegram send/reply-detection/resolve-
  back, save-as-knowledge) — explicitly deferring duplicate-question merging, topic routing, priority/urgency
  detection, the full named-role system, and the dashboard analytics/metrics page. Scoped to the direct Watch
  surface only — the legacy Panel-owner Virtual Moderator flows (`actions/moderator.ts`,
  `actions/customer-moderator.ts`) are untouched (confirmed via diff review).
- **An Escalation Group is a real `communities` row**, tagged via a new `communities.connection_type` column
  (`'community'` default | `'escalation_group'`) — reuses the EXACT SAME Telegram-membership-verified connect
  flow already built (`connectAccountCommunity`/`createAccountCommunity`), never a second/parallel connection
  path. Watchers "deploy" into it via the same `moderator_deployments` table.
- **CRITICAL BILLING RULE, enforced structurally, not just documented**: an Escalation Group never consumes a
  Watcher slot or counts toward the plan's Community allowance. `createAccountCommunity` skips its community-
  cap check ENTIRELY for `connectionType: 'escalation_group'` (never merely excluded from the count).
  `deployAccountWatcher` now ALSO skips the subscription slot-limit check entirely for an escalation-group
  target — **found and fixed a real gap in the earlier partial implementation**: excluding an already-deployed
  escalation-group Watcher from the USED count (already correct) is not sufficient on its own, since an
  account already AT its real slot cap must still be able to deploy INTO its escalation group for the first
  time. New `checkDeploymentSlotCaps` parameter `skipActiveSlotLimit` (`moderator/plan.ts`, additive, defaults
  to `false` so every existing caller is unaffected) — the independent per-community 5-deployment cap
  (`MAX_ACTIVE_DEPLOYMENTS_PER_COMMUNITY`) still applies even to an escalation-group target, per explicit
  product decision (an operational/noise safeguard unrelated to slot billing, out of this feature's scope).
  `getAccountCapacity`'s `activeDeploymentCount`/`communitiesUsed`, `getAccountSlotBreakdown`, and
  `listAccountAttentionItems`'s "no active Watcher" check all filter to `connectionType === 'community'` before
  computing — an escalation group can never trigger a false "needs attention" alert either.
- **Confidence-gated trigger, mirrors the EXISTING `INSUFFICIENT_KNOWLEDGE_SENTINEL` pattern from
  `autopost-generate.ts`**: new `ESCALATE_REQUIRED` sentinel (`chatter-generate.ts`, ANSWER only, never
  CASUAL_CHAT) — the model emits it when Project Knowledge has ZERO relevant information for a question that
  genuinely needs project-specific facts, ONLY when a real escalation group is configured for the project
  (`escalationConfigured`). An honest "not yet announced/decided" answer (real retrieved knowledge) is
  explicitly distinguished and NEVER escalates — that's a genuine answer, not a knowledge gap. Without a
  configured escalation group, behavior is byte-identical to before this feature existed.
- **New `src/lib/moderator/escalation-runtime.ts`** — `resolveProjectEscalationTarget` (resolves a project's
  connected escalation group + a deployed Watcher into it; `null` if either is missing, never a half-usable
  target), `createEscalation` (inserts the tracking row, posts the formatted escalation card via Telegram,
  returns the "forwarded to the team" text; a failed send rolls back the just-inserted row rather than leaving
  a phantom escalation), `handleEscalationGroupMessage` (branched in `handleCommunityUpdate` BEFORE sender
  classification/moderation/chatter — an escalation group is an internal ops channel, none of that is
  meaningful there). Authorization is Phase 1's real Telegram admin/creator status check — **a non-admin's
  reply is silently ignored, never resolves or publishes anything** (the spec's own hard security requirement).
  Deliberately duplicates the small token-resolution/admin-check helpers already in `community-runtime.ts`
  rather than cross-importing private functions, matching this codebase's established sibling-runtime-module
  convention (`presence-runtime.ts`/`autopost-runtime.ts` do the same).
- **Save-to-knowledge is a dashboard action, not parsed from the Telegram reply** (explicit architecture
  decision — no Telegram inline-button/callback-query handling exists anywhere in this codebase, and building
  one was judged separate, larger scope). New `src/lib/actions/watch-escalations.ts`
  (`listProjectEscalations`/`promoteEscalationToKnowledge`) — promoting an answer inserts a real PROJECT-scope
  `knowledge_sources` row (`kind: 'escalation_answer'`), flowing through the EXISTING retrieval pipeline for
  free, with an optional `expires_at` for time-sensitive facts. New `knowledge_sources.expires_at` column;
  `retrieveRelevantKnowledge` (`knowledge.ts`) now excludes an expired row exactly like an inactive one — an
  expired approved-answer is never presented as current.
- **New "Escalations" tab on the Project detail page** (`app/projects/[id]/page.tsx`,
  `ProjectEscalationsTab.tsx`) — Open/Answered list, each answered-but-not-yet-promoted escalation gets a real

  source_message_id/question_text/escalation_message_id/status/answer_text/answered_by/answered_at/

### 2026-08-26 — Telegram Leads: a directory-based lead-research tool for marketing outreach (v1.47.72)
- **Explicit scope, confirmed via AskUserQuestion before building anything**: scraping Telegram itself or
  mass-messaging communities was ruled out up front (Telegram's ToS bans unsolicited bulk messaging, real
  accounts doing it get banned fast, and API-level scraping of groups you're not in is largely blocked by
  Telegram's own privacy model — attempting it risks Innvil's own bot credentials/IP). The user picked the
  **directory-based lead list**: pull PUBLIC community listings from a site that already publishes them,
  into a structured database (name, link, member count, topic) for the team's own manual outreach. **No
  auto-messaging exists anywhere in this feature — it is lead collection only.**
- **Investigated real, fetchable sources before writing a single line of scraper code** — `tgstat.com` (403,
  bot-blocked), `combot.org/telegram/groups` (404, wrong URL shape), `telegramindex.info` (doesn't resolve).
  **`tlgrm.eu`** confirmed real and working: its category index (`/channels`) and per-category listing pages
  (`/channels/<slug>`, e.g. `/channels/crypto`) are genuinely server-rendered public HTML — fetched the actual
  raw markup via `curl` and inspected it directly (not guessed) before writing the parser. Confirmed real
  pagination (`?page=N`, with the true last-page count exposed in a `data-last-page` attribute) and confirmed
  the site marks its own paid/sponsored placements with a distinct `channel-card__promo-label` class, letting
  those be excluded from organic results.
- **New pure parser** `src/lib/marketing/telegram-directory.ts` (no I/O, directly unit-tested) —
  `parseTlgrmDirectoryHtml` (regex-based per-card extraction, the same lightweight approach already used for
  `extractSameOriginLinks` in the Project Knowledge crawler — no new DOM-parser dependency), `parseTlgrmLastPage`,
  `tlgrmCategoryUrl`, and `TLGRM_CATEGORIES`/`isKnownTlgrmCategory` — an explicit allowlist that **structurally
  excludes "adult"** (never offered as a scrape target anywhere upstream, at the type level, not just a runtime
  check — confirmed by a `tsc` error when a redundant runtime `!== "adult"` filter was left in, since the type
  guard already makes that comparison impossible). A promo/sponsored card is always skipped (not a genuine
  organic ranking, and — per the live 18+ dating-bot example found while inspecting the real page — may not
  even match the category being browsed). Entity decoding fixed mid-build after live-verifying against the
  real page: `&#039;` (zero-padded numeric apostrophe) wasn't decoded by the original `&#39;`-only rule; widened
  to a `&#0*39;` pattern and reordered so `&amp;` decodes last (avoids re-corrupting an already-decoded entity).
- **New server-only fetch orchestrator** `src/lib/marketing/telegram-directory-fetch.ts` — bounded on every
  axis so a single run can never hammer the third-party site: a 12s per-request timeout, a hard 5-page-per-
  category cap (capped again against the site's own real `data-last-page`, whichever is smaller), a 600ms
  delay between requests, and categories are always scraped in sequence, never in parallel. A failed page fetch
  stops that category's walk cleanly (never retry-loops) — whatever was already collected is still kept.
- **New migration `0107_telegram_leads.sql`** — `telegram_leads` (source/category/name/username/
  subscriber_count/description/status/notes/contacted_at, `unique(username)` since a Telegram username is
  globally unique, service-role + super-admin-only RLS, mirroring `blog_topics`' exact policy pattern). **Run
  migration `0107`.**
- **New action file `src/lib/actions/telegram-leads.ts`** — `listTelegramLeads`/`runTelegramLeadScrape`/
  `setTelegramLeadStatus`/`setTelegramLeadNotes`/`deleteTelegramLead`/`importTelegramLeadsCsv`, every export
  independently re-verifying `role === 'super_admin'` (same `requireSuperAdmin()` pattern as `blog-admin.ts`,
  not a shared helper — matches this codebase's established convention for admin-action files). A re-scrape
  **upserts by username**: updates subscriber_count/description/category/source on an already-known lead, but
  NEVER touches its `status`/`notes`/`contacted_at` — so re-running the scraper can never clobber manual
  outreach progress already recorded against a lead. `importTelegramLeadsCsv` is a manual fallback (paste
  `Name, @username, subscribers, category, description` lines) mirroring `addTopicsBulk`'s exact skip-blanks/
  skip-duplicates shape, for leads researched from elsewhere.
- **New UI** `src/components/superadmin/TelegramLeadsAdmin.tsx` — category checkboxes (adult never offered as
  an option at all) + max-pages input + "Run scrape" with a per-category result summary; a manual paste-import
  textarea; and a leads table (name/@username linking to `t.me/<username>`, subscriber count, category, a
  status dropdown + colored `Pill`, inline-editable notes, delete) with status/category/search filters and a
  client-side CSV export. Dual-mounted per this codebase's established convention: a new **"Telegram Leads"**
  tab on the `/superadmin` route, and a new **"Telegram Leads"** section in the owner-app super-admin sidebar
  (super-admin accounts only).
- New tests: `telegram-directory.test.ts` (+15, new file — promo-card exclusion, real name/username/subscriber/
  description extraction against a fixture mirroring the ACTUAL live markup, HTML-entity decoding incl. the
  live-caught `&#039;` regression, malformed/empty-HTML safety, `parseTlgrmLastPage`'s real-attribute parsing
  and its never-0/negative/non-finite guards, `tlgrmCategoryUrl`'s page-1-vs-N shape and URL-encoding, and the
  "adult" structural-exclusion guard). 1785 tests pass (up from 1770), `tsc --noEmit` clean, production build
  clean. Also manually re-verified the parser against the real, live-fetched `tlgrm.eu/channels/crypto` HTML
  (24 real organic entries extracted correctly out of 25 total cards, 1 promo correctly excluded, real last-page
  count of 2) via a throwaway script, removed after confirming correctness — not part of the permanent suite,
  since it depends on a live external page rather than a stable fixture.
- **Not deployed automatically — run migration `0107` first**, since every scrape/import write targets a table
  that doesn't exist until then.

### 2026-08-26 — New self-serve tier: BYO 20 ($199.99/mo), Platinum cut to $149.99 (v1.47.69)
- **New 5th self-serve Watch tier — "BYO 20"** — self-serve, checkout-purchasable (unlike Enterprise's
  manual/devops-only BYO tiers), $199.99/mo, always requires the customer's own AI provider credential (never
  falls back to Innvil's key), 20 Watcher slots, **10 Communities fixed with no expansion path at all** (the
  first self-serve tier structurally excluded from Community Expansion by design, not by accident), and
  **3,000 Media Moderation units bundled into the base price** — never a separate purchase, unlike every other
  tier's optional Media Moderation + add-on. Same Innvil Credit (5% monthly) / annual (10% Credit / 5% direct)
  discount treatment as Silver/Gold/Platinum. Marketed as the flagship best-value tier: a real "Best value" pill
  + teal border on its plan card, and a plain-stated "includes everything" positioning (20 slots, 10
  Communities, 3,000 Media Moderation units, all bundled) — since BYO shifts AI compute cost off Innvil's own
  books, it can bundle more included capacity for a similar-or-higher self-serve price than Managed Platinum.
- **Alongside it, Platinum drops from $199.00 to $149.99/mo** — the Gold→Platinum price jump was too large
  ($99.99 → $199.00), and the cut also makes BYO 20 read as "pay a bit more, get more, bring your own AI"
  rather than cannibalizing Platinum. Silver/Gold ($59.99/$99.99) and Bronze ($29.99) are unchanged. Since
  `moderatorEnterpriseSlotPrice()` (the Enterprise CUSTOM-quote-above-50-slots formula) derives its base
  directly from `MODERATOR_PRO_PRICE`, its own worked examples shifted too — 50 slots: $649.00 → **$599.99**;
  75 slots: $974.00 → **$924.99** (the FIXED $399/$299/$499 Managed/BYO 50/BYO Unlimited Enterprise packages
  are flat constants, never derived from this formula, and are completely unaffected).
- **Architecture decision, made explicitly rather than defaulted to**: investigated the alternative of a
  separate parallel entitlement source (mirroring how `"enterprise"`/`"trial"` sit OUTSIDE `ModeratorPlanTier`
  in `ModeratorEntitlementSource`) before choosing to make `byo20` a genuine **5th literal value of
  `ModeratorPlanTier`** instead (`"basic" | "standard" | "premium" | "pro" | "byo20"`). Enterprise/Trial are
  separate specifically because neither has a self-serve checkout and neither flows through
  `watchPlanOptions()`/`createDirectWatchCheckout`/`purchaseWatchWithCredit`/`BillingPlanPicker.tsx` — BYO 20 is
  the opposite, it genuinely IS a self-serve checkout tier, just with different downstream characteristics once
  active. Making it a 5th tier literal means it reuses ALL existing self-serve machinery (checkout, renewal,
  plan-switch, billing period, capacity display) for free, and TypeScript's own exhaustiveness checking on
  every `Record<ModeratorPlanTier, X>` map in `money.ts` forced an explicit, compile-time-verified decision for
  byo20 at every single one of those maps — caught several real spots this way, including
  `AiModeratorSurface.tsx`'s legacy Panel-reseller tier-label map (added a type-completeness entry there,
  confirmed the separate render array structurally never actually offers it through that legacy channel).
- **Pricing/capacity foundation (`money.ts`)**: `MODERATOR_PRO_PRICE = 149.99` (was `199.0`); new
  `MODERATOR_BYO20_PRICE = 199.99` wired into `moderatorPlanPrice()`;
  `MODERATOR_COMMUNITY_CAPACITY.byo20 = { included: 10, maxWithAddons: 10 }` (hard-capped, `included ===
  maxWithAddons` — the same existing convention Bronze/Silver already use for "no expansion possible");
  `COMMUNITY_EXPANSION_ELIGIBLE_TIERS` deliberately left `["premium", "pro"]` unchanged — NOT adding byo20 is
  exactly what excludes it from Community Expansion both in the UI (`isCommunityExpansionEligibleTier`) and at
  compile time; `MODERATOR_AI_GENERATION_POOL.byo20 = 0` (N/A by design — byo20 always routes through the
  customer's own credential, so `paidTier` is forced to `null` for it the same way it already is for
  Enterprise, and this value is a required-by-the-type placeholder, never actually read);
  `MODERATOR_MEDIA_ADDON.byo20 = { price: 0, units: 3000 }` (`price: 0` documents "already bundled, never
  separately charged"). `src/lib/moderator/plan.ts`: `CAPACITY.byo20 = { maxCommunities: 10, maxActiveSlots:
  20 }`. `watch-plans.ts`: `presenceSchedulingEligible`/`autoPostingEligible` both gained `tier === "byo20"` —
  a flagship tier gets every self-serve capability Platinum gets.
- **Entitlement parsing** (`watch-runtime.ts`): `parseEntitlementTier()` gained the `"byo20"` literal check, so
  `resolveAccountWatchTier`/`getAccountPaidPlan` recognize it from `subscription_ref` the same way every other
  self-serve tier already does.
- **Checkout/billing** (`watch-plans.ts`, `innvil-credit-pricing.ts`): `WatchPlanDisplayName` gained `"BYO 20"`;
  `TIER_TO_DISPLAY.byo20 = "BYO 20"`; `DISPLAY_TO_TIER["BYO 20"] = "byo20"`; `watchPlanOptions()`'s `tiers` array
  gained `"byo20"` at the end, so it renders as a genuine 5th card via the SAME existing `.map()` loop in
  `BillingPlanPicker.tsx` — no new render path. `createDirectWatchCheckout`/`purchaseWatchWithCredit` needed
  ZERO code changes — both already resolve price via `watchPlanOptions().find(...)`/`moderatorPlanPrice(tier)`,
  and the existing tier-change guard (blocks a plan switch when current Community count exceeds the new tier's
  `CAPACITY[tier].maxCommunities`) already works correctly for byo20's fixed 10-Community cap for free.
  `INNVIL_CREDIT_DISCOUNT.byo20 = 0.05` (same 5% as Silver/Gold/Platinum); `ANNUAL_ELIGIBLE_TIERS` gained
  `"byo20"`.
- **AI routing invariant** (`resolveAccountAiRouting`, `watch-runtime.ts`) — widened additively with a new
  optional 7th parameter, `isByo20 = false` (every existing call site/test unaffected by the default). Inside:
  when `isByo20` is true, the function skips the Enterprise-entitlement-table lookup entirely (byo20 is BYO by
  TIER DEFINITION, never by a checked `apiSourceMode` column on an Enterprise-shaped row) and goes straight to
  credential resolution via `getAccountByoCredential`/`checkByoUsageAllowed` — reusing the SAME
  `watch_byo_provider_credentials` table (already `account_id`-primary-keyed, one credential per account, zero
  schema change needed). Both real call sites (`community-runtime.ts`, `presence-runtime.ts`) updated to pass
  `entitlementSource === "byo20"` as the new argument. The `paidTier` derivation right above the
  `community-runtime.ts` call site (which already excludes `"trial"`/`"enterprise"` from the self-serve
  AI-Generations-pool gate) now also excludes `"byo20"` — mirroring the exact same "this tier has its own
  separate/no pool, gating it here would incorrectly cap it against a pool it never consumes" reasoning already
  documented for Enterprise.
- **Media Moderation bundling** (`community-runtime.ts`) — rather than adding a third branch to
  `runMediaModeration`'s existing two-branch gate (Enterprise-media-addon / self-serve-purchased-addon), the
  FIRST branch's resolved input (`bundledMediaAddon`, renamed from the Enterprise-only `enterpriseMediaAddon`
  for clarity since it's no longer Enterprise-exclusive) was extended at the `handleCommunityUpdate` call site
  to also cover byo20's always-active, always-3,000-unit allowance:
  `enterpriseEntitlement ? {...} : entitlementSource === "byo20" && accountId ? { active: true, units:
  MODERATOR_MEDIA_ADDON.byo20.units } : null`. The gating block's existing logic (checks `.active`, tracks usage

### 2026-08-25 — Real bounded multi-page crawl + fixed a live fabrication bug (v1.47.65)
- **Two real problems from the same live test.** A Watcher asked a question with no matching Project Knowledge
  fabricated a confident, plausible-sounding answer instead of admitting it didn't know. Separately, ingestion
  only ever fetched the ONE submitted URL — a homepage link never told the Watcher anything about the rest of
  the site (features, docs, pricing pages), which the user correctly flagged as insufficient for real projects
  that expect the bot to "dig deep," including linked whitepapers/roadmaps for crypto projects.
- **(1) Fabrication fix, confirmed via direct retrieval trace, not guessed.** Ran the actual retrieval scorer
  against the exact live question ("monitoring hub of what?") — it returned ZERO matches. `projectKnowledge
  ContextLines()` correctly returns `null` when nothing is retrieved, but the caller then just OMITTED the
  knowledge block from the prompt entirely — nothing told the model it currently had no project-specific facts,
  so it fell back to inventing a plausible one. New `NO_PROJECT_KNOWLEDGE_LINE` (`chatter-generate.ts`) fills
  that gap for ANSWER specifically (never CASUAL_CHAT, which never used knowledge to begin with): "you currently
  have ZERO project-specific facts... do not invent, guess, or improvise... say so honestly instead."
- **(2) Real bounded multi-page crawl, not just a single fetch.** New `crawlAndIngestSite()`
  (`knowledge-fetch.ts`) — starting from a submitted root URL, discovers and follows SAME-ORIGIN links up to
  **8 pages, 2 link-hops, 30s total wall-clock** (whichever limit hits first), reusing the EXACT SAME per-page
  SSRF/content-type/size guards as a single-URL ingestion for every discovered page — crawling only decides
  which same-origin URLs to fetch next, it never weakens any existing guard. New pure
  `extractSameOriginLinks()` (`knowledge-ingestion.ts`, regex-based, no DOM parser needed) resolves/filters/
  dedupes hrefs from raw HTML (cross-origin, fragment-only, mailto:/tel:/javascript: links all excluded).
  `ingestUrlIntoProject`/`refreshAccountProjectKnowledgeSource` (`watch-project-knowledge.ts`) both now chunk
  EACH crawled page independently (a chunk never spans two pages) and flatten into one ingestion, prefixing
  each chunk with its real source page once more than one page was crawled.
- **Verified live against the real test project**: force-recrawled `innvil.cloud` — went from 10 chunks off one
  page to **44 chunks across 8 real distinct pages** (homepage, design-shop, blog, login, signup, terms,
  privacy), confirmed via direct query of the stored `[Source page: ...]` markers.
- **Honest scope limits, not silently deferred**: same-origin only (a linked third-party doc/whitepaper site
  isn't followed); a linked PDF discovered mid-crawl is skipped, not fetched (submitting it directly as its own
  "Add URL"/Website source still works — `source_type: 'pdf'` already exists in the schema from migration 0106,
  but PDF extraction itself is still not built, unchanged from that migration's own documented deferral). Real
  PDF/whitepaper ingestion (via direct submission, not crawl-discovery) is the natural next step if needed.
- New tests: `knowledge-ingestion.test.ts` (+7 — `extractSameOriginLinks`' same-origin resolution, cross-origin
  exclusion, fragment/mailto/tel/javascript exclusion, dedup, the maxLinks cap, malformed-input safety, no-links
  case), `chatter-generate.test.ts` (+4 — the exact live fabrication bug as a regression test, the empty-array
  case, the fallback being replaced not duplicated once real knowledge exists, CASUAL_CHAT exemption). No
  dedicated test for `crawlAndIngestSite` itself (real network/DNS I/O — consistent with this codebase's
  established convention for `knowledge-fetch.ts`, which has never had a dedicated test file; verified instead
  via the live production trace above). 1749 tests pass (up from 1738), `tsc --noEmit` clean, production build
  clean.

### 2026-08-25 — Real Project Knowledge URL ingestion + Project-centric Community/Watcher deployment (v1.47.61)
- **Two related product corrections, per an explicit engineering brief.** (A) Project Knowledge URLs were
  previously stored as bare text — the Watcher knew a URL existed but never read what was on the page. (B) A
  Community/Watcher deployment initiated from `/watchers` silently defaulted to `projects[0]` (first-created
  Project) whenever the account had more than one Project, with the selector HIDDEN entirely when there was
  exactly one — a real, live ambiguity risk once an account holds multiple Projects. Investigated the actual
  schema/actions/runtime/UI before touching anything (per the brief's own explicit process).
- **PART A — real ingestion, not a bigger text box.** New migration `0106_knowledge_ingestion.sql`:
  `knowledge_sources.panel_id` made nullable (the SAME zero-Panel fix already applied to every other Watch
  table in migration 0069 — this table was simply never revisited); a new `'document'` kind; and real
  ingestion-state columns (`source_type`, `source_url`, `storage_path`, `status`, `error`, `content_hash`,
  `fetched_at`, `ingestion_id`, `chunk_index`). A long URL source becomes **N chunk rows sharing one
  `ingestion_id`** — the EXISTING per-row relevance scorer (`retrieveRelevantKnowledge`, `knowledge.ts`,
  completely unmodified) already ranks/retrieves individual rows, so chunking needed zero retrieval-layer
  changes; a chunk is indistinguishable from an ordinary Fact/Link row at retrieval time.
- **New `src/lib/moderator/knowledge-ingestion.ts`** (pure, no I/O — fully unit-tested): `validateIngestUrl`
  (http/https only, rejects embedded credentials), `isPrivateOrReservedIpv4`/`Ipv6` (real SSRF blocklist —
  RFC1918, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, multicast/reserved, IPv4-mapped IPv6, malformed input fails CLOSED),
  `extractReadableText` (via `sanitize-html`'s `nonTextTags` — script/style/nav/header/footer content is
  dropped entirely, not just unwrapped), `chunkText` (paragraph-aware, sentence-boundary fallback, bounded
  chunk count — never splits mid-word, never endlessly chunks a huge document).
- **New `src/lib/moderator/knowledge-fetch.ts`** (server-only, the actual network I/O): `fetchAndExtractUrl` —
  DNS-resolves and rejects private/reserved targets BEFORE connecting, a bounded manual redirect loop
  (`redirect:"manual"`, max 3 hops, **re-validates every hop** rather than trusting fetch's own automatic
  redirect-following), a response read bounded by a running byte counter (never trusts `Content-Length` alone),
  a content-type allowlist (web pages only), and a 12s timeout. Honestly documented residual limitation: this
  doesn't fully close a DNS-rebinding race between the check and the connect — a reasonable, disclosed v1
  mitigation, not a claim of complete protection.
- **New `src/lib/actions/watch-project-knowledge.ts`** (account-scoped, mirrors `watch-project-profile.ts`'s
  exact `projects.account_id === user.id` ownership check, never Panel-scoped): `listAccountProjectKnowledgeSources`
  (groups chunk rows back into one summary card per logical source), `addAccountProjectTextKnowledge` (unchanged
  plain-text path), `addAccountProjectUrlKnowledge` (the real ingestion — a failed fetch persists a real `status:
  'failed'` + short error message, never fabricated content), `refreshAccountProjectKnowledgeSource` (re-fetches;
  a content-hash match is a no-op that only bumps `fetched_at`, never duplicating chunk rows for an unchanged
  source; a real change atomically replaces every old chunk under the same `ingestion_id`),
  `deleteAccountProjectKnowledgeSource` (deletes every chunk sharing the source's key, always project-scoped).
- **Trust boundary preserved, explicitly verified via `git diff`/grep**: `link-moderation.ts`/`link-classify.ts`
  (Telegram chat-link moderation) have zero `fetch()` calls and zero import of either new ingestion module — a
  link posted in chat is still judged from message text/context alone, completely unrelated to this feature.
- **UI**: `ProjectKnowledgeTab.tsx` gained a real "Knowledge sources" card — add a plain-text entry or a
  website/docs URL, real per-source status (Ready/Processing/Failed) with a visible short error on failure,
  chunk count, Refresh (URL sources only) and Remove — never a raw internal storage key rendered anywhere.
- **PART B — Project-centric deployment, no silent Project guessing.** `WatcherConnectModal.tsx`'s Project
  selector is now ALWAYS shown (was hidden whenever the account had exactly one Project, silently defaulting to

### 2026-08-25 — Fix: the devops Enterprise grant tool showed Managed's Community-capacity numbers for
  every mode, and validated BYO capacities against Managed's own package matrix (v1.47.58)
- **Live bug report, correctly flagged as a real regression against the explicit product table**: "from managed
  to byo unli — all are 8 communities included, all re the same price for expansion." Investigated before
  touching anything — the CANONICAL pricing module (`watch-enterprise-community.ts`, shipped 2026-08-22 as
  v1.47.34) was confirmed byte-for-byte correct against the exact table given (Managed base 8 → 10/$9.99,
  15/$14.99, 25/$24.99; BYO 50 and BYO Unlimited both base 10 → 15/$12.99, 25/$19.99, BYO Unlimited continuing
  uncapped at +$4.90/mo per +10 block beyond 25) — and the real, customer-facing `/plans` selector
  (`EnterpriseModeCards.tsx`) already reads it correctly per mode. The actual bug was isolated to the **devops
  Enterprise-grant tool** (`WatchDevOpsAdmin.tsx` + `setAccountDevOpsEnterprise`, the ONLY live path to grant a
  real Enterprise entitlement today, since there's still no self-serve Enterprise checkout).
- **Root cause, UI half**: `WatchDevOpsAdmin.tsx` had a single MODULE-LEVEL constant,
  `const ENTERPRISE_COMMUNITY_BASE = getEnterpriseIncludedCommunities("managed")` (= 8), used as the Community-
  capacity select's base option AND its fallback whenever a stored value was null — for every mode, regardless
  of whether the admin had actually selected Managed, BYO 50, or BYO Unlimited. The select's own expansion
  options were likewise hardcoded to `getEnterpriseCommunityExpansionOptions("managed")` unconditionally, so
  switching to BYO never changed what the dropdown actually offered — explaining exactly what was reported.
- **Root cause, server half — a real safety gap, not just display**: `setAccountDevOpsEnterprise`
  (`superadmin-watch-devops.ts`) validated every submitted `communityCapacity` against
  `validateEnterpriseCommunityCapacity("managed", communityCapacity)` unconditionally too — meaning any real BYO
  Unlimited capacity beyond 25 (a valid, uncapped block continuation for that mode) would have been REJECTED
  outright (Managed has a hard max of 25), and a capacity that merely happened to coincide with a Managed
  package number (e.g. 10) would pass for the wrong reason rather than being validated against BYO's own table.
- **Fix**: new `communityModeFor(apiSourceMode, slots)` — the SAME `(apiSourceMode, slots) → mode` mapping
  `resolveEnterpriseMediaAddonKey` (`watch-enterprise.ts`) already uses for the Media Moderation + add-on, so the
  two can never disagree about which mode an account is actually being granted. Added independently to both the
  UI (`WatchDevOpsAdmin.tsx`) and the action (`superadmin-watch-devops.ts`) — the UI now derives the select's
  base/options from the CURRENTLY-selected mode (`apiSourceMode` + the chosen BYO tier's `maxSlots`), resets the
  capacity field to the new mode's real base whenever the mode/tier radio or dropdown changes (so a stale value
  from the previous mode's table can never linger unnoticed), correctly derives the current-entitlement display's
  fallback from the ACCOUNT's own real stored `apiSourceMode`/`enterpriseSlots` (not the form's in-progress
  selection), and gained a real "+ Add 10 Communities" step button (mirroring `EnterpriseModeCards.tsx`'s own
  customer-facing affordance) plus a synthetic current-value option so a BYO Unlimited capacity beyond 25
  displays/matches correctly instead of silently showing blank. The server action now validates against the
  real derived mode, with an error message naming the correct package family.
- **No migration, no dedicated test file** — consistent with this exact file's own long-established, already-
  documented convention (every other function in `superadmin-watch-devops.ts` has zero dedicated tests, since
  `requireSuperAdmin()` depends on real session-cookie resolution this codebase doesn't mock for server actions);
  verified instead via `tsc --noEmit` + the full 1701-test suite (unaffected, since the canonical
  `watch-enterprise-community.ts` module itself was never wrong) + production build + direct code review of the
  derivation logic against `resolveEnterpriseMediaAddonKey`'s already-tested equivalent mapping.
- **Not deployed automatically, per standing instruction.**

### 2026-08-25 — BYO Enterprise: real token counts for the AI client + token-based usage ceilings — closes the
  last two blocked items off Phase 4.V.1's honest deferred list (v1.47.56)
- **Explicit instruction: "implement full specs for Watch first before we go live."** The two remaining items
  from Phase 4.V.1 (token-based ceilings, call-latency telemetry) were previously reported as genuinely blocked
  on `aiComplete()`'s return shape not exposing real usage — this pass removes that blocker and builds on top of
  it, closing both, plus the deliberately-deferred "commercial-vs-BYO limit UX copy pass."
- **`src/lib/ai/client.ts`: new `aiCompleteWithMeta()`**, additive — every existing caller of `aiComplete()`
  (~40 across the codebase: moderation, blog, media warnings, link classification, bot manager, etc.) is
  **completely unaffected**, confirmed by `tsc --noEmit` + the full test suite passing unchanged and a
  dedicated new test proving `aiComplete()`'s own return value is byte-identical to before this refactor.
  Internally, `anthropicComplete`/`openaiComplete` now return `{text, inputTokens, outputTokens}` instead of a
  bare string (Anthropic's real `usage.input_tokens`/`usage.output_tokens`, OpenAI-compatible's real
  `usage.prompt_tokens`/`usage.completion_tokens` — DeepSeek's endpoint is OpenAI-compatible, so this covers it
  too); a new shared `aiCompleteFull()` holds the exact same primary/fallback/`providerOverride` resolution
  logic as before (copied once, not duplicated), and both `aiComplete()` (unwraps to a bare string, unchanged
  signature) and the new `aiCompleteWithMeta()` (returns `{text, inputTokens, outputTokens, durationMs}` — real
  wall-clock duration measured around the call) delegate to it. Never estimates a token count from visible text
  — a provider response with no `usage` field reports `null`, never a fabricated 0.
- **Wired into the two real generation call sites that produce BYO telemetry** — `chatter-generate.ts`'s
  `generateChatterReply` (reactive, chatter ANSWER/CASUAL_CHAT) and `presence-generate.ts`'s
  `generatePresenceMessage` (proactive, Watcher Presence Scheduling transitions) both switched from
  `aiComplete` to `aiCompleteWithMeta`, threading real `{inputTokens, outputTokens, durationMs}` onto their
  result types (`ChatterGenerationResult`/`PresenceMessageResult`, both gained a `usage`/`usage?` field) —
  present on every real AI call outcome (including a model's own decline — real spend happened even without a
  visible reply), absent when generation fell through to a deterministic fallback (chatter's own error path;
  presence's template pool) since no real call happened there to report usage for.
- **`community-runtime.ts`'s `recordByoCall`** and **`presence-runtime.ts`'s `recordByoPresenceCall`** both
  gained a `usage` parameter, now recorded on BOTH the telemetry event (real `inputTokens`/`outputTokens`/
  `durationMs` columns, migration `0104`, additive/nullable on `watch_byo_ai_usage_events`) AND fed as a real
  `tokens` count into `recordByoPolicyUsage` (input+output combined — the real total spend driver) for the
  NEW token-ceiling enforcement below.
- **Token-based usage ceilings (migration `0103`)** — `watch_byo_usage_policies` gained an optional
  `token_limit` column (independent of the always-required `request_limit` — a policy can set either, both, or
  neither); `watch_byo_usage_counters` gained `used_tokens`; `increment_watch_byo_usage`'s RPC widened to a
  6-arg overload (`p_tokens default 0`, old 5-arg overload dropped) incrementing both counters atomically in
  one upsert. `checkByoUsageAllowed`/`recordByoPolicyUsage`/`setByoUsagePolicy`/`getByoUsageStatus`
  (`watch-byo-usage-policy.ts`) all extended: the gate blocks if EITHER a configured request OR token ceiling
  is exhausted (`ByoUsageGateResult` gained `blockedBy: "requests" | "tokens" | null` for diagnostics);
  `setByoUsagePolicy`'s `tokenLimit` param follows the established omit/null/number three-state idiom (omitted
  = leave an existing token limit untouched on update; explicit `null` = clear it; a positive number = set
  it) — the same "omit to preserve" pattern already used for `activateWatchEntitlement`'s `enterpriseSlots`.
  Tokens accrue on a scope's counter even when that scope has no token ceiling CONFIGURED yet, so a limit added
  mid-period reflects real already-accrued usage rather than starting from an artificial zero.
- **UI**: `ByoUsagePolicyCard.tsx` gained a "Token limit (optional)" input alongside the existing request-limit
  field, and each configured-policy row now shows real `usedTokens / tokenLimit` alongside the existing request
  count when a token ceiling is set. The Usage page's "BYO calls" card gained a real token/duration summary
  block (total input tokens, total output tokens, average call duration) — omitted entirely (never a fabricated
  0) when nothing in the window reported usage, e.g. every recorded event predates migration `0104`.
- **Commercial-vs-BYO limit UX copy pass** (the last remaining Phase 4.V.1 item, previously assessed as "largely
  moot in practice since Enterprise doesn't consume the self-serve AI Generation pool at all" — confirmed again
  this pass: `isEnterprise` explicitly excludes `apiSourceMode === "byo"`, so the AI Generations pool card
  structurally never renders alongside the BYO usage controls card for the same account) — `ByoUsagePolicyCard`'s
  own description now explicitly states these are limits the CUSTOMER configures on their OWN provider spend, a
  genuinely different concept from the Innvil BYO Enterprise plan itself (which has no separate usage quota to
  hit), rather than the previous vaguer "Innvil's plan/pricing is unaffected either way" phrasing.
- New tests: `client.test.ts` (+4 — real Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible usage-field parsing, null-not-fabricated
  when a response has no usage field, `aiComplete()`'s own behavior unaffected), `watch-byo-usage-policy.test.ts`
  (+13 — the full token-limit CRUD three-state semantics, token-exhaustion blocking with real request headroom,
  `blockedBy` for both dimensions, a policy with no token limit never blocked by token usage no matter how high,
  tokens accruing even without a configured ceiling, `getByoUsageStatus` reporting `usedTokens`),
  `watch-byo-usage.test.ts` (+4 — real token/duration recording on insert, null-when-omitted, sum/average
  aggregation in `getByoUsageSummary`, an event with no usage skipped from totals rather than treated as 0, and
  totals reporting `null` not `0` when nothing in the window reported usage — corrected 2 pre-existing
  empty-summary assertions for the widened shape), `presence-generate.test.ts` (+2, plus every existing test
  updated for the new `{text, usage?}` return shape — real usage present on a successful call, absent on every
  fallback path). 1685 tests pass (up from 1662), `tsc --noEmit` clean, production build clean.
- **Not deployed automatically, per standing instruction.**
- **Run migrations `0103` and `0104`** before this governs anything live — until then, token-limit policies
  can't be saved and telemetry has no columns to record real usage into.
- **This closes Phase 4.V.1's full itemized deferred list except**: multi-credential provider/model scoped
  ASSIGNMENT (still deliberately deferred — a genuinely larger, security-sensitive encrypted-credential-storage
  rearchitecture for a feature with zero live BYO customers today, unaffected by this pass) and the spec's own
  structured test/report checklist as a discrete deliverable (documentation/QA exercise, not a code gap).
