### 2026-08-25 — `innvil_bot_manager` proactive marketing campaigns — the deliberately-deferred Phase 4.Q half now
  ships (v1.47.54)
- **Closes the last item explicitly deferred at v1.20.0** ("only the reactive-support half is built this pass...
  the proactive marketing-campaign SEND path is scaffolded at the DB layer only"). `innvil_bot_manager`'s
  `bot_manager_campaigns`/`bot_manager_campaign_sends`/`bot_manager_chats` schema (migration `0064`) has existed
  since that pass with real approval-gated rows and a `recordKnownChat()` that already upserts every inbound
  chat into `bot_manager_chats` on every message — this pass finally reads it and actually sends.
- **New `src/lib/moderator/bot-manager-campaign-runtime.ts`** — `sweepBotManagerCampaigns(admin, now)`, mirroring
  the exact idempotent-cron-sweep shape already established by Auto-Posting/Presence Scheduling this session:
  (1) `claimDueCampaigns` moves every `approved=true, status='scheduled'` campaign whose `scheduled_at` has
  passed (or is `null`, meaning "send as soon as approved") into `sending`, via a conditional
  `UPDATE ... WHERE status='scheduled'` — two concurrent sweep ticks can't both claim the same campaign;
  (2) `sendDueBatch` sends a **bounded batch** (`MAX_SENDS_PER_SWEEP = 25`, shared globally across every
  concurrently-`sending` campaign, so one large campaign can never starve another's progress within a tick) of
  not-yet-sent, currently-known, `marketing_enabled=true` target chats matching the campaign's audience — a large
  campaign spreads across several 5-minute ticks rather than risking a function timeout, never a single
  unbounded blast. Every real send (success OR failure) is recorded into `bot_manager_campaign_sends`
  (`unique(campaign_id, chat_id)` — the real duplicate-send guard; a `23505` unique-violation on a retried/
  overlapping sweep is a harmless race loss, never treated as an error) — a campaign only moves to `sent` once
  every currently-eligible chat has a real send record for it, including the honest zero-eligible-chats case
  (marked `sent` immediately rather than stuck forever with nothing to send to).
- **Hard approval gate preserved, per the spec's own "9. Campaign controls, not unrestricted auto-posting"** —
  nothing ever sends without `approved=true` AND `status='scheduled'` both being true; editing/creating/
  scheduling a campaign only ever writes STATE, never itself sends — only the cron sweep, on its own next tick,
  actually calls Telegram, mirroring the "editing config never itself triggers an announcement" discipline
  already established for Presence Scheduling's owner-facing actions.
- **Uses `innvil_bot_manager`'s own credential (`INNVIL_OFFICIAL_BOT_TOKEN`) — never `TELEGRAM_MANAGER_BOT_TOKEN`**
  (the control-plane-only Manager Bot, which must never post customer/community-facing content, per every prior
  pass that's touched it) — read the same way `bot-manager-runtime.ts`'s existing `botManagerToken()` already
  does, no new credential-storage mechanism.
- **Real, not-a-guess audience targeting** — new `src/lib/moderator/bot-manager-campaign-audience.ts` (a
  deliberately separate, pure, client-safe module — see the server/client boundary fix below) maps
  `target_audience` (`all|private_users|groups|channels`) onto Telegram's own real `chat_type` values
  (`private|group|supergroup|channel`, `groups` covering both `group` and `supergroup` — the same distinction
  Telegram itself draws, irrelevant to a marketing audience) — every send target is a real, already-known chat
  from `bot_manager_chats`, never an invented/guessed id.
- **New cron route `app/api/cron/bot-manager-campaigns`** + **migration `0101_supabase_bot_manager_campaigns_cron.sql`**
  (schedules `innvil-bot-manager-campaigns-every-5-min`, byte-for-byte mirroring migration `0095`'s established
  vault-secret/`net.http_get` pattern). **Run migration `0101`** (+ schedule/verify the pg_cron job) before this
  does anything live.
- **New superadmin CRUD `src/lib/actions/bot-manager-campaigns.ts`** (`requireSuperAdmin()`-gated, same role-check
  pattern as every other superadmin action file) — `listCampaigns` (with real per-campaign send/error counts),
  `createCampaign`, `updateCampaignMessage` (blocked once real sends exist for a campaign — editing copy after
  delivery has already begun would make already-sent copies disagree with a fresh send), `approveCampaign`,
  `scheduleCampaign`, `cancelCampaign` (blocked once `sent`), and `getKnownChatsSummary` (real
  marketing-opted-in chat counts by type, so a superadmin can see "0 eligible chats" before approving a campaign
  that would otherwise silently complete with zero real sends).
- **New superadmin UI `src/components/superadmin/BotManagerCampaignsAdmin.tsx`** — create/edit/approve/schedule/
  cancel, a live known-chats summary strip, a real eligible-chat-count preview per audience selection (computed
  via the SAME `chatTypesForAudience` mapping the sweep itself uses, never a duplicated category list), and a
  per-campaign send/failure count. **Dual-mounted** in both surfaces per this codebase's established convention
  — the `/superadmin` route (new "Bot manager campaigns" tab) and the owner-app super-admin sidebar (new
  "Bot manager campaigns" section, `isSuper`-gated).
- **Real server/client boundary bug caught and fixed before shipping** (the exact class already documented in
  this codebase's history, e.g. `watch-status.ts`'s own extraction): the audience-mapping function was
  initially defined inline inside the `server-only` runtime file and re-exported for the UI to use for its
  eligible-count preview — this pulled the WHOLE server-only module graph (`createAdminClient`/
  `telegramApiCall`) into the client bundle, breaking the production build (`'server-only' cannot be imported
  from a Client Component module`). Fixed by extracting `chatTypesForAudience` into its own tiny pure module
  with zero server/admin imports (`bot-manager-campaign-audience.ts`) that both the server-only runtime file and
  the client UI component import independently — caught by `npm run build`, not shipped.
- **Also caught before shipping**: the new action file initially re-exported the (synchronous, non-async)
  `chatTypesForAudience` function for the UI's convenience — a `"use server"` file may only export async
  functions (Next's own Server Actions rule, not caught by `tsc`); doing so would have silently broken the
  entire actions bundle at module-evaluation time, the exact incident already documented in this codebase's
  history (v1.23.4, the `/api/v2` "Invalid API key" root cause). Removed before it ever reached a build; the UI
  imports `chatTypesForAudience` directly from the pure module instead.
- New test: `bot-manager-campaign-audience.test.ts` (+5 — every audience→chat_type mapping incl. the `null`
  "no filter" case for `all`, and a guard that every non-`all` mapping only ever contains Telegram's own real
  chat_type vocabulary). **`sweepBotManagerCampaigns` itself has no full DB/Telegram-mocked orchestrator test**
  — consistent with this codebase's own established convention for comparably complex orchestrators
  (`sweepPresenceSchedules`/`runAutoPostSweep`/`handleCommunityUpdate`, none of which has one either) — verified
  via typecheck + build + code review instead. 1658 tests pass, `tsc --noEmit` clean, production build clean
  (confirmed `/api/cron/bot-manager-campaigns` in the build output).
- **Not deployed automatically, per standing instruction.**
- **Deliberately not built this pass** (documented, not silently skipped): AI-assisted campaign copywriting (the
  spec allows AI to help write copy elsewhere, but this pass is the send-mechanics half only — copy is
  superadmin-authored, plain text); priority-over-customer-moderators in a shared group for marketing content
  specifically (the existing reactive-support priority behavior from v1.20.0 is unrelated and unaffected); a
  campaign-performance/delivery-rate dashard beyond the simple send/failure counts already shown; recurring/
  repeating campaigns (a campaign is a one-shot send-until-exhausted, matching the schema's own `status`
  lifecycle, which has no repeat/recurrence concept).

### 2026-08-25 — AI Telegram Auto-Posting now works for standalone (Panel-less) Watch accounts (Phase 4.N.1) (v1.47.53)
- **Closes a real, previously-documented product gap, per direct instruction to finish the remaining Watch
  specs before going live.** The Watch landing page itself advertises Auto-Posting ("Schedule per-Watcher
  posting windows so your community stays active") as a real capability — but until this pass, Auto-Posting was
  entirely Panel-distributed-only (`auto_post_windows.panel_id NOT NULL` since migration 0055,
  `actions/autopost.ts` hard `panels.owner_id`-scoped throughout). A direct/standalone Watch account — this
  product's actual primary customer — could never use a feature its own landing page advertised. Flagged as a
  "structurally Panel-only" limitation in several earlier passes (BYO Phase 2, v1.47.43; Presence Scheduling,
  v1.47.44) without being fixed until now.
- **Migration `0100_watch_autopost_standalone.sql`** — `alter table auto_post_windows alter column panel_id
  drop not null`, mirroring the exact same nullable-ownership pattern already established for
  `moderator_deployments`/`communities`/`telegram_bot_integrations` (migration 0069). No other schema change —
  `community_id`/`moderator_deployment_id` are already the real ownership anchors for a standalone window.
- **`autopost-runtime.ts` (the cron sweep) now resolves entitlement via TWO branches**, both reachable from the
  same `enabled=true` window scan: a Panel-distributed window (`panel_id` set) resolves via the existing
  `panels.settings` map, byte-identical to before this pass; a standalone window (`panel_id` null) resolves via
  the SAME `resolveStandaloneModeratorSettings()` the live Telegram Q&A/moderation runtime already uses
  (`community-runtime.ts`) — reused verbatim, never a second/duplicated entitlement model — keyed by the
  window's assigned deployment's own moderator id. `virtualModContentGeneration()` itself is completely
  unchanged either way, so the real "trial excluded, any paid tier or Enterprise included" rule (spec §26)
  applies identically regardless of which ownership shape a window has. `loadKnowledgeForWindow`'s
  ORGANIZATION-scope query is now skipped entirely for a standalone window (`panelId: null`), mirroring the
  exact fix already made for the live Q&A retrieval path — a standalone window was never able to have
  panel-wide knowledge to begin with, so this is a correctness fix, not a new restriction.
- **New `src/lib/actions/watch-autopost.ts`** — a genuinely separate account-scoped action file (never widened
  in place on the legacy `actions/autopost.ts`, matching this codebase's established one-file-per-ownership-
  model convention — `watch-moderator.ts` vs `actions/moderator.ts`, `watch-presence.ts`, etc.). Ownership
  resolved via `listAccountCommunities` (the same canonical, cross-account-isolated Community list every other
  Watch action reuses); entitlement via a new `autoPostingEligible(tier)` pure helper (`watch-plans.ts`,
  mirrors `presenceSchedulingEligible`'s exact shape — any paid tier including Bronze, or Enterprise; trial
  excluded). Every window is inserted with `panel_id: null`. Deployment options and moderator-name lookups are
  read straight from the already-resolved community summary — no second query needed, unlike the legacy
  version's `virtual_moderators` embed workaround.
- **New "Auto-Posting" tab on the Community detail page** (`app/communities/[id]/page.tsx`, alongside the
  existing Presence tab — same conditional-tab pattern, gated on the `AUTO_POSTING_ENABLED` master switch),
  `AutoPostScheduleCard.tsx` (timezone setting, window creation, window list with enable/disable/delete, a
  compact recent-posts status list) — mirrors the legacy owner-facing `AutoPostingCard` in `AdminTabs.tsx`
  closely (same UX shape, Watch-styled), scoped to the single Community the tab lives on (no community
  selector needed, unlike the legacy multi-community owner surface). Shows a real "not on your current plan"
  upsell instead of a broken control when the account's tier isn't eligible — never a dead/silently-failing
  form.
- **`WatchShell.tsx`'s stale doc comments corrected** — Auto-Posting is no longer described as having "no
  account-scoped backend," now correctly documented as Community-scoped (a tab, like Presence), which is why
  it still has no global sidebar item.
- New tests: `autopost-runtime.test.ts` (+3 — a standalone window's ORGANIZATION-scope query is proven never
  queried/never surfaced, the Panel-set branch proven to delegate verbatim to `virtualModContentGeneration`
  rather than a second decision, a standalone window whose deployment resolves to no known moderator fails
  safe with provably ZERO DB calls), `watch-plans.test.ts` (+1 — `autoPostingEligible`'s full tier matrix incl.
  Bronze-is-eligible, unlike Presence Scheduling which starts at Silver). 1653 tests pass (up from 1649), `tsc
  --noEmit` clean, production build clean. Verified live via the dev server that an unauthenticated request to
  a Community detail route redirects cleanly (no crash); the new tab itself requires an authenticated session
  with a real entitlement to click-test, consistent with this session's established limitation for
  comparably complex Watch dashboard pages.
- **Master switch still OFF in production** (`AUTO_POSTING_ENABLED`/`NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTO_POSTING_ENABLED`) —
  unchanged by this pass; flipping it on is a separate, explicit decision once the whole pipeline (Panel AND
  standalone) is live-verified. **Run migration `0100`** before this governs anything live. **Not deployed
  automatically, per standing instruction.**

### 2026-08-25 — BYO usage policy: real per-Watcher-deployment scope (Phase 4.V.1, item 2) (v1.47.51)
- **Closes item 2 off the Phase 4.V.1 deferred list, per direct instruction to finish the remaining Watch
  specs before going live.** Extends yesterday's account+Community usage-policy hierarchy (v1.47.50) into the
  real 3-level model the spec asked for: account → Community → Watcher deployment, tightest ceiling wins. A
  customer can now cap one specific Watcher's own BYO spend independently of its Community or the whole account.
- **`watch-byo-usage-policy.ts` rewritten around a discriminated `UsagePolicyScope`** (`{type:"account"}` /
  `{type:"community",communityId}` / `{type:"deployment",deploymentId}`) instead of a bare nullable
  `communityId` — self-documenting and structurally impossible to set two scopes on one row at once (the DB
  also enforces this via a `check (community_id is null or deployment_id is null)` constraint). Every export
  (`setByoUsagePolicy`/`clearByoUsagePolicy`/`checkByoUsageAllowed`/`recordByoPolicyUsage`/`getByoUsageStatus`)
  now takes/returns the real scope shape; `checkByoUsageAllowed` evaluates all three applicable scopes
  (account, this Community if given, this deployment if given) and blocks on whichever is tightest and
  exhausted, exactly mirroring the existing account/Community precedent.
- **Migration `0099_watch_byo_usage_policy_deployment_scope.sql`** — additive `deployment_id` on both
  `watch_byo_usage_policies` and `watch_byo_usage_counters`, a new partial unique index
  `(account_id, deployment_id, kind) where deployment_id is not null`, `increment_watch_byo_usage` gained a
  `p_deployment_id default null` parameter (old 4-arg overload dropped). **Scope-key format also corrected**:
  counters now key by an explicit `account:__`/`community:<id>`/`deployment:<id>` prefix instead of a bare id,
  so a Community UUID and a deployment UUID can never collide in the shared `scope_key` column even in
  principle — safe to change since this table has no real production usage yet (confirmed against the live
  Supabase project before writing the migration).
- **`resolveAccountAiRouting()` (`watch-runtime.ts`)** gained an optional `deploymentId` parameter (inserted
  before `kind`, default `null`) threaded to `checkByoUsageAllowed`. `presence-runtime.ts`'s sweep — already
  iterating per-deployment — passes the real `row.deployment_id` directly, resolving all three scopes in one
  call. New exported `applyDeploymentUsagePolicy(admin, routing, accountId, communityId, deploymentId, kind)`
  is the counterpart for `community-runtime.ts`'s once-per-message resolution, which happens BEFORE a
  responder is chosen and so can't know the deployment id yet — `respondAsDeployment` calls it once the
  responding Watcher is known, narrowing (never widening) an already-usable routing to unusable if that
  Watcher's own ceiling is exhausted. Correctly scoped to the CASUAL_CHAT/ANSWER branch only (never SHORT_ACK,
  which makes zero AI calls and consumes zero BYO spend) and gated on the credential ALREADY being usable
  before the deployment check runs — an already-unusable credential (missing/unconfigured) still falls through
  to the pre-existing `GENERATION_STARTED`→`GENERATION_FAILED` path unchanged, never intercepted as a new
  SILENCE (a real regression caught and fixed by the test suite before this shipped, not after).
- **`recordByoCall`/`recordByoPresenceCall`** both gained the deployment id, so a per-Watcher ceiling only
  ever increments from a genuinely successful call by THAT Watcher — reactive from
  `community-runtime.ts`'s chatter path, proactive from `presence-runtime.ts`'s presence sends.
- **Deliberately NOT extended to link/media moderation's warning-text generation** — `runLinkModeration`/
  `runMediaModeration` use a single arbitrary "enforcer" deployment (`deployments[0]`), not a per-responder
  concept the way chatter/presence are; threading deployment-level gating through their signatures would be a
  bigger, lower-value surface change for a secondary (warning-text-only) AI usage that already degrades
  gracefully on any failure. Documented as a deliberate scope-down, not silently skipped.
- **UI**: `ByoUsagePolicyCard.tsx`'s Scope dropdown now lists Whole account / every Community / every Watcher
  deployment (grouped `<optgroup>`s), reusing the same per-Community `watchers` data the new Deployments page
  reads — no new query. `watch-byo-usage-settings.ts`'s actions take the real `UsagePolicyScope` type directly.
- New tests: `watch-byo-usage-policy.test.ts` rewritten end-to-end for the 3-scope model (+11 net — all three
  scopes coexisting independently, the tightest-of-three-wins case, deployment-vs-different-deployment
  isolation, deployment-vs-Community-of-that-deployment independence), `watch-runtime.test.ts` (+4 —
  deployment-scoped `resolveAccountAiRouting`, cross-deployment isolation, `applyDeploymentUsagePolicy`'s
  narrowing behavior and its Managed-account no-op), `community-runtime.test.ts` (+2 — a real end-to-end
  exhausted-deployment-policy SILENCE before any model/RPC call, and a headroom case correctly NOT blocking).
  1644 tests pass (up from 1636), `tsc --noEmit` clean, production build clean.
- **Run migration `0099`** before this governs anything live. **Not deployed automatically, per standing
  instruction.**

### 2026-08-25 — Real Operations → Deployments page (a genuine CRM record surface) + BYO reactive/proactive usage-ceiling split (v1.47.50)
- **Two pieces this pass, per direct product direction.**
- **(1) Operations → Deployments — the FIRST item off Phase 4.V.1's honest deferred list, unlocked by
  v1.47.44's Watcher Presence Scheduling shipping a real proactive (unprompted, scheduler-driven) BYO call
  site.** Until now `resolveAccountAiRouting()`'s usage-policy check (Phase 4.V, v1.47.45) had exactly ONE
  ceiling — "requests per period" — shared between reactive chatter replies (community-runtime.ts) and, once
  Presence Scheduling landed, proactive transition messages (presence-runtime.ts). This was a real asymmetry,
  not just an unfinished feature: a proactive send could be BLOCKED by an exhausted reactive counter, but
  presence-runtime.ts never RECORDED anything against it, so in practice proactive calls got a silent free
  ride relative to whatever reactive traffic had already consumed.
  - **Migration `0098_watch_byo_usage_policy_kind.sql`** — additive `kind text not null default 'reactive'
    check (kind in ('reactive','proactive'))` on both `watch_byo_usage_policies` and `watch_byo_usage_counters`
    (0096); re-scoped the two partial unique indexes to `(account_id, kind)` / `(account_id, community_id,
    kind)` so a reactive AND a proactive policy can now coexist at the same scope; widened
    `watch_byo_usage_counters`' primary key to `(account_id, scope_key, kind, period_key)`; `increment_watch_byo_usage`
    gained a `p_kind default 'reactive'` parameter (the old 3-arg overload explicitly dropped, not left
    stale). Backward-compatible by construction — every pre-existing row/counter defaults to `'reactive'`,
    the exact semantic every one of them already represented (the only kind of BYO call that existed before
    Presence Scheduling shipped).
  - `watch-byo-usage-policy.ts`: every export (`setByoUsagePolicy`/`clearByoUsagePolicy`/`checkByoUsageAllowed`/
    `recordByoPolicyUsage`) now takes a `kind: "reactive" | "proactive"` parameter (defaults to `"reactive"`
    where a default makes sense, so no pre-existing caller broke). The two kinds are FULLY independent gates —
    an exhausted reactive policy never blocks a proactive call at the same scope, and vice versa (a real,
    directly tested requirement, not just documented).
  - `resolveAccountAiRouting()` (`watch-runtime.ts`) gained a `kind` parameter (default `"reactive"`), threaded
    to `checkByoUsageAllowed`. `community-runtime.ts`'s one call site now passes `"reactive"` explicitly (it
    only ever runs off a real inbound Telegram message); `presence-runtime.ts`'s sweep now passes `"proactive"`
    explicitly AND — a real gap closed, not just labeled — now actually RECORDS both telemetry
    (`recordByoUsageEvent`, automation `WATCHER_PRESENCE`/`WATCHER_PRESENCE_BYO`) and policy usage
    (`recordByoPolicyUsage(..., "proactive")`) after every successful BYO-routed send, via a new
    `recordByoPresenceCall()` helper mirroring `community-runtime.ts`'s existing `recordByoCall` shape.
  - `ByoUsagePolicyCard.tsx` (Usage page) gained a "Kind" selector (Reactive replies / Proactive scheduled) —
    an account can now configure genuinely separate ceilings, e.g. cap unattended scheduled presence chatter
    tighter than real conversational replies.
  - New tests: `watch-byo-usage-policy.test.ts` rewritten with `kind` threaded through every fixture (+8 net
    new — reactive/proactive coexistence at the same scope, an exhausted one never blocking the other,
    per-kind `getByoUsageStatus` reporting, cross-kind clear isolation), `watch-runtime.test.ts` (+2 — the
    default-to-reactive proof and the explicit-proactive-gate proof). 1636 tests pass (up from 1634), `tsc
    --noEmit` clean, production build clean.
  - **Run migration `0098`** before this splits anything live — until then every BYO call (reactive or
    proactive) continues sharing the single pre-existing counter, exactly as before this pass.
  - **Deliberately not built this pass** (the rest of Phase 4.V.1's honest list, unchanged): per-Watcher/
    deployment-level policy granularity (still account+Community only), token-based ceilings, provider/model
    POLICY beyond the single stored credential, provider health/observability, richer telemetry dimensions,
    the full landing-page primary-offer treatment.
- **(2) Real Operations → Deployments page — closes a genuine CRM gap the user flagged directly, twice
  (per-Watcher/per-Community slot-consumption data existed but was "cramped" inside the Usage page instead of
  living on its own Operations surface, as previously requested).** A Deployment (Watcher↔Community
  relationship) is a real record, not merely a Usage/Billing side-effect — it now gets its own operational
  page, matching the explicit product rule: **Billing = entitlement/purchasing. Usage = consumption/limits.
  Operations → Deployments = what is deployed, where, and why it's consuming slots.**
  - New **`app/deployments/page.tsx`** — built entirely from data that already existed
    (`listAccountCommunities`'s per-Community `watchers` array already carries every deployment, enabled or
    paused; `getAccountSlotBreakdown` groups the SAME data by Watcher/Community) — no new query shape, no
    fabricated numbers. A compact capacity summary strip ("N/Total Watcher slots used", "N Watcher profiles",
    "N active deployments", "N Communities"); a prominent, always-visible three-concept glossary (Watcher
    Profile = reusable identity/persona / Active Deployment = a Watcher assigned+enabled in one Community /
    Watcher Slot = the capacity one active deployment consumes); a collapsible "How slots work, using your own
    deployments" panel that renders the REAL relationship (e.g. "Aegis → Community A = 1 slot", "Aegis →
    Community B = 1 additional slot", "= 2 Watcher slots") from the account's own `getAccountSlotBreakdown`
    data — never a hardcoded example — linking out to the existing Help Center article
    (`/support/watchers/watcher-profiles-deployments-slots`, reusing `SlotInfoPopover`'s established target,
    not a new one); and the real flat operational truth table (Watcher | Community | Status | Slot usage) —
    one row per (Watcher, Community) pairing, including PAUSED deployments (shown with "—" slot usage, never
    "1 slot", matching the backend's own enforcement that a paused deployment consumes zero slots), each
    Watcher/Community name linking to its own detail page.
  - New **"Deployments"** item in the `WatchShell` sidebar's **Operations** group (alongside Activity) —
    `/deployments`, using a `Network` icon.
  - **Usage page decluttered, not duplicated**: the "Slots by Watcher" / "Slots by Community" tables (and the
    `getAccountSlotBreakdown` call/`breakdown` variable that powered them) were REMOVED from `app/usage/page.tsx`
    entirely, replaced with a single compact pointer card ("See what's actually consuming your Watcher slots →
    Open Deployments"). Usage now stays scoped to consumption/limits only, per the stated rule — the
    operational relationship data lives in exactly one place.
  - No migration (pure UI/read-composition, reusing existing exported functions). `tsc --noEmit` clean, full
    test suite unaffected (1636 pass — no new pure logic was introduced, this is page composition over
    already-tested data functions, consistent with this codebase's established convention for comparable Watch
    UI pages), production build clean (`/deployments` confirmed in the build output).
- **Not deployed automatically, per standing instruction.**

### 2026-08-25 — Enterprise Media Moderation + gets real per-request consumption metering + Usage-page visibility (v1.47.48)
- **Follow-up to v1.47.47's grant/gate-only pass** — that pass made Media Moderation + a real superadmin-
  grantable boolean but explicitly deferred per-unit consumption metering, and had no Usage-page visibility at
  all for Enterprise. Both closed this pass, per direct request: "media moderation... should be in the usage
  too... if not added, will only show 'not added'... if added, X/total".
- **New canonical resolver** `resolveEnterpriseMediaAddonKey(apiSourceMode, slots)` (`watch-enterprise.ts`) —
  maps a LIVE account's real provisioned `{apiSourceMode, slots}` to its actual `ENTERPRISE_MEDIA_ADDON` package
  key (`managed50`/`byo50`/`byoUnlimited`) — Managed always resolves to `managed50` regardless of custom slot
  count (no per-slot Managed media-addon variant exists); BYO Unlimited (`slots: null`) resolves to
  `byoUnlimited`; an off-menu BYO slot count (shouldn't occur now that grants are tier-picker-only, per
  v1.47.47) defensively falls back to the SMALLER `byo50` allowance rather than assuming the larger one. The

### 2026-08-25 — Security fix: removed the superadmin's ability to enter a customer's BYO API key (v1.47.46)
- **Live report from the user, correctly flagged as a real security problem**: the Watch devops tool
  (`/superadmin` → Watch devops, and the owner-app sidebar mirror) had a form letting a superadmin TYPE a
  customer's BYO AI-provider API key directly and store it on their behalf. That's wrong — a customer's API
  key is their own sensitive credential; Innvil operations staff should never see, type, receive, or otherwise
  come into possession of it, regardless of how convenient it is for provisioning.
- **`setAccountDevOpsByoCredential` removed outright** from `src/lib/actions/superadmin-watch-devops.ts` — not
  hidden, not gated further, deleted. There is now no code path anywhere in this codebase through which an
  admin can submit a customer's raw API key. **`clearAccountDevOpsByoCredential` (revoke) is kept** — clearing
  a credential requires possessing nothing secret (it's a delete, not a set), so it stays available for
  legitimate incident response (e.g. the customer reports their key compromised and asks it be revoked
  immediately). Also kept: flipping `apiSourceMode` to `"byo"` (pure metadata, no credential involved).
- **The correct path was already built and unaffected**: `watch-byo-settings.ts` / the account's own "AI
  Provider" Settings tab (Phase 2, v1.47.43) is the ONLY place a BYO credential is ever stored — the customer
  enters their own key themselves, authenticated as themselves, never relayed through support or devops. This
  fix removes a redundant, insecure duplicate path; it does not add anything new.
- **UI** (`WatchDevOpsAdmin.tsx`): the "BYO provider credential" section is now status-only — shows whether a
  credential is currently stored, with a single "Revoke credential" action. The API key / base URL / model
  input fields and "Save credential" button are gone entirely. Copy explicitly tells the admin the customer
  provisions their own key from their own Settings page.
- **Doc comments corrected** in `superadmin-watch-devops.ts` — the file's own top comment and the
  `setAccountDevOpsEnterprise` doc comment both used to reference the now-deleted action; both rewritten to
  state the boundary explicitly (an admin can flag BYO and revoke, never set) and explain why.
- No migration (no schema change — this only removes an application-layer code path and a UI form). 1603 tests
  pass (unchanged — no dedicated test file existed for this action file, consistent with its established
  convention), `tsc --noEmit` clean, production build clean.
- **Not deployed automatically, per standing instruction** — this session had already deployed to Preview
  right before this fix; redeploy when ready to pick it up there.

### 2026-08-25 — BYO Enterprise usage POLICY — customer-configurable spend ceilings (Phase 4.V, v1.47.45)
- **Finishes the last real, unbuilt piece of Phase 4.V** — BYO credential storage, live runtime wiring, usage
  telemetry, self-serve credential UI, and landing positioning all already shipped (Phase 1/2, v1.47.42/43).
  The one thing genuinely missing was the customer-owned USAGE POLICY layer — configurable ceilings the
  customer sets on their OWN BYO provider spend, distinct from telemetry (which only OBSERVES calls, never
  blocks them).
- **Hierarchy scoped to account + Community only, explicitly documented, not silently narrowed.** The full
  Phase 4.V spec described account→Community→Watcher/deployment; this pass implements account-wide + per-
  Community (the two most commonly wanted ceilings — an overall spend cap plus per-Community caps for a
  multi-Community Enterprise account). Deployment/Watcher-level granularity is a reasonable future refinement,
  not built this pass — mirrors the same kind of scope-down already made and documented for BYO telemetry.
- **Unit counted: requests per period, never tokens** — `aiComplete()`'s return shape still doesn't expose a
  real token count to every caller (same honest limitation already documented for `watch_byo_ai_usage_events`);
  fabricating one would be dishonest. Period is a plain UTC calendar day/month boundary (`periodKey()`), the
  same established pattern already used for the Free Trial's reactive quota.
- **New migration `0096_watch_byo_usage_policy.sql`** — `watch_byo_usage_policies` (account-wide row has
  `community_id: null`; partial unique indexes enforce at most one policy per scope) + `watch_byo_usage_counters`
  (keyed by `(account_id, scope_key, period_key)`, `scope_key = '__account__'` for the account-wide row since
  Postgres PK columns can't be nullable) + atomic `increment_watch_byo_usage` RPC (upsert-on-conflict-increment,
  mirrors `increment_watch_ai_response_usage`'s exact single-statement pattern). RLS on, no policies
  (service-role only). **Run migration `0096`.**
- **New `src/lib/products/watch-byo-usage-policy.ts`** — `checkByoUsageAllowed()` evaluates EVERY policy
  configured for an account (account-wide + the specific Community, when given) and blocks if EITHER is
  exhausted for its own current period — the tightest configured ceiling always wins, regardless of which
  scope it's set at. `recordByoPolicyUsage()` re-resolves which scopes have a configured policy AT INCREMENT
  TIME (never assumed from the earlier gate check) — a policy added mid-period starts its counter fresh from
  0, never inheriting usage that accrued before the limit existed. An account/Community with no configured
  policy at all is never written to. Fire-and-forget, never throws (same "a usage write must never break
  generation" discipline as `recordByoUsageEvent`).
- **Wired at the single canonical routing resolver, not duplicated per call site.** `resolveAccountAiRouting()`
  (`watch-runtime.ts`) gained an optional `communityId` parameter (both real call sites —
  `community-runtime.ts`'s `handleCommunityUpdate`, `presence-runtime.ts`'s sweep — already had a `communityId`
  in scope, so this was a one-line addition at each). A policy-exhausted account resolves to the EXACT SAME
  `{required:true, credential:null}` "unusable" shape a missing/misconfigured credential already produces —
  every downstream generation call site (chatter reply, link classify/warning, media warning, presence
  messages) needed ZERO changes, since they already treat `credential:null` as "fail explicitly / fall back to
  the safe deterministic pool," never a signal to use Innvil's own key.
- **Counting scope, same documented judgment call as BYO telemetry.** `recordByoCall()`
  (`community-runtime.ts`, previously telemetry-only) now also calls `recordByoPolicyUsage()` on a SUCCESSFUL
  chatter-reply generation — the one BYO call site with a genuine, unambiguous success signal. Link-
  classification and media-moderation-warning BYO calls are NOT individually counted against the policy (they
  degrade silently by design, no real ok/error signal to key off) — but they're still BLOCKED once a
  configured limit is reached, since the gate governs the shared BYO credential itself at the routing level,
  not one specific call site.
- **New self-serve UI**: `ByoUsagePolicyCard.tsx` on the Usage page, directly below the existing "BYO calls"
  telemetry card — shown only for a BYO-flagged account (`capacity.apiSourceMode === "byo"`). Lists every
  configured policy with its real current-period used/limit count, a form to add/replace a policy (scope
  picker: whole account or a specific Community; daily/monthly; a positive request limit), and a Remove
  action per policy. New `src/lib/actions/watch-byo-usage-settings.ts` — same gating discipline as
  `watch-byo-settings.ts` (credential management): every export re-verifies the signed-in account's own real
  `apiSourceMode === "byo"` entitlement server-side, never a client-supplied account id or a UI-only gate.
- **Never touches Innvil's own commercial config** — confirmed via `git diff`: zero changes to `money.ts` or
  `watch-enterprise.ts` (Innvil's plan/pricing definitions). This is purely a customer-owned operational
  guardrail layered on top of an already-provisioned BYO credential, never a new Innvil-priced feature.
- New tests: `watch-byo-usage-policy.test.ts` (+19, new file — period-key formatting, CRUD incl. replace-not-
  duplicate and cross-account isolation, the gate's full allow/block/tightest-wins/cross-Community-isolation/
  fresh-period-reset matrix, usage recording incl. the "only configured scopes get written" rule and the
  atomic-increment-not-duplicate proof, the never-throws-on-failure guarantee, and the read-status shape),
  `watch-runtime.test.ts` (+4 — `resolveAccountAiRouting`'s new usage-policy integration: unaffected when no
  policy is configured, an exhausted account-wide policy correctly nulls the credential, a different
  Community's exhausted policy never blocks this one, and the account-wide policy still applies when no
  `communityId` is given at all). 1603 tests pass (up from 1580), `tsc --noEmit` clean, production build clean.
- **Not deployed automatically, per standing instruction.**
- **Deliberately not built this pass**: deployment/Watcher-level policy granularity (documented scope-down,
  see above); token-based limits (no real per-call token count is available anywhere in this codebase to meter
  against); counting link-classification/media-warning BYO calls individually toward the limit (no clean
  success signal exists for either, same judgment call already made for telemetry).

### 2026-08-25 — Watcher Presence Scheduling — Phase 4.U implemented (v1.47.44)
- **Deployed Watchers now auto-stagger being "conversationally present"** — sending a persona-voiced, scheduled
  arrival/departure message (`presence_started`/`presence_resumed`/`presence_ending`), so 2+ Watchers in one
  Community don't all go active/silent in lockstep. Full verbatim spec:
  `docs/moderator/watcher-presence-scheduling-spec.md` (Phase 4.U). Explicitly gated on current Telegram/
  moderation testing being stable (per the standing instruction it was queued under) — that condition was met,
  and the user picked this as the next task after BYO Enterprise Phase 2.
- **Explicit, user-confirmed scope decision (via AskUserQuestion): announcements only.** Presence controls
  ONLY the scheduled arrival/departure messages — it has ZERO effect on core safety/scam/phishing moderation
  (`runLinkModeration`/`runMediaModeration`, both untouched — confirmed via `git diff`) or on Natural Chatter's
  reactive candidate selection (`findChatterDeployments`, also untouched) — a Watcher still answers questions
  normally even while "away." Standalone (direct-Watch, Panel-less) accounts only, matching every other Watch
  feature this session — `resolveDeploymentTenant()` already returns `null` for Panel-owned deployments, so a
  legacy Panel-distributed community structurally can't reach this feature at all.
- **New pure, directly-tested scheduling algorithm** `src/lib/moderator/presence-schedule.ts` — a continuous,
  anchor-based rotation (no daily reset, DST-safe: each deployment resolves to a fixed
  `{anchorUtc, activeMinutes, cycleMinutes}`, and `presenceAt(config, now)` is plain elapsed-time-since-anchor
  arithmetic from there — never a live re-localization). `intervalKey` (the current interval's own UTC start
  instant) is the persisted idempotency identity. **Recommended formula** (deterministic, no randomness — owners
  need predictable schedules): `cycleMinutes = staggerMinutes * N`, `activeMinutes = min(staggerMinutes * 1.5,
  cycleMinutes)`, `anchorUtc = referenceUtc + orderIndex * staggerMinutes` — verified exactly against the spec's
  own N=2 worked example (Kwan 08:00–11:00 / away / 12:00–15:00, Test 10:00–13:00, real overlap at both
  10:00–11:00 and 12:00–13:00). N=1 naturally clamps to always-present. `applyCoverageWindow()` optionally
  forces `present:false` outside a community-wide local-time window (incl. overnight-wrap support).
- **Migration `0094_watch_presence_scheduling.sql`** — three tables, `enabled default false` everywhere (no
  existing deployment starts sending scheduled messages merely because the migration ran): `community_presence_settings`
  (mode/stagger/`reference_utc`/coverage window/announce-flag toggles, one row per Community, lazily created),
  `deployment_presence_config` (per-deployment resolved `{anchor_utc, active_minutes, cycle_minutes}` — the
  runtime always reads these three columns directly regardless of whether Recommended or Custom populated
  them), `deployment_presence_state` (the persisted runtime state + idempotency identity). RLS on, no policies
  (service-role only). **Migration `0095_supabase_watch_presence_cron.sql`** schedules
  `innvil-watch-presence-every-5-min` (mirrors `0056`'s exact vault-secret/`net.http_get` pattern). **Run
  migrations `0094` and `0095`** (+ schedule the pg_cron job) before this does anything live.
- **Runtime sweep** `src/lib/moderator/presence-runtime.ts` (`sweepPresenceSchedules`, cron route
  `app/api/cron/watch-presence`, mirrors `autopost`'s route exactly) — for every enabled deployment: resolves
  ownership via `resolveDeploymentTenant` (Panel-owned → skip), re-checks entitlement server-side via
  `getAccountCapacity`/new `presenceSchedulingEligible()` (Silver/Gold/Platinum/Enterprise only, Bronze/trial
  excluded — the SAME pure function gates both the UI tab and this runtime check, so they can never disagree),
  computes `{present, intervalKey}`, and compares against the PERSISTED state (never re-derived from
  `intervalKey` alone) — a genuine active↔away flip is claimed via `claimPresenceTransition()`, a real
  compare-and-swap (conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE state = priorState`, or a plain `INSERT` when no row exists
  yet — a real PK conflict on that insert is the race-loser's own signal) so two concurrent sweep invocations
  can never both announce the same transition. A delayed/missed sweep reconciles straight to the CURRENT
  computed state (`presenceAt` is a pure function of `now`, not of historical progression) — never replays
  every intermediate transition it missed. State is written (and `moderator_activity_log` gets an entry,
  `event_type: "presence"`) regardless of whether the community's matching `announce_*` flag is on — an
  announce-off transition still updates state, it just never generates/sends text.
- **Found and fixed a real bug during testing**: `transitionKindFor(priorState, nextState)` initially returned
  `"presence_ending"` for a brand-new deployment (no persisted row) that happens to compute `away` on its first
  sweep — wrong, since a deployment that's never been active has nothing to "end." Fixed: no-row + `away` is
  now correctly a no-op (matches the doc comment's own stated convention — a state row is only ever lazily
  created on the FIRST genuine transition to `active`). Caught by `presence-runtime.test.ts`, not live.
- **New sibling generation module** `src/lib/moderator/presence-generate.ts` (`generatePresenceMessage`) —
  mirrors `media-warning.ts`/`link-classify.ts`'s exact shape (small dedicated file, BYO-first, deterministic
  fallback pool) rather than force-fitting into `chatter-generate.ts` (whose whole prompt assumes a real
  triggering human message). Routed through the SAME cheap `deepseekChatterProvider()` tier CASUAL_CHAT already
  uses (low-stakes ambient text, never Sonnet 5's `getInnvilModelConfig()`). **BYO Enterprise wired in from day
  one**, reusing yesterday's `AccountAiRouting`/`byoProviderOverride` — `aiRouting?.required` checked first,
  falling straight to the per-kind deterministic template pool (never Innvil's own `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`) on any
  BYO failure. Prompt explicitly bans mentioning scheduling/rotation/presence-window mechanics — a transition
  message must read as a natural, unprompted social message, never leak internal system behavior (same
  no-hidden-mechanics principle already established for Natural Chatter, v1.9.14).
- **Owner-facing CRUD** `src/lib/actions/watch-presence.ts` — `getCommunityPresenceSchedule`/
  `resetToRecommendedSchedule`/`setDeploymentPresenceEnabled`/`setDeploymentPresenceConfig`/
  `setCommunityPresenceSettings`, ownership resolved via `listAccountCommunities` (the SAME canonical,
  cross-account-isolated Community list every other Watch action reuses). **These actions NEVER write
  `deployment_presence_state` or send a Telegram message themselves** — only the cron sweep does that, on its
  own next tick, reading whatever config now says; editing schedule config can never itself trigger an
  announcement (verified via `git diff`/grep — zero writes to that table anywhere in this file). Enabling a
  deployment immediately gives it a real starting schedule (recomputed alongside every other already-enabled
  deployment via the Recommended formula, reusing the community's existing `reference_utc` when one exists);
  disabling only flips the flag, preserving every other stored value so re-enabling later doesn't lose a custom
  configuration. `reference_utc` is recomputed ONLY by an explicit Reset-to-Recommended/first-enable action —
  never implicitly on an unrelated settings save.
- **New "Presence" tab** on the Community detail page (`app/communities/[id]/page.tsx`), between Watchers and
  Moderation — `PresenceScheduleCard.tsx` (mode badge, stagger-minutes + Reset-to-Recommended, coverage-window
  time inputs, 3 announce checkboxes, and a per-deployment row: enable toggle + a live-computed Present/Away
  status via the pure `presenceAt()` reused client-side + a "Customize" inline editor for direct active/cycle
  minute overrides). An ineligible account sees a plain upsell note instead of a broken/empty control (the
  component's own built-in eligibility gate, reused for both the UI and the runtime).
- New tests: `presence-schedule.test.ts` (16 — the N=1..5 formula, the exact spec worked example, `intervalKey`
  stability/advancement, coverage-window incl. overnight-wrap, the anchor-before-`now` edge case),
  `presence-generate.test.ts` (12 — DeepSeek routing incl. the full BYO-required/usable/missing matrix, varied
  template-pool fallback per transition kind, persona isolation, the no-hidden-mechanics prompt assertion),
  `presence-runtime.test.ts` (13 — `transitionKindFor`'s full state-machine incl. the regression above,
  `localMinutesOfDay` incl. an invalid-timezone safe fallback, and `claimPresenceTransition`'s full
  compare-and-swap contract: fresh insert, duplicate-insert-loses, valid CAS succeeds, stale CAS loses,
  exactly-one-of-two-concurrent-claims-wins). 1580 tests pass (up from 1543), `tsc --noEmit` clean, production
  build clean (confirmed `/api/cron/watch-presence` in the build output). **`sweepPresenceSchedules` itself has
  no full DB-mocked orchestrator test** — consistent with this codebase's own established convention for
  comparably complex orchestrators (`runAutoPostSweep`/`handleCommunityUpdate`, neither of which has one
  either) — verified via typecheck + build + code review instead; every exported pure/near-pure piece it calls
  is independently, thoroughly tested.
- **Not deployed automatically, per standing instruction.**
- **Deliberately not built this pass**: presence-inactive as a chatter-eligibility gate (explicitly rejected —
  see the scope decision above); a mode toggle exposed directly as Recommended/Custom radio buttons (mode is
  currently an implicit consequence of which action was last called — Reset-to-Recommended sets it to
  `recommended`, a direct Custom edit sets it to `custom` — rather than a separately click-through-able

  own Watcher list); a richer visual rotation timeline beyond the current-moment Present/Away line.

### 2026-08-24 — BYO Enterprise, Phase 2: live runtime wiring + usage telemetry + self-serve credential UI + landing positioning (v1.47.43)
- **Completes the four items deliberately deferred from Phase 1 (v1.47.42)** — BYO Enterprise now actually
  DOES something: an account flagged `api_source_mode='byo'` with a stored credential now has its real
  Telegram AI generation/classification calls routed through that credential, never Innvil's own. The
  **hard invariant held throughout**: a BYO account never silently falls back to Innvil's
  `AI_API_KEY`/`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` — a required-but-unusable credential (missing entirely, or missing a
  configured model) fails via each call site's own EXISTING safe path (a classifier's already-defined safe
  fallback; a generator's already-handled "generation failed, stay silent"; a warning generator's existing
  deterministic template pool) — confirmed by grep that `aiRouting?.required` is checked FIRST in every
  updated function, always in a branch that returns before `aiConfigured()`/`getInnvilModelConfig()`/
  `deepseekChatterProvider()` are ever reached.
- **(1) Runtime wiring.** New `AccountAiRouting` type + `MANAGED_AI_ROUTING` constant + `resolveAccountAiRouting`
  (`watch-runtime.ts`) — resolved ONCE per inbound Telegram event in `handleCommunityUpdate`, gated on
  `entitlementSource === "enterprise"` so a self-serve/trial account (the overwhelming majority of traffic)
  never pays for the extra Enterprise-entitlement lookup — and threaded through `handleHumanMessage` →
  `runMediaModeration`/`runLinkModeration`/`respondAsDeployment`/the ambient-greeting `classifyAmbientGreeting`
  call (`community-runtime.ts`). `resolveChatterRoute` (`chatter-generate.ts`) checks `aiRouting?.required`
  BEFORE any action-based branching — when true, BOTH ANSWER and CASUAL_CHAT route through the account's own
  credential (never `getInnvilModelConfig()`/`deepseekChatterProvider()`), using the credential's own configured
  `model` — a credential with no model set fails explicitly rather than guessing a default, since there's no
  honest default for an arbitrary customer-configured endpoint. Same BYO-first pattern applied to
  `classifyLinkIntent`/`generateModerationWarning` (`link-classify.ts`) and `generateMediaModerationWarning`
  (`media-warning.ts`). New shared `byoProviderOverride(credential)` helper (`watch-runtime.ts`) builds the
  `aiComplete` `providerOverride` shape once, reused by every generation module, so the per-provider default
  base URL (used only when the stored one is null) can never drift between call sites.
- **Confirmed, not assumed, which call sites are reachable for BYO at all**: `media-safety-provider.ts`/
  `sightengine-provider.ts` (the vision/NSFW CLASSIFIER, Sightengine — a fundamentally different vendor
  category `watch_byo_provider_credentials.provider` (`anthropic|openai`) has no way to represent; Innvil
  continues to own/pay for/meter it regardless of `api_source_mode`) and `bot-manager-classify.ts`
  (`innvil_bot_manager` is Innvil's own platform-wide bot, with no per-account context to resolve BYO from at
  all) are both **deliberately excluded**, a genuine scope correction from Phase 1's aspirational file list.
  `autopost-generate.ts` is **structurally unreachable** for BYO today: `auto_post_windows.panel_id` is
  `not null` and Auto-Posting has no account-scoped path at all, while Enterprise/BYO is exclusively
  account-scoped — an Enterprise BYO account cannot currently even create an Auto-Posting window, a
  pre-existing, separate, already-documented gap, not something this pass fixes.
- **(2) Usage telemetry.** New migration `0093_watch_byo_ai_usage_events.sql` — `watch_byo_ai_usage_events`
  (account_id, community_id nullable, automation, provider, model, `ok boolean`, error, created_at), indexed
  on `(account_id, created_at desc)`, service-role only. New `src/lib/products/watch-byo-usage.ts` —
  `recordByoUsageEvent` (best-effort, never throws — a telemetry write failure must never break moderation/
  chatter) + `getByoUsageSummary` (real observed call/success/failure counts grouped by automation, never a
  fabricated token/cost figure — deliberately NOT a token-cost accounting system, since capturing real token
  counts would require widening `aiComplete()`'s return shape across every existing caller in the codebase,
  a genuinely separate, larger change). **Scoped down from the original plan's "instrument all 4 call sites"
  to conversational replies only** (`respondAsDeployment`'s `generateChatterReply` outcome) — the ONE call site
  with a genuine, unambiguous ok/error signal to record (matches the scope of Innvil's own
  `MODERATOR_AI_GENERATION_POOL` metering for Managed accounts); `classifyLinkIntent`/`classifyAmbientGreeting`/
  the warning-generation functions all degrade gracefully to a safe fallback on ANY failure by design (never
  throw, never expose success/failure in their return shape) — recording them as "ok" regardless of the real
  outcome would be fabricated telemetry, so they're deliberately not instrumented. Recorded fire-and-forget
  (`void recordByoUsageEvent(...)`, never awaited) so a telemetry write can never add latency to the 30s-bounded
  webhook handler. `AccountCapacity` (`watch-runtime.ts`) gained `apiSourceMode`/`hasByoCredential` fields
  (the latter needs one small extra existence-check query, only fired for a BYO-flagged account). New
  **"BYO calls (last 30 days)"** card on `/usage`, shown only for a BYO-flagged account, real total/success/
  failure counts + per-automation breakdown, an amber note when no credential is stored yet.
- **(3) Self-serve credential UI.** New `src/lib/actions/watch-byo-settings.ts` (`getWatchByoCredentialState`/
  `setWatchByoCredential`/`clearWatchByoCredential`) — customer-session-authed (`getAuthedAdmin()`), gated

  devops-provisioned (no self-serve PURCHASE flow exists) — this only lets an ALREADY-provisioned BYO account
  manage its own credential without emailing support to rotate a key.
- **(4) Landing positioning.** `WatchPricingSection.tsx`'s Enterprise card — previously a bare "Custom pricing /
  Contact us" — now shows the real headline figures reused directly from `watch-enterprise.ts`
  (`MANAGED_ENTERPRISE_50.price` = $399, the lower `WATCH_ENTERPRISE_BYO_TIERS` price = $299) plus one honest
  line distinguishing Managed from BYO ("bring your own AI provider credential and pay less — your own

  configurator instead of a bare `/signup` dead end.
- New/updated tests: `watch-runtime.test.ts` (+13 — `resolveAccountAiRouting`'s full required/usable/missing/
  cross-account matrix, `AccountCapacity`'s new fields), `chatter-generate.test.ts` (+7 — BYO routes both
  ANSWER/CASUAL_CHAT via the actual outgoing request, missing credential/model fail explicitly with zero
  network calls, non-BYO behavior byte-identical to before), `link-classify.test.ts` (+5), `media-warning.test.ts`
  (+8, new file), `community-runtime.test.ts` (+3 — `GENERATION_STARTED`'s `provider` log field reflects BYO/
  `byo_unconfigured`/the original deepseek-or-anthropic values correctly), `watch-byo-usage.test.ts` (+8, new

### 2026-08-23 — BYO Enterprise, Phase 1: real entitlement mode + encrypted credential storage + devops grant (v1.47.42)
- **Closes the gap flagged repeatedly since the Enterprise-repricing pass (v1.47.26)**: "Bring Your Own [AI

  BYO Unlimited $499/mo) with **zero backing schema, credential storage, or grant path** — `product_entitlements`
  had no `api_source_mode`/BYO-shaped column at all, and the devops grant tool (`setAccountDevOpsEnterprise`,
  v1.47.37) could only create Managed entitlements. This pass builds the real entitlement/storage foundation;
  wiring the live AI runtime to actually USE a BYO account's credential is **explicitly deferred** — see below.

  `check (... is null or in ('managed','byo'))`, only meaningful for `tier==='enterprise'` rows; `NULL` = Managed,
  matching the already-documented "every Enterprise account today IS de facto Managed" honest state, additive,
  no backfill needed). New `watch_byo_provider_credentials` table (`account_id` PK, `provider` anthropic|openai,
  `credential_enc` bytea, `base_url`, `model`) — a SEPARATE table from `product_entitlements`, mirroring
  `telegram_bot_integrations`' own separate-table-per-credential-concept pattern. Encrypted the SAME way every
  other external credential in this schema already is — `pgp_sym_encrypt`/`pgp_sym_decrypt` via the SAME
  `PROVIDER_KEY_SECRET` env var, `set_watch_byo_credential`/`get_watch_byo_credential` `security definer` RPCs
  restricted to `service_role`, byte-for-byte the same shape as `set_provider_key`/`get_provider_key` — this is
  the 5th time this exact pattern has been used (SMM providers, panel payment gateways, platform payment
  gateways, Telegram bot tokens, now BYO AI credentials), never a new/weaker mechanism. **Run migration `0092`.**
- **New `src/lib/products/watch-byo.ts`** — `hasByoCredential` (cheap existence check, never decrypts),
  `getAccountByoCredential`/`setAccountByoCredential`/`clearAccountByoCredential`. The file's own doc comment
  states the scope boundary explicitly: storing/retrieving a credential here does **not** yet change any live
  AI call anywhere — every moderation/chatter/media-classification call site still uses Innvil's own credential
  today, regardless of what's stored here. Names every call site that must NOT import this module yet
  (`chatter-generate.ts`, `media-safety-provider.ts`, `autopost-generate.ts`, `bot-manager-classify.ts`,
  `link-classify.ts`, `media-warning.ts`) — confirmed via a repo-wide grep after implementation that this module
  is imported from exactly 3 files: the devops action, its UI (type-only), and its own test file. Zero AI-call
  sites touch it.
- **`watch-runtime.ts`'s `AccountEnterpriseEntitlement` gained `apiSourceMode: "managed" | "byo"`** —
  `resolveAccountEnterpriseEntitlement` (now exported, was private, for direct testability) resolves it
  defensively (only the exact stored string `"byo"` ever resolves to `"byo"`; anything else, including a
  corrupted value, falls back to `"managed"`, never fabricated). **Purely descriptive/routing metadata as of
  this field's introduction** — proven by a dedicated test that capacity/slot/Community-expansion resolution is
  byte-identical for a Managed vs. a BYO-flagged entitlement with otherwise-identical data.
- **`activateWatchEntitlement`** (`ownership.ts`) gained an 8th optional parameter, `apiSourceMode?: "managed" |
  "byo"` — same never-clobber-a-stray-value discipline as `enterpriseSlots`/`enterpriseCommunityCapacity`: left
  OUT of the upsert entirely when omitted (a renewal never resets an already-provisioned mode), only ever a
  real, type-restricted value when given.
- **`setAccountDevOpsEnterprise`** (`superadmin-watch-devops.ts`) gained the same optional `apiSourceMode`
  parameter, threaded straight into `activateWatchEntitlement`. **New `setAccountDevOpsByoCredential`/
  `clearAccountDevOpsByoCredential`** — same two safety gates as every other mutating action in this file
  (super-admin role + Preview-only) — let an admin store/rotate/clear a BYO account's credential as part of

- **UI** (`WatchDevOpsAdmin.tsx`) — the Enterprise grant form gained a Managed/BYO radio; selecting BYO reveals

- New tests: `watch-byo.test.ts` (+14, new file — existence check, set/get round-trip incl. optional-field

### 2026-08-23 — Media Moderation Unit metering — Media Moderation + now actually gates and meters real usage (v1.47.40)
- **Product decision, confirmed before building anything**: investigated the runtime gate first (`virtualModMediaModeration`
  in `plan.ts`) and found it never checked the paid add-on at all — `MEDIA_MODERATION_ENABLED &&
  virtualModModeration(settings)`, i.e. ANY entitled Watch account already got full photo/video classification
  and enforcement for free, completely independent of whether they'd purchased "Media Moderation +". The
  add-on's purchase had zero effect on the live runtime, only on Billing/Usage display. Confirmed with the user
  that the intended model is real gating (self-serve accounts must hold an active add-on to get media
  moderation at all, with a real unit allowance) — not a permanently-free baseline capability.
- **Gate scoped to self-serve tiers only, by design.** `runMediaModeration` (`community-runtime.ts`) gained
  `accountId`/`paidTier` parameters (threaded from `handleHumanMessage`, already resolved there for the AI
  Generation pool gate — no second lookup). The gate only runs `if (accountId && paidTier)` — `paidTier` is
  `null` for trial (can't purchase an add-on at all) AND for Enterprise (its own Media Moderation + is
  inquiry/manual-provisioning with no persisted entitlement row to check, per `ENTERPRISE_MEDIA_ADDON`'s own doc
  comment) AND for legacy Panel-distributed accounts. All three keep running media moderation exactly as before
  this pass — unmetered, ungated — a deliberate, explicit non-regression, not an oversight.
- **A self-serve account with no active add-on, or one that's exhausted its real monthly allowance, gets a
  silent skip** — never a fabricated verdict, never a deleted message, matching every other "can't classify"
  case already in this function (`too_large`/`duration_exceeded`/`download_failed`). New SKIPPED reasons
  `media_addon_required`/`media_allowance_exhausted`. Deliberately NOT run through the existing
  `recordMediaDedup` cache (unlike the size/duration checks, which are permanent file properties) — addon/
  allowance state is temporal, so caching it would permanently blacklist a file from ever being reclassified
  once the add-on is purchased or the period renews.
- **New migration `0091_watch_media_moderation_usage.sql`** — `watch_media_moderation_usage`, mirrors migration
  `0084`'s `watch_ai_response_usage` exactly (keyed by `(account_id, period_start)`, one row per real
  subscription period, a renewal naturally starts fresh at 0). One real difference: `increment_watch_media_
  moderation_usage`'s RPC increments by a variable `p_units`, not always 1 — a video's units are its real
  classified-frame count in ONE round trip, not N separate calls. **Run migration `0091`.**
- **New `src/lib/products/watch-media-moderation-usage.ts`** — `getWatchMediaModerationUsage`/
  `incrementWatchMediaModerationUsage`/`hasMediaModerationUnitsRemaining`, mirrors `watch-ai-usage.ts`'s exact
  shape and reuses its `resolveAccountBillingPeriod`/`WatchBillingPeriod` directly (Media Moderation + renews on
  the same cadence as the base subscription — never a second period resolver).
- **A "unit" is exactly what the money.ts doc comment already promised**: 1 classified photo, or 1 sampled video
  frame that received a REAL (`ok:true`) classification — never an attempted-but-failed provider call (same
  counting philosophy already established for the AI Generation pool: a provider timeout/auth failure never
  costs the customer a unit). `classifySampledFrames` (`media-moderation.ts`) widened from returning a bare
  `MediaClassificationResult` to `{result, framesClassified}` — `framesClassified` counts only the real
  successful classifications within the bounded, early-exit-respecting sample, never the raw call count. The
  existing bounded-sampling architecture (`computeSamplePositions`/`MAX_VIDEO_SAMPLE_FRAMES`) is completely
  unchanged — the entitlement never determines how many frames get sampled, only whether classification happens
  at all.
- **Usage consumed even when the result is ALLOWed** — a unit means "was this actually classified," never "was
  it flagged." Incremented once, right after classification, independent of the downstream enforcement outcome.
- **Usage page updated to match** — the Media Moderation + card now shows a real `used / allowance` count with
  a progress bar (was a static allowance-only display with an "isn't metered yet" disclaimer, now stale and
  removed). Also fixed an adjacent stale comment claiming "no purchase/removal action exists yet" for this
  add-on — that shipped in v1.47.33.
- New tests: `media-moderation.test.ts` (4 existing tests updated for the new `{result, framesClassified}`
  return shape, including a dedicated proof that a failed frame is never counted as a classified unit),
  `watch-media-moderation-usage.test.ts` (+7, new file — variable-increment behavior incl. a real video-frame-
  count worked example, zero-unit no-op guard, per-account isolation, fresh-period-starts-at-zero, headroom
  boundary). 1469 tests pass (up from 1462), `tsc --noEmit` clean, production build clean. Diff reviewed: 7
  files (3 new + 4 changed), all directly in scope.
- **`runMediaModeration` itself has no new dedicated DB-mocked integration test** — consistent with this exact
  function's own pre-existing, already-documented convention (verified via typecheck + build + careful code
  review instead, same as every other pass that's touched this function); every new PURE/IO piece it now calls
  (`getMediaModerationAddonState`, `hasMediaModerationUnitsRemaining`, `getWatchMediaModerationUsage`/
  `incrementWatchMediaModerationUsage`, `classifySampledFrames`'s new field) is independently fully tested.
- **Not deployed automatically, per standing instruction.**
- **Deliberately not built this pass**: metering/gating for Enterprise's own Media Moderation + (no persisted
  entitlement state exists to gate against — a real prerequisite gap, same category as Enterprise's still-

### 2026-08-23 — Critical fix: a standalone Enterprise Watcher did nothing on live Telegram (v1.47.39)
- **Found while investigating Media Moderation Unit metering (the next queued task), reported and confirmed
  before fixing** — an entire tier's live runtime was dark, not just one capability, so it was fixed first per
  explicit direction.
- **Root cause**: `resolveStandaloneModeratorSettings` (`watch-runtime.ts`), the function the live webhook
  handler (`handleCommunityUpdate`) uses to build the capability-gating settings object for a standalone
  (non-Panel) integration, had **no Enterprise branch at all**. It called `resolveAccountWatchTier` (only ever
  returns the 4 self-serve tiers), then fell to a trial check, then returned `null`. For an account whose ONLY
  entitlement is Enterprise, both checks fail and settings resolve to `null` — every downstream
  `virtualMod*(settings)` capability check in `moderator/plan.ts` fails closed on `null`, so the Watcher
  performed zero chatter, zero moderation, zero anything, for every real Telegram message. **Never caught
  before now because there was no way to grant a real Enterprise entitlement to any account until the devops
  tool (`setAccountDevOpsEnterprise`) shipped yesterday (v1.47.37)** — this bug was unreachable until then.
- **Fix, scoped narrowly, not a rewrite of the capability model.** `moderator/plan.ts`'s
  `ModeratorEntitlementSource` widened from `"trial" | ModeratorPlanTier | null` to also include
  `"enterprise"` — mirroring the EXACT distinction Watch's own `AccountWatchContext.tier` already makes
  (`ModeratorPlanTier | "trial" | "enterprise"`), never squeezing Enterprise into the 4-value
  `ModeratorPlanTier` union (which would have broken `CAPACITY`/`MODERATOR_COMMUNITY_CAPACITY`'s fixed
  `Record<ModeratorPlanTier, ...>` lookups). New `enterprise: boolean` field on `ModeratorAddonSub` (parsed by
  `readModeratorAddon`, alongside the existing separate `trial` sub-object — same pattern, not reusing `tier`).
  `moderatorEntitlementSource` now resolves it (precedence: self-serve tier > enterprise > trial, matching
  `requireAccountWatchContext`'s own documented order). `virtualModProactiveMode` (and everything that
  delegates through it — `virtualModAdvancedModeration`/`virtualModCommunityMemory`/`virtualModCustomPersonality`)
  now includes `source === "enterprise"`, so Enterprise correctly unlocks everything Platinum unlocks.
  `virtualModContentGeneration` also checks the new `enterprise` flag directly (was `!!moderatorTier(settings)`
  only, which structurally excludes Enterprise since `moderatorTier` only ever reads the self-serve `tier`
  field).
- **New `buildStandaloneEnterpriseModeratorSettings()`** (`watch-runtime.ts`) synthesizes `{tier: null,
  enterprise: true, ...}` — deliberately NOT reusing `"pro"`/Platinum as a shortcut. That would have introduced
  a REAL second bug: `community-runtime.ts`'s AI-Generation-pool usage gate derives `paidTier` from the same

### 2026-08-23 — Admin tooling: real `profiles.email` column — delete a test account in one place (v1.47.36)
- **Follow-up correction to v1.47.35, per explicit request** — the view-based lookup wasn't what was actually
  needed: deleting a row from `product_entitlements_with_email`/`profiles_with_email` (both views) does
  nothing, and deleting the underlying `profiles` row directly didn't fully remove the account either (see
  below) — the real ask was "delete directly from the accounts table" using a visible email column.
- **Migration `0090_profiles_email_column.sql`** — `profiles.email` is now a REAL, unique, indexed column (not
  a duplicated snapshot that can drift on its own): one-time backfill from `auth.users.email` for every
  existing row, then kept current going forward by (1) `handle_new_user()` now copies email in at signup
  alongside `display_name`, and (2) a new `sync_profile_email()` trigger on `auth.users` (`AFTER UPDATE OF
  email`) propagates any later change — every email-change action in this codebase (`customerUpdateEmail`,
  account settings) only ever writes `auth.users`, so this is the single sync point, never a second place the
  app itself needs to remember to update.
- **Root cause of "deleting from profiles doesn't actually remove the account"**: `profiles.id references
  auth.users(id) on delete cascade` only cascades ONE direction (auth.users → profiles) — deleting `profiles`
  directly left the `auth.users` row orphaned (no profile, but still a real login), and worse, re-signing up
  with the same email would fail ("already registered") since Supabase Auth still had it. Every OTHER app
  table already correctly cascades off `profiles.id` (spot-checked across every `account_id`/`owner_id`
  foreign key in the schema) — the ONE missing direction was profiles → auth.users.
- **New `delete_auth_user_on_profile_delete()` trigger (`AFTER DELETE ON profiles`)** closes that gap — deleting
  a `profiles` row (via Table Editor, or `DELETE FROM profiles WHERE id = ...`) now also deletes the matching
  `auth.users` row, making it a real, complete, one-step account removal; deleting via Studio's
  Authentication > Users (or the admin API) still works exactly as before, unaffected.
- **Supersedes `profiles_with_email` from v1.47.35** (dropped — redundant now that `profiles` itself carries
  email); `product_entitlements_with_email` is untouched, still useful for identifying which entitlement
  belongs to which account before deleting it.
- `src/types/db.ts`'s `ProfileRow` gained `email: string | null`, documented as sync-only/never-write-directly.
- No app code otherwise changed — this is DB tooling, not a product feature. 1449 tests pass (unaffected —
  purely additive schema/type change), `tsc --noEmit` clean, production build clean.
- **Run migration `0090`** (0089 should still be run first if it wasn't already — this migration drops one of
  its two views but assumes the base schema state 0089 didn't otherwise touch).
- **Caveat, stated honestly**: both the email-sync trigger AND the delete-cascade trigger touch `auth.users`
  and may fail with `insufficient_privilege` depending on the exact role migrations run as in this Supabase
  project — same known limitation the original `handle_new_user()` trigger (migration 0001) already documents
  and tolerates (guarded, never aborts the migration). If the delete-cascade trigger can't be created or its
  body can't execute, deleting from `profiles` will still clean up every other app table (that direction was
  always fine) but leave the `auth.users` row behind — fall back to deleting that user via Studio's
  Authentication > Users page in that case.

### 2026-08-22 — Fix: Managed Enterprise >50-slot pricing bug ($662→$407) + real add-on CTAs (v1.47.32)
- **Root cause of the $662/51-slot bug**: `managedEnterprisePrice(slots)` (`watch-enterprise.ts`) still called the
  OLD, superseded Platinum-based dynamic per-slot formula (`moderatorEnterpriseSlotPrice`) for any slot count
  above 50 — that formula was only ever meant to price the standalone Panel-side Enterprise sale, never the new
  fixed $399 Managed Enterprise 50 package's own continuation above 50 slots. At 51 slots it computed
  `$199.00 base + 31×$15 = $664.00`, not the intended `$399 + $8 = $407`.
- **New canonical formula** (`managedEnterprisePriceAtSlots` in `money.ts`, `ENTERPRISE_MANAGED_EXTRA_SLOT_PRICE
  = 8`): `slots <= 50` → the fixed $399; `slots > 50` → `$399 + $8 × (slots − 50)`, integer-cents exact. Worked
  examples, all now correct: 50 = $399, 51 = $407, 60 = $479, 75 = $599, 100 = $799, 150 = $1,199.
  `moderatorEnterpriseSlotPrice`/`moderatorEnterpriseIncludedCommunities` are no longer called anywhere in the
  Managed Enterprise pricing path — they remain only for `resolveAccountEnterpriseEntitlement`'s Community-count
  resolution on an existing manually-provisioned entitlement (a separate, narrower concern, pending the queued

  as fact) from PROVISIONING (still manual/completed-with-support) rather than hedging the price itself as an

### 2026-08-22 — "AI Generations": new pooled allowances + a real counting-semantics change (v1.47.28)
- **Phase 2 of the pricing overhaul (self-serve base price cut was Phase 1, v1.47.27).** Renamed the pooled
  monthly self-serve usage unit from "AI response(s)" to **"AI Generations"** throughout, and changed BOTH the
  allowance values and WHEN a unit is actually consumed.
- **New allowances** (`MODERATOR_AI_GENERATION_POOL` in `money.ts`, was `MODERATOR_AI_RESPONSE_POOL`): Bronze
  1,200→**2,000**, Silver 2,400→**5,000**, Gold 4,200→**10,000**, Platinum 7,200→**20,000**, per billing period,
  pooled per ACCOUNT (never per-Watcher). Enterprise keeps its own separate, much larger fixed pool
  (`ENTERPRISE_MANAGED_50_AI_GENERATIONS` = 50,000, added in v1.47.26) — never this `Record`.
- **Real counting-semantics change, not just a rename.** Was: incremented only after the Telegram send actually
  succeeded (`sent.sentMessageId` truthy). Now: incremented the moment the underlying provider call **succeeds**
  (right after `generateChatterReply` returns a real reply, in `respondAsDeployment`, `community-runtime.ts`) —
  moved BEFORE the Telegram send, unconditional on delivery outcome. Concretely: a provider timeout/auth
  failure/outage/declined generation still counts **0** (every one of those paths `return`s before reaching the
  new increment line); a successful generation whose Telegram delivery subsequently fails still counts **1**
  (the provider spend already happened). Deterministic/zero-call paths (SILENCE, REACT, SHORT_ACK, moderation)
  are unaffected — they never reached the increment either way. **The trial's own SEPARATE reactive-quota
  counter (`TRIAL_REACTIVE_DAILY_LIMIT`, a different daily/per-Community mechanism) keeps its existing
  count-on-confirmed-send rule, unchanged** — the two are different products with different counting rules,
  never conflated.
- **Full terminology rename, values-and-names kept in lockstep so nothing could drift**:
  `MODERATOR_AI_RESPONSE_POOL`→`MODERATOR_AI_GENERATION_POOL`, `aiResponsePoolLimit`→`aiGenerationPoolLimit`,
  `hasAiResponsePoolRemaining`→`hasAiGenerationPoolRemaining`, `getWatchAiResponseUsage`→
  `getWatchAiGenerationUsage`, `incrementWatchAiResponseUsage`→`incrementWatchAiGenerationUsage`,
  `customerModeratorAiResponsePool`→`customerModeratorAiGenerationPool` (the older Panel-distributed customer-
  entitlement variant), the `SILENCE` reason code `ai_response_pool_exhausted`→`ai_generation_pool_exhausted`.
  **Deliberately did NOT rename the underlying DB table/RPC** (`watch_ai_response_usage` /
  `increment_watch_ai_response_usage`) — that would require a migration touching live data for zero customer-
  visible benefit; only the exported function/constant names and all customer-facing copy changed. Usage page
  card titles renamed ("AI responses" → "AI Generations", "AI responses (today)" → "AI Generations (today)" for
  the trial's own daily card).
- New/updated tests: `money.test.ts` (repriced pool values), `watch-ai-usage.test.ts` (renamed + repriced
  boundary tests), `customer-entitlement.test.ts` (renamed function, repriced values), `community-runtime.test.ts`
  (renamed exhaustion reason code + repriced boundary fixtures, 2000 now the exact Bronze boundary). **The
  positive "does the increment actually fire independent of delivery outcome" path is NOT covered by a new
  end-to-end test** — consistent with this exact test file's own pre-existing, explicitly-stated convention of
  never exercising `respondAsDeployment`'s successful-generation path in tests (it would require a real
  `generateChatterReply`/AI provider call, which risks hitting a live provider if a key happens to be configured
  in the test shell); verified instead via code review of the exact reordering (the increment call was moved to
  execute unconditionally right after `generation.ok`, strictly before the `SEND_TEXT`/`executeAction` call, with
  no remaining reference to `sent.sentMessageId` anywhere near it). 1392 tests pass, `tsc --noEmit` clean,
  production build clean.
- **Not deployed automatically, per standing instruction.**
- **Still not built** (unchanged scope from v1.47.26/27): a self-serve Media Moderation + add-on, the Plans-page
  FAQ removal/relocation and Watcher-slot-education relocation, and a broader terminology sweep beyond the two
  Usage-page card titles + the internal identifier rename above (e.g. any remaining "reply"/"response" wording
  in onboarding copy, emails, or the storefront AI Moderator surface was not audited this pass).
