### 2026-08-20 — Explicit product decisions: "everyone" engages every deployed moderator + decline-fallback reroute (v1.47.22)
- **Live bug report, investigated via direct DB query before touching anything**: (1) "hi everyone, how are you
  guys?" with 2 moderators deployed only got one reply; (2) "doing fine, how about Ms VP?" (right after Mr Pres
  had just replied) got no reply at all from either moderator.
- **Root cause 1**: `roomWideResponderCount()` (v1.13.1) scaled "everyone"/"everybody" responders as
  `ceil(deployed/2)` — 2 deployed → 1 responds, by design, not a bug. **Explicit product decision (confirmed
  with the user via AskUserQuestion): "everyone" should engage every currently deployed moderator**, matching
  the old panel-based product's behavior, not a fraction of the team. `roomWideResponderCount()` now returns
  `min(activeModeratorCount, MAX_ROOM_WIDE_RESPONDERS)` (new cap = 5, so a very large deployment — up to 20
  Active Moderator Slots on Pro — still can't pile on unboundedly), never less than the deployed count for a
  realistic (≤5) team. Supersedes the old `ceil(n/2)` scaling entirely; the small explicit plural ("you both",
  `MAX_ADDITIONAL_RESPONDERS = 2`) is a separate, already-correct category, untouched.
- **Root cause 2, found by tracing the real activity log**: "how about Ms VP?" has no `@mention`/comma-before-
  name, so (correctly, per the existing referential-vs-vocative rule from v1.9.3) it wasn't treated as directed
  at Ms VP — continuity picked Mr Pres (he'd replied last), Mr Pres tried to answer, and the model correctly
  **declined** rather than fabricate an answer about someone else (`MODEL_DECLINED`) — which previously just
  produced silence with no recovery. **Explicit product decision: when the picked responder's own model
  declines, and a DIFFERENTLY-deployed moderator's name appears anywhere in the message, retry once with that
  moderator, treated as directed.** `respondAsDeployment()` now returns `{replied:false, modelDeclined?:
  boolean}` (was a bare `{replied:false}`) so `handleHumanMessage` can distinguish "the model made a reasoned
  decline" from every other reason a responder might not reply (generation timeout/failure, quota exhaustion —
  none of those are retried, since a different moderator wouldn't fix an infra failure). The reroute is bounded
  to exactly ONE retry — never chains further even if the reroute itself also declines — and the downstream
  multi-target/additional-responder logic was updated to key off whichever deployment actually ended up
  responding (`respondingDeployment`), not always the originally-picked one, so a rerouted reply is correctly
  excluded from any further additional-responder fan-out and correctly attributed in `priorResponsesToThisMessage`.
- New/updated tests: `chatter-coordinator.test.ts` — `roomWideResponderCount`'s pinned examples rewritten for the
  new "everyone = every deployed moderator" semantics (2→2, 3→3, 5→5, capped at 5 for 10/20 deployed), the small-
  plural cap test unaffected. 1373 tests pass (unchanged count — 2 old pinned examples replaced by 2 new ones),
  `tsc --noEmit` clean, production build clean. **The decline-fallback reroute itself (community-runtime.ts) has
  no new dedicated DB/AI-network-mocked test** — reaching it requires a full fake admin plus a mocked model
  "decline" response, the same category of orchestration this codebase already leaves to typecheck + build +
  code review for comparably deep paths (documented precedent throughout this file); the pure logic change
  (`roomWideResponderCount`) is fully unit-tested.
- **Not deployed automatically, per explicit instruction.**

### 2026-08-20 — Watcher Profile: Disconnect / Replace Telegram bot token (v1.47.21)
- **New, narrowly-scoped feature**: a Watcher Profile's Telegram bot integration can now be disconnected and
  reconnected/rotated without touching anything else — the Watcher Profile (name/persona/settings), its
  Communities, its `moderator_deployments` records, and all Activity/moderation history are completely
  untouched by either operation. Deliberately NOT a general Telegram identity feature and does NOT touch
  Profile's personal-Telegram-account linking (`ConnectTelegramCard`, a structurally separate table/flow).
- **Disconnect (`disconnectAccountModeratorBot`, `watch-moderator.ts`)**: best-effort `deleteWebhook` on
  Telegram using the current credential ONE LAST TIME (never blocks on Telegram being unreachable — the owner's
  explicit disconnect request always succeeds on our side), then the stored `credential_enc` is nulled and
  `telegram_bot_integrations.manager_relationship` set to `'revoked'` (row itself is KEPT, preserving the last-
  known @username for display — never deleted, so history like "previously @mrpreswan_bot" survives). The bot
  is never deleted from Telegram/BotFather — only Innvil's own ability to act on its updates is removed.
  `virtual_moderators.provisioning_status` moves to a new **`'disconnected'`** value (migration
  `0085_watch_bot_disconnect.sql`, additive to the existing CHECK constraint) — distinct from every
  pre-connection status (`draft`/`cancelled`/`expired`/...), since none of those honestly describe "this
  Watcher HAD a working bot, the owner deliberately disconnected it." `moderator_deployments` rows are never
  disabled/deleted here — they're left exactly as they were, and the Watcher detail page (Deployments tab)
  shows an explicit amber note ("these deployments are preserved but not currently operational") rather than
  implying anything was removed.
- **Reconnect / Replace token (`replaceAccountModeratorBotToken`)** covers BOTH first-time connect and
  rotating an already-connected bot's token via one flow: the new token is ALWAYS verified against Telegram
  (`verifyBotToken`, the SAME helper `connectCustomerBotToken`'s existing customer-facing flow already uses)
  **before** anything is written — an invalid token never touches stored state, so a Watcher can never be left
  partially connected. Bot username/id come ONLY from Telegram's own verified response, never from user input.
  Once validated, a single upsert overwrites the old credential (`set_telegram_bot_key`) — there is no window
  where two credentials are simultaneously live for the same integration row. Existing `moderator_deployments`
  rows are never touched — the moment a live credential exists again, those SAME rows become operational on
  their own, so reconnecting can never produce a duplicate deployment. New pure
  `nextProvisioningStatusAfterConnect(deploymentCount)` (`watch-runtime.ts`, directly unit-tested — kept out of
  `watch-moderator.ts` itself since every export of a `"use server"` file must be async, the same lesson
  learned the hard way in the v1.11.1 incident) resolves back to `'active'` when real deployment records
  already exist, `'bot_ready'` otherwise.
- **Security**: the token is never read back from the server after storage (`getWatcherTelegramIntegration`
  returns only `{connected, username, telegramBotId, deploymentCount}` — never the credential), never logged,
  and the new `WatcherTelegramCard.tsx` UI clears its local `token` state immediately on submit regardless of
  outcome — there is no "reveal token" control anywhere.
- **Confirmation UX**: Disconnect requires an explicit second click; when the Watcher has ≥1 deployment, the
  confirm panel shows the exact requested warning shape ("This Watcher is deployed to N Communities.
  Disconnecting its Telegram bot will stop Telegram activity for those deployments until a bot is
  reconnected."). Copy throughout says "Disconnect Telegram bot," never "Delete bot."
- **Audit**: both operations write to the existing `audit_logs` table (`watch.moderator_bot_disconnected`
  / `watch.moderator_bot_token_replaced`) with only `{moderatorId, username}` in `meta` — the token itself is
  never included, by construction (callers never have it in scope at logging time).
- **Account isolation**: both actions reuse `ctxModerator()`, the SAME ownership guard
  (`virtual_moderators.account_id === signed-in account`) every other Watcher action in this file already uses
  — never a second/parallel check.
- **UI**: new `WatcherTelegramCard.tsx`, mounted on the Watcher detail page's existing **Settings** tab
  (`app/watchers/[id]/page.tsx`) — Connected state shows `@username` + Replace/Disconnect; Disconnected state
  shows "Not connected" (or "Previously @username" once a bot has existed) + Connect. `WatcherConnectCta` /
  `WatcherConnectModal` (the existing managed-bot creation flow) are completely untouched — this is an
  additional, independent control for the token-paste path, not a replacement.
- New tests: `watch-runtime.test.ts` (+2 — `nextProvisioningStatusAfterConnect`'s both branches). **No dedicated
  DB/Telegram-mocked action-level test file was added for `disconnectAccountModeratorBot`/
  `replaceAccountModeratorBotToken`/`getWatcherTelegramIntegration` themselves** — consistent with this exact
  file's own pre-existing convention (every other function in `watch-moderator.ts`, including the original
  `connectCustomerBotToken`/`connectAccountCommunity` this pass extends, has zero dedicated tests, since
  `ctxModerator()` depends on `getAuthedAdmin()`'s real session cookie resolution, the same session-auth-wrapping
  reason this codebase doesn't DB-mock comparable action files elsewhere). Verified instead via `tsc --noEmit` +
  full test suite (1373 pass, up from 1371) + production build + thorough code review of the new functions
  against every explicit requirement (validate-before-write, no duplicate deployments, no token echo, audit
  metadata excludes the token, account isolation via the existing guard).
- **Run migration `0085`** before this governs any live account.
- **Not deployed automatically, per explicit instruction.**

### 2026-08-20 — Needs Attention: full plan capacity is healthy, not a warning (v1.47.20)
- **Live-observed gap, reported directly by the user**: a Bronze account exactly at 1/1 Community capacity showed
  a MEDIUM "Community capacity is at 1/1 on your current plan" item inside "Needs attention (2)" — alongside a
  genuine LOW item ("Ms VP isn't deployed to a community yet"). Root cause: `listAccountAttentionItems`
  (`watch-runtime.ts`) fired a MEDIUM item whenever usage was `>= 90%` of the plan limit (`CAPACITY_ATTENTION_
  THRESHOLD = 0.9`) — a "nearing/at capacity, consider upgrading" nudge that reads as upsell framing dressed up
  as an operational warning, and is trivially true for ANY fully-utilized account on ANY plan.
- **Final semantics** (explicit product decision): being AT/full capacity (used === total) is a normal, healthy
  state — it means the customer is using exactly what they purchased, never a problem. "Needs attention" is
  reserved for incomplete, blocked, failed, expired, or genuinely INCONSISTENT states — never "you're fully
  using your plan." The only capacity-related condition that still surfaces is usage **exceeding** the current
  entitlement's limit (`capacityExceedsLimit(used, total) = total > 0 && used > total`) — a real anomaly (e.g. a
  downgrade left more Communities/deployments active than the new plan allows; this codebase never deletes
  resources on downgrade/expiry, confirmed unchanged) that can never happen through normal server-side-enforced
  creation, but is a real, representable state worth surfacing.
- **Plan-agnostic by construction** — `capacityExceedsLimit` is a plain `used > total` comparison with zero
  plan-name branches; applies identically to Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum/Enterprise-BYO capacity, per explicit
  instruction not to scatter tier-specific exceptions.
- **Structural capacity stays fully visible, per explicit instruction** — `CapacityRow` (`WatchUI.tsx`, used on
  both Overview and Usage's Plan Capacity card) now shows a small neutral-teal **"· Capacity full"** note when
  `used >= total`, alongside the existing "X of Y" + progress bar — informational, never colored as a warning.
  The change is scoped entirely to whether "full" counts toward the Needs Attention list/badge — nothing about
  capacity became less visible.
- **Everything else in the resolver is untouched**: HIGH (a Community with no active Watcher) and LOW
  (undeployed/paused Watcher) conditions are exactly as before — only the MEDIUM capacity branch's threshold
  changed. `watch-notifications.ts`'s email-digest sweep needed no code change (it only reuses
  `listAccountAttentionItems` directly) — its doc comment was corrected for accuracy.
- New/updated tests (`watch-runtime.test.ts`): exactly-at-limit Watcher-slot and Community capacity now assert
  **no** attention item (was the opposite before — that assertion was itself testing the now-rejected behavior,
  rewritten rather than blindly preserved), two new genuine-over-capacity regression tests (6 active deployments
  on a 5-slot plan; 3 Communities on a 2-community plan) confirming the real-inconsistency case still surfaces
  as MEDIUM, existing under-limit/saved-profiles-alone/undeployed-Watcher-stays-LOW/severity-sort tests all still
  pass unchanged. 1371 tests pass (up from 1368), `tsc --noEmit` clean, production build clean. Diff reviewed:
  exactly 4 files, no plan-name-specific checks, no duplicated capacity math, no upsell copy in the operational
  path, no unrelated UI changes.
- **Not deployed automatically, per explicit instruction.**

### 2026-08-20 — Fixed: a directed @mention right after another user's greeting-shaped message went unanswered — a routing bug, not an idempotency bug (v1.47.17)
- **Live reproducible bug**: in the same Community, User A sent "hi Mr Pres" (answered correctly); User B, a
  different Telegram account, then sent "hey @mrpreswan_bot" — Mr Pres never responded.
- **Full investigation performed first, per explicit instruction, before touching any code** — traced the
  complete webhook -> routing -> Coordinator pipeline and inspected EVERY dedup/claim/handled mechanism in
  `community-runtime.ts`: `isDuplicateUpdate` (keyed on `(integration_id, update_id)` — Telegram's own per-bot
  update id, a DIFFERENT id for User A's and User B's messages, so this can't be the cause) and
  `recordCommunityMessage` (the cross-bot claim-race, unique on `(community_id, platform_message_id)` — Telegram's
  own per-chat message id, again distinct for the two messages, and correctly NOT keyed by sender/content/Watcher
  at all). **Both of these are correctly scoped exact-event-duplication guards and were confirmed innocent** —
  neither one is, or was, the bug.
- **Actual root cause: a routing/classification bug in `selectChatterAction`'s `COMMUNITY_OPENER` branch**
  (`chatter-coordinator.ts`). `classifyMessageKind` classifies any message containing a bare greeting word
  (`gm`/`hi`/`hey`/`hello`/…, via `GREETING_RE`/`isConversationalOpener`) as `COMMUNITY_OPENER` whenever it isn't
  ALSO a question/problem/acknowledgement — "hey @mrpreswan_bot" has no `?`, no problem word, no closing-ack
  signal, so it classified as `COMMUNITY_OPENER` purely because of "hey". The `COMMUNITY_OPENER` branch then
  checked ONLY `input.recentlyAnsweredByModerator`/`recentlyRespondedByHuman` — an AMBIENT "has the room already
  been handled" signal, correct for a truly untargeted "gm everyone" right after the room was just answered —
  and returned `SILENCE("already_handled")` **without ever checking `isDirectedAtBot`**, unlike every other
  branch in this function (QUESTION, SUBSTANTIVE), which already treat an explicit @mention/reply/configured-name
  match as an override of ambient continuity/suppression state. This is a genuine, narrow inconsistency in one
  branch, not a systemic idempotency problem — confirms the user's own hypothesis that "isHandled" reasoning was
  scoped too broadly, but the actual over-broad state lives in the Coordinator's ambient-opener suppression, not
  in any DB-level dedup/claim table.
- **Fix — narrowly scoped to the `COMMUNITY_OPENER` branch, nothing else touched.** A directed candidate
  (`isDirectedAtBot`) is now checked FIRST inside that branch; when present, the message resolves to
  `CASUAL_CHAT` with reason `directed_opener`, completely bypassing the ambient `already_handled` suppression —
  matching the same directed-overrides-continuity precedent every other branch already follows. An undirected,
  purely ambient opener ("gm everyone" with nobody @mentioned) is STILL correctly suppressed by
  `already_handled` exactly as before — this fix changes nothing about ambient-opener behavior, only about a
  message that is ALSO explicitly directed at a specific Watcher.
- **Idempotency and single-enforcer protections are completely untouched and still fully intact** —
  `isDuplicateUpdate`/`recordCommunityMessage` were not modified at all; a genuine retry of the exact same
  Telegram update/message is still suppressed exactly as before. **No TTL, cache, or new state was added** — the
  fix is a pure reordering of two already-existing checks inside one branch of a pure, synchronous function.
  `resolveAmbientOpenerFallback` (the DeepSeek-assisted "waddup guys"-style fallback classifier) needed no
  equivalent fix — it's only ever reached from the `low_social_priority` SILENCE case in the `SUBSTANTIVE`
  branch, which already requires the message to be non-directed before it can reach that state at all, so a
  directed message structurally never enters that fallback path.
- **Final distinction, now explicit in code comments**: **event idempotency** (`isDuplicateUpdate`/
  `recordCommunityMessage`) answers "has this exact Telegram update/message already been processed?" — scoped by
  `(integration_id, update_id)` and `(community_id, platform_message_id)` respectively, never by sender/content/
  Watcher, and untouched by this fix. **Coordinator claim/continuity** (`recentlyAnsweredByModerator`/
  `recentlyRespondedByHuman`/`wasLastSpeaker`, gated by the existing 5-minute `RECENT_EXCHANGE_WINDOW_MS`) is a
  SEPARATE, social-relevance concept — "does this ambient message still need a reply given what the room just
  did?" — and is what this fix corrected the precedence of, never idempotency itself. There is no conversational
  "cooldown"/rate-limit concept conflated into either of these; the pre-existing `ChatterPacingState`/
  `deployment_state` pacing (`loadChatterPacing`/`recordBotSpoke`) is the genuine, already-separate rate-limit
  mechanism, and a directed message already bypasses it (`bypassesPacing`) — confirmed unaffected by this change.
- New tests (`chatter-coordinator.test.ts`, +5): the exact live-bug repro (a directed greeting-shaped @mention
  answered even though `recentlyAnsweredByModerator: true`), the same for a human-responded-last variant, an
  ambient (non-directed) opener still correctly suppressed by `already_handled` (proving the fix is scoped, not
  a blanket removal of the suppression), a directed opener answered with zero prior activity at all, and two
  different candidates' directed status never blocking each other. 1364 tests pass (up from 1359), `tsc --noEmit`
  clean, production build clean.
- **Not deployed automatically, per explicit instruction.** Live verification (User A -> reply, User B directed
  @mention -> a SECOND independent reply, another distinct User A message -> still independently eligible) was
  not performed this pass — no Preview deploy was requested/authorized as part of this fix; the regression tests
  above directly reproduce and prove the exact reported failure mode and its fix at the pure-function level.

### 2026-08-19 — Fixed: a legitimate Watcher self-mention was deleted/warned as spam + superadmin Watch devops subscription grant (Preview-only) (v1.47.15)
- **Root cause, found by tracing the actual pipeline (message received -> entity extraction -> spam/scam
  classification -> enforcement -> Watcher response), not guessed.** `extractLinks()` (`link-moderation.ts`)
  already treats a bare `@handle` as a "link" candidate for moderation purposes (by design — "join @othergroup"
  is functionally a t.me link). `runLinkModeration()` (`community-runtime.ts`) then gated purely on "were ANY
  link-like things found" and handed the WHOLE message text to `classifyLinkIntent` (Sonnet 5) for
  classification, with no concept of "this @handle is the bot's own username, not an external reference." A
  message like `@mrpreswan_bot hello` was therefore classified exactly like an external promotional link, and
  the AI classifier — seeing an isolated `@username` with no other context — plausibly mislabeled it
  `UNSOLICITED_PROMOTION` (confirmed live via `moderator_activity_log`), triggering `DELETE_WARN`: the user's
  message deleted, a warning issued, for legitimately addressing the Watcher by name.
- **Fix, at the extraction/gating layer — not the AI prompt, not the deterministic policy.** New pure
  `filterOutOwnBotMentions(links, botUsernames)` + `isOwnBotMention` + `normalizeTelegramUsername`
  (`link-moderation.ts`) strip bare mentions of the community's own deployed Watcher bot usernames OUT of the
  candidate list BEFORE classification ever runs — sourced from `ChatterDeployment.botUsername`
  (`telegram_bot_integrations.username`, the SAME trusted runtime bot identity every other addressing/routing
  decision already reads), never a hardcoded name, never a manual whitelist. If a message contains ONLY a
  self-mention (no other link), `runLinkModeration` now returns `{handled:false}` immediately — zero DB calls,
  zero AI calls, zero Telegram calls, structurally proving no deletion/warning can happen. Any OTHER link in
  the same message (a real phishing URL, an unrelated external @handle) is left completely untouched and still
  evaluated normally — `@Watcher click <phishing-link>` is still classified and still enforceable; the
  exemption is narrowly "the self-mention itself isn't suspicious," never "this message is exempt." Also added
  one clarifying line to the classification system prompt (`link-classify.ts`): a bare @username alone, with
  no other suspicious content, is not sufficient for PHISHING_OR_SCAM/UNSOLICITED_PROMOTION — a narrow
  reinforcement, not a weakening of any existing detection rule.
- **Multi-Watcher correct by construction**: `filterOutOwnBotMentions` is given EVERY deployed bot's username
  in the community (not just the one processing the update), so mentioning `@KwanBot` is exempt for every
  Watcher's own moderation pass, not just Kwan's — satisfies "Test must not treat Kwan's mention as its own
  scam signal." Direct-address ROUTING itself (`resolveDirectedModerator`/`selectChatterAction`,
  `chatter-coordinator.ts`) is completely untouched — this fix only changes the moderation GATE, never the
  message text, so a Watcher still correctly recognizes it's being addressed and can still respond.
- **Telegram entity-aware parsing (mention/text_mention) was investigated and confirmed NOT supported anywhere
  in this codebase's ingestion pipeline today** — `CommunityEvent` carries only raw `text`, no `entities` array
  is captured from the Telegram update at all. Building that support is a real, separate, larger architecture
  change (spans `event-types.ts` and the webhook ingestion), out of scope for this root-cause fix; the regex +
  canonical-normalization approach fully resolves the reported bug. Documented as a known gap, not silently
  skipped.
- **Investigated "it doesn't send any messages" as a possible rate-limit issue — confirmed NOT a plan/quota
  problem.** Checked `community_reactive_quota` for the affected community/day: zero rows (0/20 of the trial's
  `TRIAL_REACTIVE_DAILY_LIMIT` used). `moderator_activity_log` showed the real explanation: several messages
  were legitimately `SILENCE`d (`empty_message`, `trivial_low_value` — correct, unrelated to this bug), and
  the false-positive warning itself put the room into `already_handled` continuity state for several minutes
  afterward, correctly (by existing design) suppressing further chatter replies in that window — a real
  cascade FROM the same bug, not a separate rate-limit issue. Fixing the self-mention bug directly resolves
  this symptom too.
- **New: superadmin can manually grant a Watch subscription tier to an account for live QA — Preview-only.**
  New `src/lib/actions/superadmin-watch-devops.ts` — `findAccountByEmail` (reuses the existing
  `auth_user_id_by_email` RPC, migration 0038, no second email->id lookup), `getAccountDevOpsSubscription`
  (read-only, NOT Preview-gated — a superadmin must still be able to SEE an account's real entitlement from
  Production), and the two MUTATING actions `setAccountDevOpsSubscription`/`clearAccountDevOpsSubscription`,
  both hard-gated server-side on new `isPreviewEnvironment()` (`config.ts`, `VERCEL_ENV === "preview"`) — fail
  explicitly outside Preview, never a silent no-op, and never only hidden in the UI. Reuses the EXACT canonical
  `activateWatchEntitlement` (`ownership.ts`) every real paid purchase already calls — never a second/parallel
  entitlement-writing path — tagging the grant distinctly (`subscription_ref: "<tier>:devops:<superadminId>:
  <timestamp>"`, vs. a real purchase's `"<tier>:<depositId>"`) so it's always visually distinguishable and so
  `clearAccountDevOpsSubscription` refuses to ever touch a row that isn't itself devops-tagged (never
  accidentally cancels a real paid subscription). **"Brought live" clarified**: Preview and Production read/
  write the SAME Supabase project (confirmed this session) — there is no separate promotion step; a devops
  entitlement granted on Preview is immediately the account's real entitlement everywhere, including
  Production. Only the ACT of granting/revoking it this way is Preview-restricted.
- New UI: `src/components/superadmin/WatchDevOpsAdmin.tsx` (email search -> current entitlement state -> tier
  picker + grant/clear), mounted in BOTH superadmin surfaces per this codebase's established dual-mount
  convention — the `/superadmin` route (new "Watch devops" tab) and the owner-app super-admin sidebar (new
  "Watch devops" section, `isSuper`-gated, matching Products/Design pricing).
- New tests: `link-moderation.test.ts` (+13 — the exact live-bug repro, case-insensitive/optional-@ matching,
  multi-Watcher exemption, real-phishing-link-still-enforceable, arbitrary external handle NOT exempted,
  no-op-with-no-known-bots), `community-runtime.test.ts` (+5 integration-level — a bare self-mention structurally
  never touches the DB/Telegram (NO HIDDEN FALLBACK-style proof), same-sentence and different-casing variants,
  the multi-Watcher requirement 8 case, an arbitrary external handle confirmed to still reach real moderation
  logic), `config.test.ts` (+3 — `isPreviewEnvironment`'s exact gate). 1345 tests pass (up from 1333),
  `tsc --noEmit` clean, production build clean. Diff reviewed: 11 files, every one maps directly to this
  scope — no broad spam/scam weakening, no hardcoded bot usernames, no global whitelist, no duplicated entity
  parsing, no coordinator/single-enforcer regression (verified: `chatter-coordinator.ts` untouched).
- **Live verification status, stated honestly**: deployed to Preview and confirmed via direct DB inspection
  (temporary, removed diagnostic routes — never committed) that the exact live account/community/bot involved
  in the original report now has this fix live, and that quota/activity logs match the analysis above. Did
  **not** send a fresh live Telegram message end-to-end to visually confirm post-fix behavior in this pass —
  marking that as **unverified live** rather than claiming it was proven; the fix is proven at the pure-logic
  and integration-test level (13+5 new tests), and the diagnostic-route DB inspection confirmed the pre-fix
  failure mode exactly matches the described bug with no other contributing cause found.
- **Not deployed automatically** — commit is local; will deploy to Preview on request (this pass's live
  diagnostic inspection above was done via a separate already-authorized Preview deployment mid-session, not
  this final committed state).

### 2026-08-19 — Removed Settings' Moderation Defaults + fixed live "Connect community" DB error (v1.47.14)
- **Removed Settings → Moderation, per explicit product decision.** Now that persona is always an explicit
  per-Watcher assignment (v1.47.11 — `createAccountWatcher` no longer inherits an account-wide default), the
  "Default for new Watchers" concept this section existed to configure no longer applies to anything. Deleted
  outright, confirmed zero remaining importers first: `ModerationDefaultsCard.tsx`,
  `actions/watch-moderation-defaults.ts`, `products/watch-moderation-defaults.ts`, and its test file.
  `app/settings/page.tsx` drops the Moderation tab/fetch; `SettingsSummary.tsx` drops the "Moderation defaults"
  stat (now a 3-up strip: Timezone/Notifications/Security). The `watch_moderation_defaults` DB table itself is
  left in place, unread by any code path — not dropped this pass (a destructive migration wasn't asked for).
- **Live bug, found while testing: connecting a Watcher to a Telegram group failed with a raw Postgres error**
  — "there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification" — visible directly in
  the Connect modal instead of succeeding. Root cause: `createAccountCommunity` (`watch-runtime.ts`) called
  `.upsert(..., {onConflict: "platform,chat_id"})`, but the ONLY unique constraint that could match a
  standalone (`panel_id: null`) row on those two columns is `idx_communities_standalone_chat`, a **partial**
  index (`where panel_id is null`, migration 0069) — Postgres requires an `ON CONFLICT` target to match a
  partial index's `WHERE` predicate exactly for inference, and PostgREST's `upsert()` has no way to express
  that predicate, so the call failed every time it reached a real database (never caught by tests — the test
  suite's fake DB mock's `upsert()` never modeled this real Postgres constraint-matching rule, since it's a
  live-DB-specific failure mode).
- **Fix**: replaced the upsert with select-then-branch, reusing `existingForChat` (already fetched a few lines
  above for the community-cap check) — `UPDATE ... WHERE id = existingForChat.id` when it exists, else a plain
  `INSERT`. A genuine concurrent-insert race (two requests for the same brand-new chat at once) is handled by
  catching a real `23505` and re-selecting the winner's row instead of surfacing a raw DB error — same
  tolerant-idempotency pattern already used elsewhere in this codebase's webhook handlers.

- New tests (`watch-runtime.test.ts`, +2): the exact live-bug repro proving reconnecting the same chat with a
  new title/handle actually UPDATES the existing row (not a second row, not a silent no-op), and a dedicated
  concurrent-insert-race test (scripted 23505 on the first insert attempt, proves the retry correctly returns
  the winner's row). 1326 tests pass (down from 1333 — 9 tests removed with the deleted
  `watch-moderation-defaults.test.ts` file, +2 new), `tsc --noEmit` clean, production build clean. Diff

### 2026-08-19 — Watchers restructured into a scalable CRM master/detail layout (v1.47.13)
- **Root UX problem.** `/watchers` was a flat table; opening a Watcher fully REPLACED the workspace with a
  large standalone detail page — no persistent way to jump between Watchers without going back to the list
  first. With more than a couple of Watchers, navigating between them would get cumbersome and there was no
  scalable pattern for a growing roster.
- **Final structure: `App sidebar | Watcher navigator | Watcher detail`**, a genuine CRM-style master/detail —
  the navigator lives INSIDE the Watchers workspace only (never added to `WatchShell`'s global sidebar, which
  is completely untouched this pass — confirmed via `git diff`, zero changes). New
  `src/components/watch/WatcherNavigator.tsx` — compact scrollable list (name, a status dot + deployment-count
  line, a "Connect" action for unassigned Watchers), a search box + status filter chips (shown once there are
  4+ Watchers, so 1-2 Watchers stay uncluttered), and a small icon-only "+" create button. Exactly one Watcher's
  detail is ever rendered at a time — the navigator has no capability to show more than one detail pane.
- **Selection is route-driven, not client-only state.** Every navigator row is a plain `<Link href="/watchers/
  [id]">` — the SAME two pre-existing routes (`app/watchers/page.tsx`, `app/watchers/[id]/page.tsx`) still exist,
  unchanged in shape/path, so deep links, `notFound()` on an invalid/unowned id, and browser back/forward all
  keep working exactly as before. New `src/components/watch/WatchersWorkspaceClient.tsx` is the shared shell
  both routes render into — `selectedId={null}` on `/watchers` (nothing chosen yet), `selectedId={id}` on
  `/watchers/[id]` (with the server-rendered tabs content passed in as a `detail` prop, the same established
  "server JSX passed into a client component" pattern `WatchTabs` already used).
- **Responsive**: desktop always shows navigator + detail together. Mobile shows exactly one column — the
  navigator alone (acting as the Watchers list "screen") when nothing's selected, or the detail pane alone
  (with a small "← Watchers" back link, `lg:hidden`) once a specific Watcher's route is loaded. No third
  column, no horizontal Watcher strip, no simultaneous multi-detail rendering anywhere.
- **Create/connect actions preserved, not duplicated.** `WatchersWorkspaceClient` owns the Create-Watcher modal
  (reuses the shared `Modal` from `WatchUI.tsx`, same as v1.47.12's Persona picker) and the navigator's per-row
  "Connect" action (opens the existing `WatcherConnectModal`, unchanged) — the detail pane's own big "Connect to
  Telegram"/"Connect a Community" button (`WatcherConnectCta`, `WatcherDetailClient.tsx`) is untouched and
  self-contained, so there are two independent entry points into the SAME connect flow, never two competing
  implementations.
- **No duplicated Watcher data loading**: new pure helpers in `watch-status.ts` — `watcherOperationalStatus`
  (active/paused/unassigned, the same real deployment-derived definition the old flat list's inline `statusOf`
  used) and `deploymentSummaries` (flattens `listAccountCommunities`'s per-Community watcher lists into one
  per-deployment row list) — are now the SINGLE source both `app/watchers/page.tsx` and `app/watchers/[id]/
  page.tsx` call, instead of each page re-deriving the same `.flatMap(...)` independently. The detail route does
  fetch two more queries than before (`listAccountWatchers`/`listAccountCommunities`, for the navigator) — a
  legitimate, necessary cost of adding a persistent navigator alongside the detail pane, not duplicate loading
  of the same data for the same purpose.
- **Old flat list UI deleted outright** — `src/components/watch/WatchersClient.tsx` (`WatchersListClient`) is
  fully superseded by `WatcherNavigator`/`WatchersWorkspaceClient`; confirmed via grep it had zero remaining
  importers before deletion. `Breadcrumbs` dropped from the detail pane (redundant now that the navigator
  itself provides "you're in Watchers, here's the list" context on desktop, and the new mobile back link covers
  the same need on mobile) — no duplicate Watcher headers remain.
- **Persona tab unaffected, already correct from v1.47.12** — `WatcherPersonaTab.tsx`/`PersonaPresetPicker.tsx`/
  `presets.ts` are byte-for-byte untouched this pass (confirmed via `git diff`). It still renders inside the
  detail pane's existing "Persona" tab, still scoped by `moderatorId={detail.id}` (the currently selected
  Watcher, unchanged), so "Persona description → Current preset (compact) → Behavior instructions" and the
  focused preset-picker modal carry forward correctly into the new layout with no changes needed.
- **Ownership semantics reconfirmed unchanged**: `watch-watcher-persona.ts` (per-Watcher persona mutations) and
  the deployment-ownership logic in `watch-runtime.ts` were not touched — Community/deployment still never own
  Persona; only the Watcher profile does.
- New tests (`watch-status.test.ts`, +11, new file): `watcherOperationalStatus`'s full active/paused/unassigned
  truth table incl. cross-Watcher isolation (one Watcher's deployments never bleed into another's status),
  `deploymentSummaries`' flattening + title/chatId fallback + empty-Communities case, an end-to-end composition
  test proving the two functions agree when chained exactly as the navigator uses them, plus 3 tests for the
  previously-untested `communityOperationalStatus`. 1333 tests pass (up from 1322), `tsc --noEmit` clean,
  production build clean (confirmed `/watchers` and `/watchers/[id]` are still the only two Watcher routes — no
  route regression, no new/removed paths).
- **No React component-interaction tests** ("navigator renders multiple Watchers," "selecting a Watcher,"
  "mobile list-to-detail") — consistent with this codebase's established convention of zero RTL/jsdom
  infrastructure anywhere (reconfirmed again this pass); the underlying pure logic every one of those behaviors
  depends on (status/filter computation, deployment-summary construction, route-driven `selectedId` matching)
  is fully unit-tested instead. Verified via typecheck + full test suite + production build + code review of
  the responsive class logic, not live browser interaction (no authenticated session available this pass).
- **Not deployed this pass, per explicit instruction.**

### 2026-08-19 — Watcher Persona tab: compact "current preset" card + a focused preset picker modal (v1.47.12)
- **Root cause / UX issue.** The per-Watcher Persona tab (`WatcherPersonaTab.tsx`) showed a large,
  always-expanded preset grid sitting directly in the main content flow between the description and behavior-
  instructions textareas — visually dominating the page and making "pick a preset" read as the primary task
  when the real task is "configure this Watcher's persona."
- **Final page hierarchy** (unchanged section order, only the middle section's SIZE changed): **Persona
  description → Current preset (compact) → Behavior instructions.** The preset section is now a small summary
  card — current preset name + short description + tags (or "Custom persona" / "No preset applied…" when
  unassigned) — plus a single **"Change preset"** button. No permanently-expanded grid remains in the main flow.
- **Modal, not a drawer — no existing drawer/sheet pattern to reuse.** Investigated first: the only "drawer"
  in this codebase is `WatchShell`'s mobile NAVIGATION drawer (unrelated), and no right-side content-drawer
  component exists anywhere. A centered modal already existed for Create Project/Watcher
  (`WatchDashboard.tsx`'s local `Modal`) — extracted that into a shared, reusable **`Modal`** in `WatchUI.tsx`
  (new optional `maxWidth` prop, defaults to the original `max-w-sm` so the existing Create-Project/Watcher
  usage is byte-identical) instead of building a second, redundant modal implementation.
- **New `src/components/watch/PersonaPresetPicker.tsx`** — opened by "Change preset," renders the full 18-preset
  catalog in a responsive grid inside the shared `Modal` (`max-w-3xl`, scrollable), reusing the EXACT SAME
  preset-card markup/content the old inline grid used (never redesigned per preset). Applies via the SAME
  existing action the old grid called (`applyAccountWatcherPersonaPreset`, `watch-watcher-persona.ts`) —
  selecting a preset behaves identically to before, just from a relocated, focused surface. Dropped the old
  "10 surfaced + More presets" two-tier disclosure inside the picker (redundant now that browsing presets is
  already a deliberate, explicit action, not competing for main-page space) — shows all 18 directly.
- **Real staleness bug fixed in the same pass, not scope creep — same code path this pass already touches.**
  The old inline `apply()` only re-synced the LOCAL `description` state after applying a preset, never
  `customInstructions` — even though the server-side `applyPersonaPreset` materializes BOTH fields from
  `preset.overrides`. The Behavior Instructions textarea would show stale text until a reload. Fixed via two
  new pure helpers in `presets.ts`: **`currentPersonaPresetSummary(presetId)`** (resolves the summary
  card/picker's selected state, `null` for unassigned or a stale/removed preset id — never a fabricated label)
  and **`personaFieldsAfterApply(preset)`** (returns exactly `{description?, customInstructions?}` — the same
  two fields the server writes, never a third field, never anything that would imply the textareas become
  locked once a preset is applied).
- **Preset stays a one-time starting template, not authoritative** — confirmed by construction: applying a
  preset only ever writes an initial value into `description`/`customInstructions` state; both textareas remain
  ordinary controlled inputs with their own independent Save buttons, exactly as before. Nothing in the new UI
  implies a manual edit is invalid after a preset is chosen.
- **Persona stays Watcher-owned, not Community/deployment-owned — confirmed unchanged, not re-verified via new
  code.** `watch-watcher-persona.ts` (the mutation layer) was NOT touched by this pass — every action still
  scopes strictly by `moderatorId` + `virtual_moderators.account_id === user.id`; the new picker component
  simply calls the exact same existing action with the exact same `moderatorId` prop it's given, so per-Watcher
  scoping is inherited unmodified. No deployment-level persona override was introduced — a Watcher deployed to
  multiple Communities still reads one shared persona, per explicit product decision to keep this out of scope.
- **Deliberately NOT touched**: `ModerationDefaultsCard.tsx` (the SEPARATE Settings → account-level Moderation
  Defaults page) — a different feature/page, out of scope for this Watcher-tab-specific pass; it already had
  its own more modest collapsible "More presets" disclosure, not the always-expanded grid this pass fixed. The
  legacy owner-side (Panel-owner) `PersonaPresetPicker` function inside `AdminTabs.tsx` is unrelated (different
  directory, different flow, same name is not a collision since neither is imported across files) and untouched.
- New tests (`presets.test.ts`, +6): `currentPersonaPresetSummary`'s known/null/stale-id resolution, and a
  dedicated proof that it can never disagree with `resolvePersonaPreset`; `personaFieldsAfterApply`'s exact
  field mirroring against real preset overrides across all 18 presets, and a dedicated proof it never returns
  a field beyond `description`/`customInstructions`. **No new React component-interaction tests** ("opening the
  picker," "choosing a preset" as literal UI actions) — consistent with this codebase's established convention
  of no RTL/jsdom infrastructure (verified again this pass, no test file exists for ANY Watch component);
  Watcher-level scoping is unchanged/verified via code review of the untouched action file rather than a new
  DB-mocked action test, matching every other action file's established precedent in this codebase. 1322 tests
  pass (up from 1316), `tsc --noEmit` clean, production build clean. Diff reviewed: exactly 6 files changed
  (`WatchDashboard.tsx` — Modal consolidation only, byte-identical behavior; `WatchUI.tsx` — new shared Modal;
  `WatcherPersonaTab.tsx` — the actual UX rewrite; `presets.ts`/`presets.test.ts` — the two new pure helpers +
  tests; `PersonaPresetPicker.tsx` — new file), no accidental Community/deployment persona coupling, no
  duplicated preset UI (the full grid now exists in exactly one place), no dead controls introduced.
- **Not deployed this pass, per explicit instruction** — verified via typecheck + full test suite + production
  build + code review only.

### 2026-08-19 — Moderation persona is assigned per-Watcher, never a silent account-wide default + new onboarding step + auto-advancing guide (v1.47.11)
- **Live product-direction fix: a new Watcher's persona was silently pre-filled from Settings' account-level
  "Moderation Defaults" preset** (v1.40.0) — every new Watcher on an account with a configured default started
  identical, with no explicit per-Watcher decision ever made. Per explicit instruction, persona is now ALWAYS an
  explicit, individual assignment — `createAccountWatcher` (`watch-runtime.ts`) no longer reads
  `watch_moderation_defaults` at all; a new Watcher starts on the plain, genuinely-unconfigured platform
  `DEFAULT_MODERATOR_PERSONA`. Settings' Moderation Defaults card still exists (re-worded — "Suggested starting
  point" / "Suggested starting persona," never "applied when you create a new Watcher") as a convenience preset
  to reach for during that explicit assignment, never something silently applied.
- **New `moderatorPersonaIsAssigned(persona)`** (`moderator/domain.ts`) — true once a preset was applied or a
  real description/custom-instructions was typed (mirrors the exact "isDefault" check
  `ModerationDefaultsCard`/`WatcherPersonaTab` already used inline); false for the untouched platform default.
  Numeric style dials alone never count — only an explicit preset/description/instructions is a real assignment
  signal.
- **New onboarding stage, second-to-last as requested**: `create_watcher → assign_moderation → connect_watcher
  (deploy) → operational` (was `create_watcher → connect_watcher`). `watch-onboarding-state.ts`'s
  `OnboardingStateInput` gained `watcherPersonaAssigned`; `resolveOnboardingStage`/`onboardingChecklist` gate on
  it between create_watcher and connect_watcher. Computed in `getWatchAccessState`
  (`actions/watch-dashboard.ts`) as `watchers.some(w => moderatorPersonaIsAssigned(w.persona))`. The guide's new
  "Assign moderation persona" CTA links to `/watchers/[id]?tab=persona` — `app/watchers/[id]/page.tsx` gained
  `searchParams` support for `?tab=` (mirrors the existing `communities/[id]` pattern) so it actually opens the
  Persona tab, which is the SAME `WatcherPersonaTab` editor already used elsewhere (no new UI built).
- **Guide now auto-advances after each step, instead of needing a manual reload.** Root cause: creating a
  Project already did a full `window.location.reload()` (so the next real server-resolved stage rendered
  immediately), but creating a Watcher only updated local client state — the `onboardingStage` prop (server-
  resolved, passed once) never changed, so the guide visibly stalled on "Create a Watcher" even after one was
  created. `WatchDashboard.tsx`'s watcher-creation branch now also reloads while still inside onboarding
  (`showOnboarding` true), landing correctly on the new `assign_moderation` stage — matching the same mechanism
  Project creation and Watcher deployment (`WatcherConnectModal`'s `onConnected`) already used, not a new
  client-side stage-prediction mechanism.
- New tests: `domain.test.ts` (+6, new file — every `moderatorPersonaIsAssigned` case incl. whitespace-only
  and dial-only non-signals), `watch-onboarding-state.test.ts` (rewritten — the new 6-item checklist order,
  every stage transition incl. the new assign_moderation gate, both REQUIRED renumbered cases),
  `watch-runtime.test.ts` (the old "inherits the account's configured default" test now asserts the OPPOSITE —
  a configured default is present but never applied). 1316 tests pass (up from 1308), `tsc --noEmit` clean,
  production build clean, diff reviewed (every changed file maps directly to this scope).
- **Not verified live this pass** — same sandbox limitation as most Watch dashboard work (no authenticated
  session available); verified via the full test suite + typecheck + production build + code review.

### 2026-08-19 — One-click Telegram connect (Profile + Free Trial cards) (v1.47.10)
- **Live UX report: connecting Telegram took two clicks** — "Connect Telegram" started verification, then a
  second, separately-rendered "Open Telegram" link had to be clicked to actually open the deep link.
- **Fix, both cards** (`src/components/watch/ConnectTelegramCard.tsx` on `/profile`,
  `src/components/watch/FreeTrialCard.tsx` on `/plans`): `window.open("", "_blank")` now runs SYNCHRONOUSLY
  inside the click handler, before the `await startWatchTelegramVerification()` call — browsers generally only
  allow a popup as a direct result of a user gesture, not after an awaited async call, so opening blank
  immediately and navigating that handle to the real deep link once it resolves keeps this to one click. Falls
  back to a direct `window.open(deepLink, ...)` if the popup handle came back null/closed (blocked anyway). The
  existing fallback "Open Telegram" link/Cancel UI in the pending state is unchanged, still usable manually.
- 1308 tests pass (unaffected — no logic changed, UI-only), `tsc --noEmit` clean, production build clean.

### 2026-08-19 — Stable Vercel Preview alias now classifies as Innvil Watch, for this branch's QA only (v1.47.9)
- **Root cause**: `isWatchHost()` (`watch-host.ts`) did an exact-match comparison against `WATCH_ROOT_DOMAIN`
  (`watch.innvil.cloud`) only — the stable Preview branch alias confirmed working in the prior pass
  (`innvil-git-rebrand-innvil-v020-ako-me.vercel.app`) never matched that, so every Watch-gated surface
  (`app/page.tsx`'s root routing, `product-brand.ts`'s auth branding, `requireWatchPage()`) fell through to the
  main Innvil/Forge experience when opened on that alias — the main landing rendered instead of Watch, exactly
  as reported.
- **Fix — one new named exception, Preview-only, never a wildcard.** New `isWatchHostname(host, vercelEnv)` in
  `config.ts` (pure, directly testable): the existing Production rule (`WATCH_ROOT_DOMAIN`, exact match, any
  environment) plus a single additional check — a NAMED constant, `WATCH_PREVIEW_ALIAS_HOST` =
  `"innvil-git-rebrand-innvil-v020-ako-me.vercel.app"` — matched only when `process.env.VERCEL_ENV === "preview"`
  (Vercel's own automatically-set env var; unset/`"production"`/`"development"` never match). Explicitly NOT
  derived by reconstructing Vercel's branch-name slugification (lowercasing/dot-stripping/team-suffix rules) —
  not worth reverse-engineering for a one-off QA convenience when the alias is already known and stable across
  redeploys of this branch. Explicitly NOT a `*.vercel.app` wildcard — every other preview hostname (this
  branch's own raw per-deployment hash URLs, and any other branch's alias) is unaffected. `isWatchHost()` now
  delegates to this function instead of comparing inline.
- **Production is provably unchanged**: the Production branch of `isWatchHostname` is byte-identical to the old
  logic (still just `host === WATCH_ROOT_DOMAIN`), and the new Preview branch is additive and gated on an env
  var that's never `"preview"` in Production — confirmed both by the pure function's own tests and by
  `WATCH_ROOT_DOMAIN`/`isTrustedWatchHost` (the password-reset redirect-origin allowlist) being completely
  untouched.
- **`proxy.ts` needed no change** — confirmed by reading it first: it already treats every `*.vercel.app` host
  as ordinary app-host traffic (`h.endsWith(".vercel.app")`, no panel-subdomain rewrite attempted), so API/
  webhook routing on the Preview alias was never broken and required no fix.
- New tests (`config.test.ts`, +7): `watch.innvil.cloud` classified as Watch in every environment; the plain
  apex `innvil.cloud` never classified as Watch; the exact stable Preview alias classified as Watch only when
  `VERCEL_ENV=preview`; an unrelated Vercel preview hostname (including a differently-named branch alias and a
  raw per-deployment hash URL shape) never classified as Watch even in Preview; the SAME alias hostname is NOT
  Watch outside Preview (unset/production/development); case-insensitivity for both rules. 1308 tests pass (up
  from 1302), `tsc --noEmit` clean, production build clean. Diff reviewed: exactly 3 files touched
  (`config.ts`, `config.test.ts`, `watch-host.ts`) — no scope creep into `proxy.ts`, `product-brand.ts`,
  `watch-page.ts`, or `app/page.tsx` (all three consumers benefit automatically via the shared `isWatchHost()`
  call, none needed their own edit).
- **Deployed to Preview only, verified live**: opening `https://innvil-git-rebrand-innvil-v020-ako-me.vercel.app`
  now renders the Watch landing/dashboard instead of the main Innvil landing; Watch metadata/branding confirmed

### 2026-08-19 — Telegram-identity-first onboarding: a real account-state machine replaces the old plan-first welcome screen (v1.47.4)
- **Investigated first.** The Overview welcome panel (`WatchDashboard.tsx`'s old `OnboardingEmptyState`) had
  exactly two states — entitled vs. not — and its primary CTA for a not-yet-entitled account was the single
  ambiguous button "View plans / Start Free Trial". It also disappeared the instant ANY resource existed
  (`hasAnyResource`, a plain `projects.length > 0 || watchers.length > 0 || communities.length > 0` check) —
  meaning a customer who'd only created a Project would drop straight into the full operational dashboard with
  empty tables everywhere, never the guided checklist the report explicitly asked to keep showing (with earlier
  steps checked off) until a Watcher is actually deployed.
- **New pure state machine, `src/lib/products/watch-onboarding-state.ts`** (no I/O — the same "pure resolver +
  caller gathers real state" pattern as `watch-status.ts`) — `resolveOnboardingStage()`: `connect_telegram` →
  `try_watch` → `create_project` → `create_watcher` → `connect_watcher` → `operational`. Checked in strict
  dependency order, first unmet condition wins. Telegram PERSON identity (`watch_telegram_links`, Profile's
  existing `ConnectTelegramCard` flow) is checked FIRST, unconditionally — even ahead of an already-active paid
  entitlement, per explicit product decision — and is structurally never confused with a Telegram COMMUNITY
  connection (a real Telegram group/supergroup/channel) anywhere in this file or its consumers.
  `onboardingChecklist()` derives the SAME 5-item checklist from the SAME input, so the checklist and the
  resolved stage can never disagree (a dedicated test pins this).
- **Honest adaptation to the real UI, not the report's literal step count.** The report's suggested order was
  Telegram → Trial/Plan → Project → Community → Watcher → Deploy (6 steps after identity). This codebase's
  ACTUAL UI has no standalone "connect a Community with no Watcher yet" control — Community connection only
  ever happens through `WatcherConnectModal` (bot creation → Telegram membership verification → Community
  connect → deploy, all one guided flow per Watcher, confirmed via code review before writing the state
  machine). Per the report's own explicit "adapt later steps to current actual route/business logic" allowance,
  Community-connect and deploy were collapsed into one `connect_watcher` stage rather than inventing a UI
  control that doesn't exist — documented here, not silently done.
- **`getWatchAccessState()` (`actions/watch-dashboard.ts`) extended** — now also resolves
  `getAccountTelegramIdentity()` and `getWatchTrialState()` (both already-existing, already-tested functions,
  reused verbatim — no second Telegram-identity or trial-status implementation) and computes the real
  `onboardingStage` via the new resolver. `WatchAccessState` gained `telegramVerified`/`trialStatus`/
  `onboardingStage`; `app/page.tsx` threads all three into `WatchDashboard`.
- **`WatchDashboard.tsx` rewritten**: the onboarding gate is now `onboardingStage !== "operational"` (was
  `!hasAnyResource`) — the welcome panel now correctly stays up through Project/Watcher creation, only handing
  off to the normal operational Overview once a real deployment is active. New `OnboardingGuide` (replaces
  `OnboardingEmptyState`) — one stage-specific headline + body, a 5-item checklist with real checkmarks
  (`onboardingChecklist`, strikethrough + teal check on completed items, the current stage highlighted), and
  exactly ONE primary CTA per stage: `connect_telegram` → "Connect Telegram" → `/profile#connected-identities`
  (a new anchor id added to Profile's existing Connected identities card — no second Telegram-linking
  implementation); `try_watch` → "Start Free Trial" (or "Choose a plan" when `trialStatus === "expired"`, per
  the explicit "trial-consumed accounts must never see Start Free Trial again" requirement — the actual
  gating still lives entirely in `/plans`'s existing `FreeTrialCard`, this is copy-only) → `/plans`;
  `create_project`/`create_watcher` → the existing create-Project/create-Watcher modals, unchanged; 
  `connect_watcher` → opens the existing `WatcherConnectModal` for the account's first Watcher. The Overview
  CTA never calls `startWatchTrialAction` itself — Telegram verification only makes the account ELIGIBLE, the
  customer must still explicitly click through to Plans and start the trial there, exactly as required.
- **Navigation is never blocked during onboarding** — `WatchShell`'s sidebar (Profile/Usage/Plans/Billing/
  Settings/Support, unchanged) renders unconditionally around the onboarding panel; only the Overview CONTENT
  area swaps between the guide and the operational dashboard.
- **Zero-Panel confirmed**: no code in `watch-onboarding-state.ts` or the `OnboardingGuide` rewrite touches
  `panels`/`panel_id` at all — the resolver's five inputs (Telegram identity, entitlement, Project/Watcher/
  deployment counts) are all already-Panel-free reads this codebase established in earlier passes.
- **Short "How it works" summary on the public landing corrected to match** (`WatchLanding.tsx`'s 4-card `STEPS`

  visitor-facing 8-step Getting Started guide (`watch-onboarding.ts`) to match; that's marketing content for a

  Supabase auth session with a controllable fresh Telegram-identity state, which (consistent with every other

  panel-scoped, since one Innvil account spans every product) to its login email, server-side only — an

  updated — the email/username field only widens to `type="text"`/"Email or username" in **login** mode; signup

### 2026-08-19 — Critical fix: standalone Innvil Watch was unreachable for a brand-new, zero-Panel, zero-entitlement account (v1.47.1)
- **Live bug report: a brand-new Innvil account, registered directly through Watch with zero Panels, could not
  enter or use the Watch dashboard at all** — every page (Overview, Plans, Billing, Usage, Profile, Settings,
  Projects, Communities, Watchers, Activity, Support) bounced back to the marketing landing. Root cause found by
  tracing the actual request path (not guessed): TWO separate places conflated **authentication** with
  **entitlement**.
  1. **`src/lib/watch-page.ts`'s `requireWatchPage()`** — the shared guard behind all 13 real Watch feature
     routes (`/projects`, `/communities`, `/watchers`, `/activity`, `/usage`, `/billing`, `/plans`, `/profile`,
     `/settings`, `/support`, plus the two `[id]` detail routes) — called `hasProductAccess()` and
     `redirect("/")` whenever it returned `false`. A fresh account with no Panel, no trial, and no paid
     subscription is, correctly, NOT entitled — but that meant **every one of these pages, including `/plans`
     and `/billing` themselves**, was unreachable for exactly the account that most needs to reach them (to
     start the Free Trial or subscribe in the first place). Fixed: this guard now checks ONLY Watch-host +
     signed-in — it no longer touches entitlement at all. Every downstream page was ALREADY built to render a
     real empty/upsell state for `capacity: null` (`getAccountCapacity` already returns `null` for no
     entitlement, and Usage/Billing/`WatchShell` already branch on it correctly) — confirmed by reading each of
     the 13 route files before touching anything, not assumed; this was a one-function fix, not a rewrite.
  2. **`getWatchAccessState()`** (`src/lib/actions/watch-dashboard.ts`), which powers the ROOT `/` route (Watch's
     "Overview") — early-returned a mostly-empty `EMPTY_ACCESS` object for a non-entitled authenticated user,
     and `app/page.tsx` then rendered `<WatchLanding authenticated={true}>` (the marketing page) instead of the
     real dashboard shell. Fixed: `getWatchAccessState()` now always fetches the full real read set (Projects,
     Watchers, Communities, capacity, activity — all genuinely empty for a fresh account, never fabricated) for
     any authenticated user; `app/page.tsx` now renders `<WatchDashboard>` for any `access.authenticated`,
     dropping the `&& access.entitled` condition. `WatchDashboard`'s own pre-existing `hasAnyResource` check
     (zero Projects/Watchers/Communities) already renders its `OnboardingEmptyState` for exactly this account
     shape — no new empty-state UI needed to exist, it just couldn't be reached before.
  3. **`OnboardingEmptyState` improved** (small, targeted addition, not part of the root cause): it previously
     always pointed "Start setup" at the Create-Project modal — which fails for a non-entitled fresh account
     (`createStandaloneProject` correctly requires entitlement) with a confusing inline rejection, since Watch's
     real order of operations is Plan/Trial → Project → Community → Watcher → Deploy. Now takes an `entitled`
     prop (`capacity != null`) and shows a 5-step list ending in "View plans / Start Free Trial" → `/plans`

### 2026-08-19 — Community Expansion: a real, paid Gold/Platinum-only Watch capacity add-on (v1.47.0)
- **Investigated first, per explicit instruction, before writing anything.** Confirmed `MODERATOR_COMMUNITY_
  CAPACITY[tier].maxWithAddons` (money.ts) already existed and was already DISPLAYED on Plans (Gold "3 included
  / Up to 5", Platinum "5 included / Up to 10") — but was purely decorative: `requireAccountWatchContext`
  (watch-runtime.ts, the SINGLE canonical resolver every Watcher/Community/Deployment creation path and
  `getAccountCapacity` already go through) only ever read `CAPACITY[tier].maxCommunities` (the INCLUDED count),
  never `maxWithAddons` — there was no purchase mechanism anywhere that could actually raise a Community's
  effective ceiling. This pass builds that missing mechanism, reusing the existing included/max numbers as the
  canonical source (never redeclared) — Bronze/Silver get nothing (their own `maxWithAddons === included`,
  hard-capped, unchanged); Gold expands 3→5 for $12.99/mo; Platinum expands 5→10 for $19.99/mo.
- **New migration `0083_watch_community_expansion.sql`** — `watch_subscription_addons` (`account_id`,
  `addon_type` check-limited to `'community_expansion'`, `status` active/removed, `cancel_at_period_end`,
  timestamps; RLS on with no policies, service-role only, same convention as every other Watch runtime table).
  **At most one active row per account, enforced at the DB level** via a partial unique index
  `(account_id, addon_type) where status='active'` — a concurrent duplicate purchase attempt can never create a
  second active row or push capacity beyond the canonical max, proven by a dedicated race-safety test.
  Deliberately NO period columns on the add-on itself — "renewing" it just means its price is folded into the
  BASE subscription's own next renewal charge; it belongs to the exact same billing period as
  `product_entitlements`, never an independent renewal date. `platform_deposits.purpose` gained a fourth value,
  `watch_addon_purchase`, with its own required-field shape in the existing check constraint. **Run migration
  `0083`.**
- **New `src/lib/products/watch-community-expansion.ts`** — deliberately the ONLY module that reads
  `watch_subscription_addons` directly (both `watch-runtime.ts` and `innvil-credit.ts` import from here, never
  from each other, since `innvil-credit.ts` already depends on `watch-runtime.ts` for `getAccountPaidPlan` —
  importing the other direction would create a cycle). `getCommunityExpansionState`/`hasActiveCommunityExpansion`
  (plain reads), `finalizeAddonsOnRenewal` (marks a `cancel_at_period_end` row `removed` — real no-op otherwise,
  safe to call unconditionally after every base-subscription settlement), and `finalizeAddonsOnTierChange`
  (unconditionally removes ANY active row — used only for a genuine plan CHANGE, see below).
- **Capacity resolution — one line changed in the ONE canonical resolver, nothing duplicated.**
  `requireAccountWatchContext`'s paid-tier branch now computes `maxCommunities` as
  `isCommunityExpansionEligibleTier(tier) && hasActiveCommunityExpansion(...) ? MODERATOR_COMMUNITY_CAPACITY[tier]
  .maxWithAddons : CAPACITY[tier].maxCommunities` — every existing enforcement point (`createAccountCommunity`'s
  cap check, `getAccountCapacity`) picks this up automatically, with zero changes needed at those call sites.
  `AccountCapacity` gained `communityExpansionActive`/`communityExpansionEligible` (derived by comparison against
  the plain included cap — no second DB read needed, since `requireAccountWatchContext` already resolved the
  effective ceiling internally). **Watcher slots are completely untouched** — `maxActiveSlots` is computed
  identically regardless of the add-on, confirmed by a dedicated test.
- **Purchase (Innvil Credit — `purchaseCommunityExpansionWithCredit`, `innvil-credit.ts`)**: eligibility
  (Gold/Platinum only, active paid subscription required — rejected server-side, not just hidden in UI),
  already-active is a safe idempotent no-op (never double-charges; un-cancels a removal-pending add-on for
  free, since it was already paid for), priced via the SAME canonical `creditPriceUsd`/`annualCreditPriceUsd`
  functions the base plan already uses (Gold $12.34/mo credit price via the existing 5% rule, Platinum $18.99/mo;
  annual $140.29/$215.89/year via the existing 10% rule applied to the REGULAR $12.99/$19.99 — never stacked on
  top of the monthly discount, pinned by a dedicated test), debit-then-activate with a compensating reversal
  ledger entry on any activation failure (same documented pattern as the base subscription purchase — a real
  disclosed compensating-transaction choice, not full single-statement DB atomicity). Race safety: two
  concurrent purchase attempts with ample balance for both still activate exactly once (the loser's debit is
  reversed via the same DB-level partial-unique-index guard, reporting `active:true` rather than a hard failure).
- **Purchase (direct crypto — `createCommunityExpansionCheckout`, `watch-checkout.ts`)**: monthly-only,
  structurally (no `billingInterval` parameter exists on this function at all) — annual stays Innvil-Credit-only
  by product rule. Reuses the exact same `platform_deposits`/adapter/webhook pipeline as the base subscription,
  with `purpose:'watch_addon_purchase'`; activation happens ONLY in `platform.ts`'s webhook handler (never from
  a browser redirect), inserting the add-on row with the same 23505-tolerant idempotency as every other webhook
  branch in this file.
- **Renewal — folded into the SAME base-subscription charge, never a second/independent one.** Both
  `purchaseWatchWithCredit` (credit) and `createDirectWatchCheckout` (crypto) now check: is this a renewal of
  the SAME tier the add-on is active under, and is it not scheduled for removal? If so, the add-on's own credit/
  regular price is added into the ONE combined debit/checkout amount (worked example: Gold base $208.99 credit
  + $12.34 add-on = $221.33, ONE transaction, pinned by test) — `finalizeAddonsOnRenewal` runs after every
  successful settlement either way, so a removal-pending add-on is charged nothing further and correctly
  finalized to `removed` on that same renewal.
- **Removal (`scheduleCommunityExpansionRemoval`)** — never an immediate capacity cut, never a refund for unused
  time. Blocked SERVER-SIDE (not just hidden in UI) if current Community usage already exceeds the plan's plain
  INCLUDED cap (would otherwise leave the account instantly over its own new effective capacity) — the add-on
  stays fully active (expanded capacity still available, since it's already paid for) until finalized on the
  next renewal.
- **Plan-change transitions (Gold+expansion↔Platinum) — explicitly investigated and handled, per direct
  instruction.** A plan CHANGE to a DIFFERENT tier never silently carries the add-on across tiers — it was
  priced/sized for the OLD tier, and letting it ride along would mean either a Gold-priced add-on suddenly
  granting Platinum's 10-Community ceiling for free, or the reverse commercial mismatch. Both `purchaseWatch
  WithCredit` and `createDirectWatchCheckout` now detect a genuine tier change with an active add-on and: (1)
  BLOCK the change server-side if current Community usage exceeds the NEW tier's plain included cap (the exact
  "Platinum+expansion, 8 connected → Gold" worked example from the request — Gold's own max is 5, even
  expanded, so 8 is rejected regardless; blocked with zero debit, the account stays on its current tier, and
  the add-on is left completely untouched, not silently finalized for a change that itself never took effect),
  else (2) let the change proceed with ONLY the new tier's own base price (no add-on price folded in) and call
  `finalizeAddonsOnTierChange` after activation — the old tier's add-on is cleanly finalized (removed, no
  refund), and the customer can re-purchase Community Expansion under the new tier's own price/capacity if they
  still want it. The crypto webhook path (`platform.ts`) mirrors this: resolves the prior tier via
  `getAccountPaidPlan` BEFORE `activateWatchEntitlement` overwrites it, then finalizes the add-on the same way.
- **UI**: `BillingPlanPicker.tsx`'s Gold/Platinum cards now show a real "+$12.99/mo" / "+$19.99/mo" Community
  Expansion line under the capacity block (annual view: "+$140.29/year · Innvil Credit only") — Bronze/Silver
  show nothing about expansion at all, matching the existing `expandable` gate. `CommunityExpansionInfoPopover`
  copy updated to reference the real priced package instead of vague "can be added" language. New
  `CommunityExpansionCard.tsx` (Usage page, gated on `capacity.communityExpansionEligible`) — not-active state
  shows the regular + Innvil Credit prices and an "Add with Innvil Credit" button (immediate, atomic) plus
  "Pay with [gateway]" buttons for monthly-only direct crypto (real `listAvailableDirectWatchGateways()`
  results, never a fabricated option); active state shows included/expanded capacity + real current usage and a
  "Remove" action, or an amber "scheduled to end at your next renewal" note once removal is scheduled. Billing
  page's "Current subscription" card now folds the add-on into its displayed price ("$232.98/mo (incl. Community
  Expansion)") with a "+ Community Expansion" pill, and the payment-history table labels standalone add-on rows
  distinctly ("Gold · Community Expansion") using the real `purpose` field `listWatchPaymentHistory` already
  returns.
- **Enterprise is completely untouched** (not in this diff at all) — Managed/BYO remain custom capacity/
  commercial models; `COMMUNITY_EXPANSION_ELIGIBLE_TIERS` is structurally `["premium","pro"]` only, and
  Enterprise was never a `ModeratorPlanTier` to begin with (can't compile into this logic even by accident).
  **Free Trial is unaffected** — `isCommunityExpansionEligibleTier("trial")` is a compile-time type error (the
  function only accepts `ModeratorPlanTier`), and `getAccountCapacity`'s trial branch never calls it at all;
  pinned by a dedicated test (a stray active add-on row never expands a trial account's capacity).
- **Code-review sweep performed** (all 12 requested items): no expansion pricing/logic reachable for Bronze/
  Silver anywhere in the diff; no per-Community quantity/multiplier concept exists anywhere (confirmed —
  explicitly a fixed package, no selector); zero duplicated `12.99`/`19.99` literals outside `money.ts` (every
  other reference reads the canonical constant); zero duplicated annual-discount arithmetic (every annual price
  goes through the existing `annualCreditPriceUsd`/`annualCreditPriceCents`); all money math is integer-cent
  based via the existing canonical helpers, no new floating-point risk; zero `panel_id`/panel dependency
  anywhere in the new add-on code (the two `panel_id: null` occurrences in `watch-checkout.ts` are the existing,
  correct "this deposit belongs to no Panel" pattern, unchanged from the base subscription); effective capacity
  is read EXCLUSIVELY through `requireAccountWatchContext`/`getAccountCapacity`, never re-derived from
  `watch_subscription_addons` rows directly anywhere outside `watch-community-expansion.ts` itself; Watcher
  slots verified untouched by both code review and a dedicated test; duplicate-payment/duplicate-activation
  safety verified via the partial unique index + 23505 handling in both the credit path and the webhook, plus a
  dedicated concurrency test; Enterprise confirmed untouched (not present in the diff); migration/RLS reviewed
  (service-role only, matches convention); full diff reviewed file-by-file for scope creep (clean — every
  changed file maps directly to this feature).
- New tests: `watch-community-expansion.test.ts` (+15, new file), `money.test.ts` (+4), `innvil-credit-
  pricing.test.ts` (+9, incl. the exact $140.29/$215.89 worked examples and the never-stack-the-monthly-discount
  proof), `innvil-credit.test.ts` (+22 — eligibility incl. Bronze/Silver/no-entitlement rejection, exact
  discounted pricing incl. annual, insufficient-credit debits/activates nothing, idempotent re-purchase, race

  recharges, and both explicit plan-change worked examples — Gold+expansion→Platinum finalizes for free (no

### 2026-08-19 — Annual billing (Innvil Credit only) — a billing interval on the existing plan, not a new plan (v1.46.0)
- **Extends the existing Plans/Billing/Innvil Credit architecture — no new plan/product ids.** Investigated
  first: confirmed no billing-interval concept existed anywhere (`product_entitlements` had no such column) and
  reused every piece of the v1.44.0 subscription-period architecture rather than building parallel annual code.
  `plan_id`/tier stays exactly `basic`/`standard`/`premium`/`pro` — annual is stored as a `billing_interval`
  column on the SAME entitlement row, never `silver_annual`.
- **Migration `0082_watch_billing_interval.sql`** — `product_entitlements.billing_interval` (`'monthly'|'annual'`,
  default `'monthly'`). Every existing paid row was created exclusively through the monthly-only crypto/credit
  paths, so `'monthly'` is the deterministically correct default for 100% of existing customers — no guessing.
- **One canonical period rule, extended not duplicated.** `watch-billing-period.ts` gained `addOneYearClamped`
  (mirrors `addOneMonthClamped`'s Postgres-matching day-clamping, e.g. Feb 29 → Feb 28 the next non-leap year)
  and `computeRenewedPeriod(existingEnd, now, interval)` now takes the interval as its extension-length
  parameter — the anchor-selection logic (extend from existing end if still valid, else fresh from now) is
  completely unchanged and applies identically to monthly, annual, AND an interval switch mid-cycle. This is
  what makes monthly↔annual switching safe with **zero invented proration**: paying annual while a monthly
  period is still active extends from that period's own end by a year; paying monthly while an annual period
  is still active extends from the annual end by a month — no paid time is ever lost, and no special-case code
  was needed for either direction (confirmed via 2 dedicated regression tests). `billing_interval` is stored as
  whatever the LATEST successful payment specified, taking effect immediately (it only affects renewal
  price/behavior, never capacity, so there's nothing to "schedule for later").
- **Annual pricing — one centralized helper, verified against every spec worked example exactly.** New
  `ANNUAL_CREDIT_DISCOUNT_BPS = 1000` (10%, basis points) + `ANNUAL_ELIGIBLE_TIERS` (all 4 self-serve tiers,
  including Bronze — its monthly credit discount is 0% but annual still applies, an intentional, independent
  commercial rule) in `innvil-credit-pricing.ts`. `annualCreditPriceCents/Usd` computes 10% off **12× the
  REGULAR monthly price** (never the already-discounted monthly-credit price — a dedicated test proves these
  would diverge if ever confused), deterministically rounded: Bronze $539.89, Silver $1,403.89, Gold $2,375.89,
  Platinum $4,103.89 — every one matches the request's own worked examples byte-for-byte.
  `annualEquivalentMonthlyUsd`/`annualSavingsUsd` are display-only, computed from the same canonical price
  (savings vs. 12 ordinary monthly DIRECT payments, per explicit instruction, not vs. the discounted monthly
  credit price).
- **Purchase/renewal — the SAME function, not a second annual-only path.** `purchaseWatchWithCredit` gained a
  `billingInterval` parameter (default `"monthly"`, every existing call site unaffected); for `"annual"` it
  computes `annualCreditPriceCents` instead, debits atomically via the same `apply_innvil_credit_change` RPC,
  and calls the same `activateWatchEntitlement(..., "annual")` — which forces `renewal_mode: "innvil_credit"`
  on the row (annual is Innvil-Credit-only by product rule, enforced here so Billing never has to re-derive it).
  Race-safety re-verified at the LARGER annual dollar amounts specifically (a dedicated test: two concurrent
  $1,403.89 annual attempts against a $1,500 balance — exactly one succeeds, balance never negative); a
  duplicate/second successful annual payment extends by exactly one more year, never two (verified by asserting
  the actual delta between consecutive `paidThrough` dates).
- **Annual direct crypto is structurally impossible, not merely hidden.** `createDirectWatchCheckout` has no
  interval parameter at all and never had one — there is no code path through which "annual" could reach it,
  so this isn't a runtime branch that could be forgotten; confirmed via a targeted grep (zero interval
  references in `watch-checkout.ts`).
- **UI**: `/plans`' `BillingPlanPicker` gained a Monthly/Annual toggle (a local view-state, not per-card) — 
  Annual shows the real annual price, "Equivalent to $X/month" (display-only, upfront charge stated
  explicitly), real savings, and "Innvil Credit only"; the "Current plan" badge now also checks the account's
  actual `currentBillingInterval` (so switching intervals for the SAME plan still shows a real action button,
  not a false "current plan" state). `WatchCheckout` gained a `billingInterval` prop — when `"annual"` it skips
  the payment-method-choice screen entirely and never renders a crypto option (never merely hides a button
  reachable another way), shows the annual-specific copy/pricing, and an "Add credit" shortcut appears directly
  in the insufficient-credit message (works for both monthly-credit and annual). `RenewWatchButton` now takes
  the account's own current `billingInterval` (never a client guess) so a renewal never silently switches a
  customer's interval. Billing's "Current subscription" card shows a Monthly/Annual pill, the correct
  price/period label ("Paid through" for annual vs. "Current period ends" for monthly), and honest renewal
  copy ("Renewal: Innvil Credit only... does not currently auto-charge").
- **Enterprise fully untouched** — `ANNUAL_ELIGIBLE_TIERS` is typed as `ModeratorPlanTier[]`, and Enterprise
  isn't a `ModeratorPlanTier` value at all (confirmed unchanged from prior passes), so it structurally cannot

- New/extended tests: `innvil-credit-pricing.test.ts` (+13 — every one of the 4 tier worked examples exactly,
